summary: Iyengar, Khare and Manning define congruence modules Ψ_A(M) := Coker(Ext^c_A(O,M)^tf → Ext^c_A(O,M/p_AM)^tf) and the Wiles defect δ_A(M) = rank·length Φ_A − length Ψ_A(M) for augmented complete local rings λ: A → O regular at p_A = Ker λ of any codimension c, and prove the higher-codimension Wiles–Lenstra–Diamond numerical criterion: δ_A(M) ≥ 0, and δ_A(M) = 0 for depth M ≥ c + 1 iff A is a complete intersection and M has a free summand of full rank at p_A (Theorems A–E, J: Theorem 6.8 on the torsion-free Ext algebra, invariance of domain 7.4, deformation invariance 8.2, criteria 9.2, 9.5, 9.6). Part 2 recalls ultrapatching of perfect complexes (Theorem 10.6) and proves that patching commutes with duality (Theorem 11.3). Part 3 runs the Wiles–Diamond induction on the level for Calegari–Geraghty patched modules and proves integral non-minimal R = T with a free summand in positive defect: for PGL₂ over any number field assuming Conjectures A–D (Theorem F; Bianchi case Theorem G), and unconditionally for weight-one forms on Shimura curves over Q (Theorem H), with a torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence (Theorem I). The atlas has depth, complete intersections, patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3, P7–P9), deformation rings (LocalGaloisDeformationRings, GlobalGaloisDeformations) and arithmetic manifolds (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces), but no congruence module or numerical criterion in any codimension, no duality of patching, no positive-defect or weight-one R = T. Routes: a Part II of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra (congruence modules, Wiles defects, numerical criteria); a Part II of GL2ModularityLifting (integral non-minimal R = T in positive defect and in weight one); source routes to R03.3 (general local algebra: dualizing complexes, Gorenstein rings, multiplicity, symbolic powers, Lescot), to P7–P9 (patching and duality), to LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2, GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.x, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0/ALS.3/ALS.5 and SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3. 65 mistakes are recorded, including a failing step in the proof of Theorem 5.6, a false 'equality iff' in Theorem 7.4/E, an unsupported Conjecture A input for Theorem G, a missing orientation twist in Proposition 13.6 at real places, and a determinant error at the weight-one Taylor–Wiles levels.

items.name: Torsion submodule and torsion-free quotient over a discrete valuation ring
items.statement: O is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ. For an O-module U, tors(U) is its torsion submodule and U^tf := U/tors(U) its torsion-free quotient, giving the exact sequence 0 → tors(U) → U → U^tf → 0, functorial in U. When U is finitely generated, U^tf is finite free, so the sequence splits (non-functorially); hence for any additive functor E on finitely generated O-modules, E(U) → E(U^tf) is surjective. For a map α: U → V the induced map Coker α → Coker(α^tf) is surjective (so α onto implies α^tf onto), and if Ker α is torsion then α^tf is injective.
items.note: The defining objects are in Mathlib: tors(U) is `Submodule.torsion O U` (elements killed by a non-zero-divisor), U^tf is `U ⧸ torsion O U`, which is torsion-free, and it is free when U is finitely generated over the DVR (a PID). The splitting comes from `Module.projective_lifting_property`; Mathlib's structure theorem over a PID uses exactly this splitting. Mathlib does not state the induced map α^tf, the surjectivity of E(U) → E(U^tf) for additive E, or the two remarks (Coker α ↠ Coker α^tf; Ker α torsion ⇒ α^tf injective). These are short consequences (`Submodule.mapQ`, once linear maps are shown to preserve torsion), and whichever layer builds F^i_A (item F-functor) must supply them.

items.name: Augmented local rings: λ_A: A → O, the prime p_A and its codimension c
items.statement: A is a noetherian local ring and λ_A: A → O a surjective local homomorphism onto the discrete valuation ring O. Set p_A := Ker(λ_A), a prime ideal, and c := height p_A (the codimension; c = dim A_{p_A}). Then dim A ≥ height p_A + dim(A/p_A) = c + 1; no restriction is placed on dim A.
items.note: The setting of 2.2 needs no new definition. It consists of a Noetherian local A, a surjective local hom to a DVR (`IsDiscreteValuationRing`, `IsLocalHom`), p_A = ker (prime by `RingHom.ker_isPrime`) and c = `Ideal.height` p_A, which equals dim A_p by `IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height`. The inequality dim A ≥ height p + dim A/p = c + 1 is not stated in ring form. It follows from the order-theoretic `krullDim = ⨆ (height + coheight)` together with `ringKrullDim_quotient` / `Order.coheight_eq_krullDim_Ici` (and dim O = 1), a short bridge that the consumer writes. Mathlib bundles no 'augmented local ring' structure; the category C_O is a separate item (category-CO).

items.name: The functors F^i_A(M) := Ext^i_A(O, M)^tf
items.statement: D(A) is the derived category of A-modules and D^b(mod A) the full subcategory of complexes M with each H_i(M) finitely generated and zero for |i| ≫ 0; for such M, Tor^A_i(O, M) and Ext^i_A(O, M) are finitely generated O-modules, zero for i ≪ 0. For M in D^b(mod A) and each integer i, F^i_A(M) := (Ext^i_A(O, M))^tf, the torsion-free quotient; F^i_A(−) is a functor from D^b(mod A) to O-modules.
items.note: Mathlib has Ext^i between A-modules (the `HasExt` instance on `ModuleCat A`), its A-module structure, finite generation over a Noetherian ring (`ModuleCat.finite_ext`), and the fact that the annihilator of the first argument kills Ext. It does not have the induced O-module structure on Ext^i_A(O,M), Ext from O into a complex M ∈ D^b(mod A) (no D^b(mod A) and no RHom), or the functor F^i_A(M) = Ext^i_A(O,M)^tf. No atlas layer plans F^i_A. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 plans derived tensor products and duals for perfect complexes only, and O is not perfect over A unless A is regular.

items.name: The congruence module Ψ_A(M) of a finitely generated module
items.statement: For a finitely generated A-module M, the map λ_A(M): M → O ⊗_A M = M/p_A M induces F^c_A(λ_A(M)): F^c_A(M) → F^c_A(M/p_A M), where c = height p_A. The congruence module of M is Ψ_A(M) := Coker F^c_A(λ_A(M)); Ψ_A := Ψ_A(A). (When the augmentation must be tracked one writes Ψ_λ(M).) M ↦ Ψ_A(M) is a functor from finitely generated A-modules to O-modules (3.8).
items.note: Neither library has a congruence module; AUDIT-17 on AutomorphicCongruences:L0 found none. The atlas mentions congruence modules only for particular automorphic Hecke modules in codimension 0: AutomorphicCongruences:L0 says it imports them from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants, but no IHG layer plans them; see also SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.1, PadicFamilies:L1 and IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5. Nothing plans the general Ψ_A(M) = Coker F^c_A(λ_A(M)) in codimension c, or its functoriality (3.8).

items.name: F^c_A of an O-module (Observation 2.3 and (2.4))
items.statement: For any finitely generated O-module U, viewed as an A-module via λ_A, the O-split surjection U → U^tf with torsion kernel induces isomorphisms F^c_A(U) ≅ F^c_A(U^tf) ≅ F^c_A(O) ⊗_O U^tf. In particular, for every finitely generated A-module M there is a natural isomorphism (2.4) F^c_A(M/p_A M) ≅ F^c_A(O) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf.
items.note: This depends on F^c_A, which is missing. The only library inputs are the freeness of U^tf and the O-linear splitting of U → U^tf (see torsion-tf). Neither isomorphism F^c_A(U) ≅ F^c_A(U^tf) ≅ F^c_A(O) ⊗_O U^tf, nor (2.4), is in the libraries or the atlas.

items.name: Regularity of A at a prime
items.statement: For a prime ideal p of A, A is regular at p when the local ring A_p is regular.
items.note: 'A is regular at p' is `IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)`. Mathlib's definition (the span rank of the maximal ideal equals `ringKrullDim`) is the paper's edim = dim convention, by `iff_finrank_cotangentSpace`. Mathlib's `IsRegularRing` is defined with exactly this pattern at every prime. No separate 'regular at p' predicate is named.

items.name: Lescot's criterion for regularity via the Ext map
items.statement: For a noetherian local ring R with residue field k and Krull dimension c, the map Ext^c_R(k, R) → Ext^c_R(k, k) induced by the surjection R → k is nonzero if and only if R is regular. (Lescot [42, 1.4]; see also Avramov–Iyengar [5, Theorem 2.4].) Also used: for a local ring R the vector spaces Ext^i_R(k,k) are nonzero for 0 ≤ i ≤ dim R (Bruns–Herzog [13, Cor. 1.3.2, Thm. 1.3.3]).
items.note: Neither library has Lescot's criterion: Ext^c_R(k,R) → Ext^c_R(k,k) is nonzero iff R is regular. Nor do they have the nonvanishing of Ext^i_R(k,k) for 0 ≤ i ≤ dim R. Mathlib has only the regular-local-ring definition and `projectiveDimension`, with no global-dimension characterisation of regularity. No atlas layer mentions Lescot or the evaluation map. R03.3's accepted decomposition plans 'regular iff finite global dimension' (Serre), which a proof of the nonvanishing claim may use, but not this criterion.

items.name: Theorem 2.5: regularity at p_A is detected by the congruence module
items.statement: In the context of 2.2 (A noetherian local, λ_A: A → O surjective, c = height p_A), A is regular at p_A if and only if the O-module Ψ_A is torsion; equivalently, iff the map Ext^c_A(O, λ_A) has nonzero rank. When this holds: (1) the O-modules F^c_A(A) and F^c_A(O) are free of rank one; (2) F^c_A(λ_A): F^c_A(A) → F^c_A(O) is injective; (3) Ψ_A is torsion and cyclic.
items.note: This is the paper's own result and is missing (it depends on F^c_A, Ψ_A and Lescot's criterion, all missing). Mathlib can express its hypotheses (regularity at p_A via `IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)`, and rank) but has none of its objects.

items.name: Lemma 2.6: vanishing of F^n above the codimension; Ψ_A(M) is torsion
items.statement: Let λ_A: A → O be as in 2.2 with A regular at p_A, and M a finitely generated A-module. Then F^n_A(M) = 0 for every n ≥ height p_A + 1, and the O-module Ψ_A(M) is torsion (hence of finite length). The proof uses: for a regular local ring R of dimension c with residue field κ and any R-module N, κ ⊗_R N ≅ Ext^c_R(κ, N) naturally.
items.note: Missing: both the vanishing of F^n_A(M) for n > height p_A and the torsion-ness of Ψ_A(M). The regular-local-ring input κ ⊗_R N ≅ Ext^c_R(κ,N) is also missing. It needs RHom_R(κ,R) ≃ κ[−c], Koszul self-duality, and the tensor-evaluation isomorphism for the perfect complex κ. The Koszul complex is planned in IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6; RHom and ⊗^L are planned in tauceti DGAInfinity layer 5 and P7.

items.name: The cotangent (conormal) module p_A/p_A² and Φ_A
items.statement: The cotangent module of λ_A is the finitely generated O-module p_A/p_A². Its torsion submodule is Φ_A := tors(p_A/p_A²) (2.8). When c = 0 and A is regular at p_A, Φ_A = p_A/p_A².
items.note: The cotangent module p_A/p_A² is `Ideal.Cotangent p_A`, a module over A ⧸ p_A. That ring is identified with O by `RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective` λ_A, and Φ_A is its `Submodule.torsion`. The remark that Φ_A = p/p² when c = 0 and A is regular at p_A is a consequence of Lemma 2.7, which is missing.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: rank of the cotangent module is the embedding dimension of A_{p_A}
items.statement: For λ_A: A → O as in 2.2, rank_O(p_A/p_A²) = edim A_{p_A}. Thus height p_A ≤ rank_O(p_A/p_A²), with equality if and only if A is regular at p_A.
items.note: The identity rank_O(p/p²) = edim A_p, and the resulting criterion 'height p ≤ rank, with equality iff A_p is regular', are not in the libraries or the atlas. The key step (p/p²)_p ≅ pA_p/(pA_p)² follows from Mathlib's flat base change of cotangent modules (`Ideal.tensorCotangentEquiv`, since localization is flat), with `iff_finrank_cotangentSpace` then giving the regularity criterion. Tau Ceti's `Ideal.cotangentLocalizationEquiv` covers only a maximal ideal, a near miss because p_A is not maximal.

items.name: The categories C_O and C_O(c)
items.statement: (§2, p. 16) C_O is the category of pairs (A, λ_A) where A is a complete noetherian local ring and λ_A: A → O is a surjective local homomorphism with A regular at p_A := Ker(λ_A), i.e. A_{p_A} is a regular local ring. The paper says only that the morphisms are 'the obvious ones'; in later use (e.g. 7.1) a morphism φ: (A, λ_A) → (B, λ_B) is a local homomorphism with λ_B ∘ φ = λ_A. Completeness is imposed 'only for ease of exposition, especially in Section 5 and beyond'. One often speaks of the ring A being in C_O. C_O(c) is the subcategory of C_O of those A with height p_A = c, equivalently rank_O(p_A/p_A²) = c (Lemma 2.7). (The Introduction, p. 4, and the Glossary, p. 80, describe the narrower class of pairs with A a complete local noetherian O-algebra (in CNL_O) and λ a surjective O-algebra map; the Introduction says the text treats a larger class.)
items.locator: §2 ('Wiles defect'), p. 16; cf. Introduction p. 4 and Glossary p. 80
items.note: No library or layer defines the category of pairs (A, λ_A: A ↠ O) with A complete Noetherian local and A_{p_A} regular, or its subcategories C_O(c). DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1 plans the coefficient categories C_Λ and Ĉ_Λ, objects with a residue-field identification. That is a near miss: it has no augmentation to O and no regularity at p_A. See sourceIssues E23: the §2 definition must require O-algebras.

items.name: The Wiles defect δ_A(M)
items.statement: For A in C_O(c) and a finitely generated A-module M, the Wiles defect is the integer δ_A(M) := (rank_{A_{p_A}} M_{p_A}) · length_O Φ_A − length_O Ψ_A(M) (2.9). For c = 0 this is the invariant of [7, 12]; for M = A Cohen–Macaulay an analogous invariant was introduced in [8].
items.note: The invariant δ_A(M) = rank_{A_p}(M_p)·length Φ_A − length Ψ_A(M) is missing. Its ingredients `Module.length`, `Module.finrank`, `Ideal.Cotangent` and `Submodule.torsion` exist, but Ψ_A(M) does not. No atlas layer mentions the Wiles defect or the numerical criterion.

items.name: Proposition 2.10: comparison with Diamond's congruence module when c = 0
items.statement: For an ideal J of A and an A-module M, write M[J] := {m ∈ M : Jm = 0} (so A[J] = Ann_A J). Suppose A is in C_O(0) and set I_A := A[p_A]. For any finitely generated A-module M there is a natural surjection of O-modules M/(M[p_A] + M[I_A]) ↠ Ψ_A(M) whose kernel is a torsion O-module; it is an isomorphism if depth_A M ≥ 1. Moreover, when depth_A M ≥ 1 one has M/M[I_A] = (M/p_A M)^tf, so the module on the left can be recovered without recourse to I_A. (This reconciles Ψ_A(M) with Diamond's congruence module for c = 0.)
items.note: Missing: the comparison with Diamond's congruence module in codimension 0, M/(M[p_A] + M[I_A]) ↠ Ψ_A(M), an isomorphism when depth M ≥ 1, together with M/M[I_A] = (M/p_A M)^tf. Mathlib can form M[I] (`Submodule.torsionBySet`) and annihilators, but has no depth invariant and no Ψ_A. No layer plans this comparison. AutomorphicCongruences:L0 and SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.1 mention congruence modules only for particular Hecke modules.

items.name: Example 2.11: the comparison map need not be injective in depth zero
items.statement: Let A := O[[t]]/(ϖ²t) (in C_O(0)) and M := A/(ϖ³). Then M is O-torsion so Ψ_A(M) = 0, whereas I_A = (ϖ²), M[p_A] = (ϖ²)M, M[I_A] = (ϖ, t)M, and M/(M[p_A] + M[I_A]) ≅ O/(ϖ).
items.note: This is an example, and it is missing. I checked it by hand. In A = O[[t]]/(ϖ²t), A_{(t)} is a field, so A is in C_O(0) and I_A = (ϖ²). For M = A/(ϖ³): M[p_A] = ϖ²M and M[I_A] = (ϖ,t)M, so M/(M[p_A] + M[I_A]) ≅ O/ϖ, while Ψ_A(M) = 0 because F^0 of the O-torsion modules M and M/p_A M vanishes.

items.name: grade(I, M): length of a maximal M-regular sequence in I
items.statement: For an ideal I of the noetherian local ring A and a finitely generated A-module M, grade(I, M) is the length of the longest M-regular sequence contained in I (∞ if IM = M); depth_A M = grade(m_A, M), and grade(I, M) ≤ depth_A M. Facts used in §3 for A in C_O(c): grade(p_A, M) ≤ depth_{A_{p_A}} M_{p_A} ('clear'); depth_A M ≤ grade(p_A, M) + 1 for every finitely generated M, by [13, Exercise 1.2.23], since dim(A/p_A) = dim O = 1; grade(p_A, M) = min{depth_{A_{p_A}} M_{p_A}, depth_A M}, because p_A and m_A are the only primes containing p_A ([13, Prop. 1.2.10]); and Ext^i_A(A/I, M) = 0 for i < grade(I, M) ([13, Theorem 1.2.5]), applied with A/I = k and A/I = O.
items.locator: §3, p. 17 (and proofs of Lemmas 3.1, 3.2, 3.10, pp. 17–20); Glossary p. 80
items.note: Mathlib has M-regular sequences and Rees's theorem, which covers [13, Thm 1.2.5] when IM ≠ M: an M-regular sequence of length n in I gives Ext^i(W,M) = 0 for i < n when Supp W ⊆ V(I). But neither library defines grade(I,M) or depth; Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/Depth.lean is an empty deprecated module. R03.3 plans depth and regular sequences, and grade(I,M) is the I-depth. Its accepted decomposition, however, covers only depth at the maximal ideal. The facts used here — grade(p,M) ≤ depth M_p, BH Prop. 1.2.10 (grade = min depth over V(I)) and BH Ex. 1.2.23 — are not among its nodes; R03.3's coverage is 'partial'. The paper is a good source for them.

items.name: Lemma 3.1: depth and grade bounds for A in C_O(c)
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module. (1) If M_{p_A} ≠ 0 then grade(p_A, M) ≤ c and depth_A M ≤ c + 1. (2) If grade(p_A, M) ≤ c and depth_A M ≥ c + 1 then grade(p_A, M) = c and depth_A M = c + 1. (3) If grade(p_A, M) ≥ c then M is free at p_A (M_{p_A} is a free A_{p_A}-module). In particular depth A ≤ c + 1 ≤ dim A.
items.note: This is the paper's own lemma for A in C_O(c) and it is missing. Its inputs are planned in R03.3 or listed in the grade item: the grade and depth inequalities, BH Ex. 1.2.23, Auslander–Buchsbaum, and dim A/p + height p ≤ dim A. The library covers none of them except the dimension inequality in order-theoretic form.

items.name: Lemma 3.2: modules of depth at least c + 1
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module with depth_A M ≥ c + 1. (1) If M is supported at p_A (M_{p_A} ≠ 0), then grade(p_A, M) = c and depth_A M = c + 1. (2) If M is not supported at p_A, then grade(p_A, M) = depth_A M. (3) M is free at p_A. (4) Ext^c_A(O, M) is a torsion-free O-module. Summary 3.3: for A in C_O(c) and M in mod A, depth_A M ≥ c + 1 ⇒ grade(p_A, M) ≥ c ⇒ depth_A M ≥ c, and grade(p_A, M) ≥ c ⇒ M is free at p_A. The two conditions grade(p_A, M) ≥ c and depth_A M ≥ c are vacuous when c = 0, while depth_A M ≥ c + 1 is not. (Depth ≥ c+1 is used for the freeness and complete-intersection criteria of §9, the grade condition for reduction to c = 0 in §8, and only depth ≥ c for invariance of domain in §7.)
items.note: Missing (the paper's own lemma). Part (4), that Ext^c_A(O,M) is torsion-free when depth M ≥ c+1, uses the vanishing Ext^c_A(k,M) = 0. That vanishing is Rees's theorem, which is in Mathlib. Parts (1)–(3) need grade, depth, BH 1.2.10 and Auslander–Buchsbaum, which are planned in R03.3. See sourceIssues E20.

items.name: The second symbolic power p^(2)
items.statement: For a prime ideal p of a ring A, p^(2) := p²A_p ∩ A, the second symbolic power.
items.note: Neither library has symbolic powers. The only mention is a docstring in Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Eisenstein/Criterion.lean:51-53: 'The mod P^2 hypothesis will have to be rephrased to a condition in the second symbolic power of P'. No atlas stage mentions symbolic powers. The definition p^(2) = comap (A → A_p) of (pA_p)² is expressible with `Ideal.comap`, `Ideal.map` and `Localization.AtPrime`, but it has not been made.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: cutting down by one element outside p_A^(2)
items.statement: Fix A in C_O(c) with c ≥ 1 and f ∈ p_A nonzero in A_{p_A}. The local ring A/fA (with the induced augmentation) is in C_O if and only if f ∉ p_A^(2); in that case A/fA is in C_O(c − 1).
items.note: Missing (the paper's own lemma): A/fA is in C_O iff f ∉ p_A^(2), and then it is in C_O(c−1). It needs the regular-quotient criterion BH 2.2.4, which is in neither library (the Mathlib regular-local-ring API has no quotient lemma), together with the missing symbolic square and C_O(c).

items.name: Lemma 3.5: regular sequences reducing the codimension
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module with grade(p_A, M) ≥ c. For any 1 ≤ n ≤ c there is a sequence g = g_1, …, g_n in p_A such that (1) A/gA is in C_O(c − n); (2) g is M-regular and depth_{A/gA}(M/gM) = depth_A M − n. When A is Cohen–Macaulay, g can be chosen A-regular as well. (Proof by prime avoidance, Kaplansky [36, Theorem 81], avoiding Ass M and p_A^(2).)
items.note: Missing (the paper's own lemma). The prime-avoidance step (avoiding Ass M, Ass A and the non-prime ideal p_A^(2)) is covered by `Ideal.subset_union_prime`, which allows two non-prime ideals. Mathlib also has regular sequences and the finiteness of associated primes. The drop depth(M/gM) = depth M − 1 is planned in R03.3; membership in C_O(c−n) needs Lemma 3.4, which is missing.

items.name: The map η_M: F^c_A(A) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf → F^c_A(M) and diagram (3.6)
items.statement: Let A be as in 2.2 (in use, A in C_O(c)) and M a finitely generated A-module. The natural morphism RHom_A(O, A) ⊗^L_A M → RHom_A(O, M) and the Künneth map induce the O-linear map Ext^c_A(O, A) ⊗_A M → Ext^c_A(O, M). Here Ext^c_A(O, A) ⊗_A M = Ext^c_A(O, A) ⊗_O (M/p_A M). Hence, on torsion-free quotients, it induces η_M: F^c_A(A) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf → F^c_A(M). Diagram (3.6) commutes: under the isomorphism (2.4) F^c_A(M/p_A M) ≅ F^c_A(O) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf, the composite F^c_A(λ_A(M)) ∘ η_M equals F^c_A(λ_A) ⊗ id: F^c_A(A) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf → F^c_A(O) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf. Such a diagram exists for each cohomological index i, with F^i in place of F^c.
items.note: Missing. The construction needs the tensor-evaluation morphism RHom_A(O,A) ⊗^L_A M → RHom_A(O,M) and the Künneth map H(X) ⊗ H(Y) → H(X ⊗^L Y), neither of which is in either library. RHom and ⊗^L are planned (tauceti DGAInfinity layer 5, P7); this morphism, the Künneth map in the module setting, the map η_M and diagram (3.6) are not.

items.name: Lemma 3.7: the defect formula
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module free at p_A. Then F^c_A(λ_A(M)) is injective, and there is an exact sequence of O-modules 0 → Coker(η_M) → Ψ_A ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf → Ψ_A(M) → 0. Hence δ_A(M) = rank_{A_{p_A}}(M_{p_A}) · δ_A(A) + length_O Coker(η_M), using rank_{A_{p_A}} M_{p_A} = rank_O (M/p_A M)^tf. The paper says this generalizes Brochard–Iyengar–Khare [12, Theorem 1.2], the case c = 0. For c = 0, with I_A := A[p_A], one has Coker(η_M) = M[p_A]/(I_A M + tors_O M[p_A]). This equals M[p_A]/I_A M when M[p_A] is O-torsion-free, e.g. when depth_A M ≥ 1. (The printed remark omits this condition: sourceIssues E21.)
items.note: Missing: the defect formula δ_A(M) = rank·δ_A(A) + length Coker η_M. It depends on η_M, Ψ_A, Theorem 2.5 and the freeness of M at p_A, all missing. I checked the exact sequence by hand from (3.6): the injective top row gives coker(F^c(λ_A(M))∘η_M) ↠ Ψ_A(M), with kernel ≅ Coker η_M. See sourceIssues E21 for the c = 0 remark.

items.name: Lemma 3.10: change of congruence modules along maps of modules of equal rank
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and π: M → N a map of finitely generated A-modules, both free at p_A of the same rank. (1) F^c_A(M) and F^c_A(N) are free O-modules of the same rank. (2) If π is surjective, then F^c_A(π) is injective and F^c_A(π ⊗_A O) is bijective, hence length_O Ψ_A(M) = length_O Ψ_A(N) + length_O Coker F^c_A(π). (3) If π is injective with cokernel of depth c + 1, then F^c_A(π) is bijective.
items.note: Missing (the paper's own lemma): F^c_A(M) and F^c_A(N) have equal rank, the length formula for surjections, and bijectivity when the cokernel has depth c+1. It needs F^c_A, Ψ_A and Lemmas 3.2 and 3.7. The Ext vanishing step, Ext^c_A(O,C) = 0 when grade(p_A,C) = c+1, is covered in Mathlib by Rees's theorem.

items.name: Normalized dualizing complex ω_A and the duality functor ω_A(−)
items.statement: Since each A in C_O is a quotient of a regular ring, namely a power series ring over O [this presumes, as in the Introduction p. 4 and the Glossary p. 80, that A is an O-algebra and λ_A a map of O-algebras; sourceIssues E23], A has a dualizing complex ω_A. It is unique up to isomorphism in D(A) once normalized so that Ext^i_A(k, ω_A) ≠ 0 precisely when i = 0 (Stacks [51, Tag 0A7M]). For an A-complex M in D(A), ω_A(M) := RHom_A(M, ω_A) (4.1). The assignment M ↦ ω_A(M) induces an auto-equivalence ω_A(−): D^b(mod A)^op → D^b(mod A), so the biduality map M → ω_A^2(M) is an isomorphism for M in D^b(mod A). Facts about ω used in §4 and later: ω_A(O) = RHom_A(O, ω_A) is the (normalized) dualizing complex of O, and hence ω_A(O) ≅ O[1] because O is Gorenstein of dimension 1 ([51, Tags 0AX1, 0DW7]). If A (or any Gorenstein local ring R) is Gorenstein, then ω_A ≅ A[dim A] in D(A) ([51, Tag 0DW7]).
items.locator: §4 ('Dualizing complexes'), (4.1), p. 21; ω_A(O) ≅ O[1]: proof of Proposition 4.7, p. 23; ω_R ≅ R[dim R] for Gorenstein R: §9, p. 38 and 11.1, p. 49
items.note: Neither library has dualizing complexes, a derived Hom functor RHom_A(−,−) on D(A), derived tensor products of modules, biduality, or Gorenstein rings. Mathlib has only the derived category, Ext groups and a definition of local cohomology with no duality theorems. No atlas layer plans normalized dualizing complexes of Noetherian local rings. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.1 only lists 'dualizing modules' in an inventory, tauceti StableReduction layer 2 plans the relative dualizing sheaf of Cohen–Macaulay curves, and AnalyticStacks:AS.1 (a new roadmap) plans proper-smooth Grothendieck–Serre duality in a six-functor formalism.

items.name: (4.2) Depth and dimension via the dualizing complex
items.statement: For a nonzero finitely generated A-module M: depth_A M = min{i | H_i(ω_A(M)) ≠ 0} and dim M = max{i | H_i(ω_A(M)) ≠ 0}. (Grothendieck local duality; Stacks [51, Tag 0DWZ]; Bruns–Herzog [13, Theorem 3.5.7].)
items.note: (4.2), depth_A M = min{i : H_i(ω_A(M)) ≠ 0} and dim M = max{i : H_i(ω_A(M)) ≠ 0}, needs dualizing complexes and Grothendieck local duality, which exist in neither library. Mathlib has Rees' theorem (depth-type Ext vanishing ⇔ regular sequences) and a bare definition of local cohomology, but no depth invariant, no Grothendieck vanishing/non-vanishing and no local duality. The reviewed DDPA decomposition node R03.3/depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds plans only depth = least i with Ext^i(R/m, M) ≠ 0 and dim Supp M ≥ depth M, not the dualizing-complex formula.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulay modules, the dual M^∨ and self-duality
items.statement: Fix A in C_O(c). An A-module M is Cohen–Macaulay if it is finitely generated and depth_A M ≥ dim M; equality holds when M ≠ 0. If M is Cohen–Macaulay, then H_i(ω_A(M)) = 0 for all i ≠ dim_A M. For a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay M with d := dim_A M, the A-module M^∨ := H_d(ω_A(M)) (4.3), the dual of M, is also Cohen–Macaulay of dimension d (easy, given M ≃ ω_A^2(M)), and ω_A(M) ≃ M^∨[d] in D(A). The paper then states that M ↦ M^∨ is an auto-equivalence on the category of Cohen–Macaulay A-modules. (Read with d fixed: M ↦ M^∨ is a contravariant self-equivalence, M^∨∨ ≅ M, of the category of Cohen–Macaulay A-modules of dimension d; every use in the paper has d fixed.) A Cohen–Macaulay module M is self-dual if there is an isomorphism of A-modules M ≅ M^∨. (The paper uses 'maximal Cohen–Macaulay' from 4.8 on without defining it; the standard meaning is finitely generated with depth_A M = dim A.)
items.note: Cohen–Macaulay modules (depth ≥ dim) are planned in DDPA:R03.3, and so implicitly are maximal CM modules. The audit finds 'No Cohen–Macaulay (or maximal Cohen–Macaulay, Gorenstein local) predicate in either tree'. The item's main content is not planned anywhere: the dual M^∨ := H_d(ω_A(M)) of (4.3), ω_A(M) ≃ M^∨[d], the auto-equivalence M ↦ M^∨ and self-duality all need the dualizing complex. Recommend splitting: the CM/MCM definition is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3), and the dual is missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.4: change of congruence module along a surjection of self-dual Cohen–Macaulay modules
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M, N self-dual Cohen–Macaulay A-modules of dimension c + 1 with the same rank at p_A. If π: M → N is surjective then length_O Ψ_A(M) − length_O Ψ_A(N) = ν_O(det α) = ν_O(det β), where ν_O is the valuation of O and α: F^c_A(M) → F^c_A(M), β: F^c_A(N) → F^c_A(N) are the composites F^c_A(M) →(F^c(π)) F^c_A(N) ≅ F^c_A(N^∨) →(F^c(π^∨)) F^c_A(M^∨) ≅ F^c_A(M) and F^c_A(N) ≅ F^c_A(N^∨) →(F^c(π^∨)) F^c_A(M^∨) ≅ F^c_A(M) →(F^c(π)) F^c_A(N), using the chosen self-dualities.
items.note: This is a length formula for the paper's congruence modules Ψ_A along a surjection of self-dual CM modules of dimension c+1, using F^c_A (cluster C1), the CM dual and Lemma 3.10. Neither library has Ψ_A, F^c_A or CM duals; LinearMap.det and DVR valuations exist but are only generic ingredients. The atlas's congruence modules are classical Hecke-module constructions with no higher-codimension Ψ_A(M): AutomorphicCongruences:L0 imports them from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants, and SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.1 and PadicFamilies:L1 also build them.

items.name: The pairing ⟨−,−⟩: Ext^c_A(O, M) ⊗_O Ext^c_A(O, M^∨) → F^c_A(O) ≅ O
items.statement: For A in C_O(c) and M Cohen–Macaulay of dimension c + 1, biduality gives a pairing M ⊗^L_A M^∨ ≃ M ⊗^L_A ω_A(M)[−c−1] → ω_A[−c−1] (4.5). For α: O → M[c] and β: O → M^∨[c] in D(A), α ⊗ β: O ⊗^L_A O → (M ⊗^L_A M^∨)[2c] → ω_A[c−1] induces by adjunction γ: O → RHom_A(O, ω_A[c−1]) ≃ O[c] (O Gorenstein of dimension 1); ⟨α, β⟩ is the class of γ in F^c_A(O) ≅ O (4.6).
items.note: The pairing Ext^c_A(O,M) ⊗_O Ext^c_A(O,M^∨) → F^c_A(O) ≅ O is built from M ⊗^L_A M^∨ → ω_A[−c−1] (adjoint of biduality, Stacks 0A5W), ⊗^L/RHom adjunction and ω_O ≅ O[1]. None of these exists in the libraries: Mathlib has Ext and composition in D(A), but no derived tensor product of modules, no RHom object and no dualizing complex. EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1 plans derived internal Hom and derived tensor as infrastructure, but no layer plans this pairing or the duality inputs.

items.name: Proposition 4.7: the congruence module as the cokernel of the pairing
items.statement: For A in C_O(c) and M a Cohen–Macaulay A-module of dimension c + 1, Ψ_A(M) is the cokernel of the map Ext^c_A(O, M) → Hom_O(Ext^c_A(O, M^∨), F^c_A(O)) adjoint to the pairing (4.6).
items.note: This describes Ψ_A(M) as the cokernel of the map adjoint to (4.6), for M CM of dimension c+1. The proof uses the adjunctions and ω_A(O) ≅ O[1] (O Gorenstein of dimension 1, Stacks 0AX1, 0DW7). There is no congruence module, dualizing complex or pairing in either library, and no layer plans it.

items.name: 4.8: the pairing via a Gorenstein ring and the codimension-zero case
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a Cohen–Macaulay A-module of dimension c + 1. Suppose there is a map R → A with R a Gorenstein (local) ring of dimension c + 1 and M finitely generated over R. Then M is maximal Cohen–Macaulay as an R-module, hence M^∨ ≅ Hom_R(M, R), and the pairing (4.6) is induced by the natural pairing M ⊗_R Hom_R(M, R) → R. When c = 0 one can take R = O [provided M is finitely generated as an O-module; the paper leaves this implicit: sourceIssues E27]. The pairing (4.6) is then the composite M[p_A] ⊗_O Hom_O(M, O)[p_A] ⊆ M ⊗_O Hom_O(M, O) → O. This reconciles the congruence modules of this paper with those of Böckle–Khare–Manning [7, §3].
items.note: For R → A with R Gorenstein of dimension c+1, this uses M MCM over R, M^∨ ≅ Hom_R(M,R), and (4.6) induced by M ⊗_R Hom_R(M,R) → R. For c = 0 (R = O) it reconciles Ψ_A(M) with the congruence module of Böckle–Khare–Manning [7, §3]. Neither library has Gorenstein rings, MCM modules or CM duals. The evaluation map M ⊗ Hom(M,R) → R is Mathlib's contractRight/contractLeft, only a generic ingredient. The classical c = 0 congruence modules planned for Hecke modules (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.1, PadicFamilies:L1, via IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants/AutomorphicCongruences:L0) do not state this comparison. See sourceIssues E27.

items.name: Tate cohomology modules Ext-hat^i_A(O, M) (Buchweitz)
items.statement: For A in C_O(c) Gorenstein and M maximal Cohen–Macaulay, the paper uses Buchweitz's Tate cohomology modules of the pair (O, M), written \underline{Ext}^i_A(O, M), citing [14, Definition 6.1.1] without recalling a definition. It also uses the map H^c N(O, M): Tor^A_{−c}(M, RHom_A(O, A)) → Ext^c_A(O, M) of [14, Theorem 6.2.5]; the paper prints ω_A(O) in place of RHom_A(O, A) (sourceIssues: E8). By part (3) of op. cit., this map sits in an exact sequence of O-modules Tor^A_{−c}(M, RHom_A(O, A)) → Ext^c_A(O, M) → \underline{Ext}^c_A(O, M) → 0.
items.locator: Before Proposition 4.9, p. 23, and proof of Proposition 4.9, p. 24 (citing [14, Definition 6.1.1, Theorem 6.2.5(3)])
items.note: Buchweitz's Tate cohomology (Definition 6.1.1, written with an underlined Ext in the paper) and the norm map H^c N(X,M): Tor^A_{−c}(M, RHom_A(X,A)) → Ext^c_A(X,M) with the exact sequence of Theorem 6.2.5 are absent from both libraries. Mathlib's tateCohomology is Tate cohomology of a finite group (Rep R G), a different notion. tauceti StablePeriodicCurved layer 2 plans totally acyclic complexes/complete resolutions, Iwanaga–Gorenstein rings, D_sg(R) and Buchweitz's equivalence stable(Gproj-R) ≃ D_sg(R), but not the Tate cohomology modules nor the norm-map sequence. So this is a near miss, not planned.

items.name: Proposition 4.9: Coker(η_M) is Tate cohomology
items.statement: Let A in C_O(c) be Gorenstein and M a maximal Cohen–Macaulay A-module. Then there is an isomorphism of O-modules Coker(η_M) ≅ \underline{Ext}^c_A(O, M), the Tate cohomology of the pair (O, M) in degree c in the sense of Buchweitz [14, Definition 6.1.1]. Here η_M: F^c_A(A) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf → F^c_A(M) is the map of (3.6), whose cokernel appears in the defect formula, Lemma 3.7.
items.note: Coker(η_M) ≅ Tate cohomology in degree c, for A Gorenstein in C_O and M MCM. It needs η_M (C1), Tate cohomology (previous item), ω_A(O) and Buchweitz 6.2.5, none of which is in the libraries or planned. The proof has misprints already recorded as source issue E8: the printed 'ω_A(O) ≅ Ext^c_A(O,A)[−c]' is the formula for RHom_A(O,A), and 'i ≤ c+1' should be 'i ≥ c+1'. The proposition is not used in the proofs of the main theorems; Lemma 9.4 is proved directly. The proof has misprints and misidentifies η_M (sourceIssues E8, E32).

items.name: (9.1) Maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules over a Gorenstein ring
items.statement: A noetherian local ring R is Gorenstein if R has finite injective dimension as a module over itself. Over a Gorenstein local ring R, a finitely generated R-module M is maximal Cohen–Macaulay iff Ext^i_R(M, R) = 0 for all i ≥ 1 (9.1) (from (4.2), ω_R ≅ R[dim R]; [13, Theorem 3.3.10]).
items.note: Mathlib can express 'R has finite injective dimension over itself' through CategoryTheory.injectiveDimension, but it has no Gorenstein-ring predicate, no MCM notion and no (9.1): MCM ⇔ Ext^i_R(M,R) = 0 for i ≥ 1. The Gorenstein definition is essentially planned: tauceti StablePeriodicCurved layer 2 plans Iwanaga–Gorenstein rings, which for commutative Noetherian local rings agree with the paper's definition, and DDPA:R03.3 plans CM modules. The characterization (9.1) is planned nowhere. StablePeriodicCurved layer 7 relates Gorenstein-projectives to MCM modules only over hypersurfaces S/(w).

items.name: Multiplicity e_A(M) (Hilbert–Samuel)
items.statement: e_A(M) is the multiplicity of the finitely generated A-module M with respect to the maximal ideal [13, §4.6]; e(A) := e_A(A). Facts used: e_A is additive on direct sums of modules of dimension dim A, and a nonzero maximal Cohen–Macaulay module has positive multiplicity.
items.note: Neither library has the Hilbert–Samuel function or the multiplicity e_A(M) of a finitely generated module over a local ring, nor additivity on modules of dimension dim A or positivity for nonzero MCM modules. Mathlib's Polynomial.hilbertPoly is only the formal polynomial attached to p/(1−X)^d, with graded-module Hilbert polynomials still a TODO. Module.length exists. No atlas stage mentions Hilbert–Samuel. PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp:R30.5 and CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility:R31.5 mention Breuil–Mézard 'multiplicity statements' but plan no general e_A(M).

items.name: The trace map τ_M(R) and the trace-ideal criterion for a free summand
items.statement: For a module M over a local ring R, τ_M(R): Hom_R(M, R) ⊗_R M → R, f ⊗ m ↦ f(m). R is a direct summand of M iff τ_M(R) is surjective (Lindo [43, Proposition 2.8(iii)]).
items.note: The map τ_M(R) is in Mathlib as contractLeft R M : Module.Dual R M ⊗[R] M →ₗ[R] R (f ⊗ m ↦ f m). Mathlib also splits surjections onto projective or finite free modules. The criterion itself is not a declaration: over a local ring, R is a direct summand of M iff τ_M(R) is surjective (Lindo, Prop. 2.8(iii)), and the step that one f_i(m_i) is a unit is not stated. No atlas layer plans trace ideals or free-summand criteria.

items.name: Lemma 9.3: lifting free summands along a regular element
items.statement: Let R be a Gorenstein local ring, M ∈ mod R (finitely generated) a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module, and x ∈ R not a zero-divisor on R and on M (x lies in the maximal ideal in every application, and the Nakayama step of the proof uses this). If the R/xR-module M/xM has a free summand of rank µ, then so does the R-module M.
items.note: This lifts free summands from M/xM to M for an MCM module over a Gorenstein local ring, using the trace-ideal criterion, Nakayama and Ext^1_R(M,R) = 0 from (9.1). Neither library has Gorenstein rings, MCM modules or the trace criterion. Generic ingredients exist: Nakayama, contractLeft, and IsSMulRegular short exact sequences in ModuleCat. No layer plans it.

items.name: Artinian Gorenstein rings: socle and self-injectivity
items.statement: For a Gorenstein local ring S′ of Krull dimension zero, the socle Soc(S′) is the smallest nonzero ideal and S′ is injective as a module over itself; hence for an S′-module N′ and a ∈ N′ with Soc(S′)a ≠ 0, the map S′ → N′, 1 ↦ a, is split injective. Also used: Ext^r_S(k, N) ≅ Soc(N/xN) for x an N-regular sequence of length r in m_S ([13, Lemma 3.1.16]).
items.note: Nothing states that for a zero-dimensional Gorenstein local ring S′ the socle is the smallest nonzero ideal and S′ is self-injective. The same holds for the resulting split-injectivity of S′ → N′ and for Ext^r_S(k,N) ≅ Soc(N/xN) (Bruns–Herzog 3.1.16). Tau Ceti has TauCeti.socle (the sum of simple submodules; equal to (0 :_N m) over a local ring only after a comparison) and self-injectivity of Frobenius algebras over a field. That is a near miss, since S′ need not be an algebra over a field (e.g. mixed characteristic). PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 plans self-injectivity only of R/aR for Gorenstein O-orders, a special case.

items.name: Lemma 9.4: a free summand from surjectivity of Ext^c_R(O,R) ⊗ M → Ext^c_R(O,M)
items.statement: Let R be a Gorenstein local ring, M a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module, λ: R → O a surjective map, p := Ker λ and c := height p. If the natural map η̃_M: Ext^c_R(O, R) ⊗_R M → Ext^c_R(O, M) is surjective and M_p ≠ 0, then M has a free R-summand. (The hypothesis on Ext is the vanishing of Tate cohomology Êxt^c_R(O, M).)
items.note: This is the free-summand criterion over a Gorenstein local ring R with λ: R ↠ O: η̃_M: Ext^c_R(O,R) ⊗_R M → Ext^c_R(O,M) surjective and M_p ≠ 0 give a free R-summand. The proof reduces to dimension zero via Lemma 9.3, Bruns–Herzog 3.1.16 and Artinian Gorenstein self-injectivity, and chooses x ∈ λ^{-1}(ϖ) regular on R and M (coset prime avoidance, C1). None of this is in the libraries or planned. The patching freeness results planned in DDPA:R03.5–R03.6 (e.g. Calegari–Geraghty Prop. 2.3, 'H is a free R-module') are different statements. See sourceIssues E28.

items.name: Theorem 9.2 (Theorem B): free summands over Gorenstein rings via the defect
items.statement: Let A be a Gorenstein local ring in C_O and M a maximal Cohen–Macaulay A-module with µ := rank_{A_{p_A}}(M_{p_A}) ≠ 0. Then δ_A(M) = µ · δ_A(A) if and only if M ≅ A^µ ⊕ W with W_{p_A} = 0. When this holds and e_A(M) ≤ µ · e(A), M is free.
items.note: Theorem B: for A Gorenstein in C_O and M MCM with µ = rank M_{p_A} ≠ 0, δ_A(M) = µ·δ_A(A) iff M ≅ A^µ ⊕ W with W_{p_A} = 0, and M is free when additionally e_A(M) ≤ µ·e(A). It needs the Wiles defect δ_A (C1), Lemma 9.4 and Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity, none of which is in the libraries. No layer plans the Wiles–Lenstra–Diamond numerical criterion in any codimension; atlas search finds no 'Wiles defect', 'numerical criterion' or 'Lenstra' in a commutative-algebra layer. GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2–R22.4 and DDPA:R03.5–R03.6 plan patching freeness and support instead.

items.name: Presentations A = O[[t_1,…,t_n]]/I with I ⊆ (ϖ)(t) + (t)² and the linear-part matrix (u_ij)
items.statement: Every A considered is P/I with P := O[[t_1, …, t_n]] and I ⊆ (ϖ)(t) + (t)²; λ_P: P → O is reduction modulo (t) and λ_A the induced map. For a minimal generating set f = f_1, …, f_m of I, each f_i = Σ_j u_ij t_j + g_i uniquely with u_ij ∈ (ϖ)O and g_i ∈ (t)² (5.2), and O^m →(u_ij) O^n → p_A/p_A² → 0 is a presentation of the cotangent module; it depends only on n and the linear parts of the f_i.
items.note: This elementary construction is in neither library nor the atlas. Mathlib supplies the pieces: MvPowerSeries, Ideal.Cotangent, and the kernel description of (t)/(t)² → p_A/p_A² from Ideal.mapCotangent_ker_of_surjective. It does not supply the augmented setting or the linear-part presentation.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: C_O(c)-membership from the linear parts
items.statement: Fix A = P/I as in 5.1 and let c := height p_A (the convention of 2.2). Then A is in C_O(c) iff rank(u_ij) = n − c. When this holds, dim A ≥ c + 1 and height I ≤ n − c, with equality iff dim A = c + 1.
items.note: Missing. It rests on C1's C_O(c) and Lemma 2.7 and on the CM identity height I + dim P/I = dim P. That identity is in R03.3's scope but not yet decomposed; Mathlib has only Krull-type inequalities.

items.name: Normal form (5.4)–(5.5) of the relations and the structure of Φ_A
items.statement: Let A = P/I be as in 5.1 and in C_O(c). Then A can be written as P/(f), where f = f1, …, fm is a minimal generating set of I satisfying (5.4): fi = ϖ^{di} ti + gi with gi ∈ (t)². Here d1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ dm, di < ∞ for i ≤ n − c, and di = ∞ for i > n − c, with the convention ϖ^∞ = 0, so fi = gi for those i. The paper derives this only as 'it also follows from the preceding discussion': diagonalise the linear-part matrix (uij) over O by changing the minimal generators and making an O-linear change of the variables t. Then pA/pA² ≅ O^c ⊕ O/ϖ^{d1}O ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O/ϖ^{d_{n−c}}O as O-modules. So d1, …, d_{n−c} are Fitting invariants of pA/pA² and do not depend on the presentation, and ΦA ≅ O/ϖ^{d1}O ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O/ϖ^{d_{n−c}}O (5.5).
items.note: Missing. Over the DVR O the module content is Mathlib's Smith normal form and PID structure theorem. The ring-level normal form (5.4), independence of the d_i as Fitting invariants and the formula (5.5) for Φ_A are not stated anywhere.

items.name: Complete intersection local rings
items.statement: Let A = P/I be in C_O with P = O[[t1, …, tn]] (a regular local ring), presented as in 5.1. Such a presentation exists when A is an O-algebra and λA is a map of O-algebras. A is a complete intersection if and only if I can be generated by a regular sequence ([13, §2.3]). In that case the minimal generating set f of I is itself a regular sequence (used in the proof of Proposition 6.11 and in 6.12). By Proposition 6.11 this holds if and only if the augmentation A⟨X, Y⟩ → O of the Tate construction of 6.1 is a quasi-isomorphism. Complete intersections are Gorenstein.
items.locator: §9 ('Complete intersection rings'), p. 40; used in Theorem 5.6, Lemma 5.10, Proposition 6.11 and 6.12 (pp. 25–31); 'hence Gorenstein': §15, p. 79
items.note: Planned in R03.3, which plans the complete-intersection notion and criteria. The item's equivalence with acyclicity of the Tate construction is the separate item prop-6-11, which is missing. 'Complete intersections are Gorenstein' is outside R03.3's stated scope: the atlas plans Gorenstein rings only as Iwanaga–Gorenstein rings (tauceti StablePeriodicCurved Layer 2) and Gorenstein orders (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6).

items.name: Theorem 5.6: a regular sequence of relations and a complete intersection with the same cotangent module
items.statement: Fix A in C_O(c) and let h := height I. There is a minimal generating set f = f_1, …, f_m of I, of the form (5.4), whose first h elements f_1, …, f_h form a regular sequence. In particular, when dim A = c + 1, the complete intersection C := O[[t]]/(f_1, …, f_h) is in C_O(c) and C → A induces isomorphisms p_C/p_C² ≅ p_A/p_A² and Φ_C ≅ Φ_A. (The hypothesis on dim A cannot be dropped.)
items.locator: Theorem 5.6, p. 25 (c = 0: Wiles [56, App., Prop. 2]; DDT [22, Thm 5.26])
items.note: Missing; it generalizes Wiles [56, App. Prop. 2] and DDT Thm 5.26 to C_O(c). The printed induction step is wrong (sourceIssues E1: it must use f″ ∈ (f′_{j+2},…,f′_m)²), but the theorem holds; I checked that the E1 counterexample ideal has height 2 and that (ϖ+t₂) is an associated prime of P/(f₁). The printed proof has a failing step (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Example 5.7: choosing the right complete intersection
items.statement: (a) A := O[[s,t]]/(ϖs, ϖ²s + st) is in C_O(1) of dimension two; both O[[s,t]]/(ϖs) and O[[s,t]]/(ϖ²s + st) are complete intersections in C_O(1) mapping onto A, but only the first has the same cotangent module. (b) A := O[[s,t]]/(ϖs, ϖt, st) is in C_O(0) of dimension one; O[[s,t]]/(ϖs, ϖt) is in C_O(0), maps onto A with the same cotangent module but is not a complete intersection, whereas O[[s,t]]/(ϖs, ϖt + st) is a complete intersection with the same cotangent module.
items.note: Missing. These examples show that one must choose the right minimal generators in Theorem 5.6, and they are natural acceptance tests.

items.name: 5.8/(5.9): surjections in C_O(c) induce surjections on Φ
items.statement: For a surjective map ϕ: A → B in C_O(c), the induced map p_A/p_A² → p_B/p_B² is surjective, the induced map (p_A/p_A²)^tf → (p_B/p_B²)^tf is an isomorphism of free O-modules of rank c, and the induced map Φ_ϕ: Φ_A → Φ_B is surjective (snake lemma on diagram (5.9)).
items.note: Missing. Surjectivity on cotangent modules and the snake lemma are in Mathlib. The tf isomorphism for maps in C_O(c) and surjectivity of Φ_ϕ depend on C1's C_O(c), torsion-tf and Φ_A, which are absent.

items.name: André–Quillen homology D_i(B/A; W) and the Jacobi–Zariski sequence
items.statement: For a ring map A → B and a B-module W, Di(B/A; W) denotes the i-th André–Quillen homology module of A → B. The following facts are used in the proof of Lemma 5.10. (i) Jacobi–Zariski: ring maps A → B → C and a C-module W give a long exact sequence ⋯ → D2(C/B;W) → D1(B/A;W) → D1(C/A;W) → D1(C/B;W) → D0(B/A;W) → D0(C/A;W) → D0(C/B;W) → 0. When A → B is surjective, D0(B/A;W) = 0, so the sequence ends ⋯ → D1(C/A;W) → D1(C/B;W) → 0. (ii) If A → B is surjective with kernel J, then D1(B/A; W) = (J/J²) ⊗_B W. In particular D1(O/A; O) = pA/pA². (iii) If the kernel J of a surjection A → B is generated by a regular sequence, then Di(B/A; W) = 0 for i ≥ 2 and J/J² is a free B-module. This is applied to P → O (kernel (t)), giving Di(O/P;O) = 0 for i ≠ 1, and to P → B for B a complete intersection, where D1(B/P; O) is a free O-module. (iv) Localising at pB, the module D2(O/B; O) becomes D2 of the surjection B_{pB} → k(pB), which vanishes when B_{pB} is regular. So D2(O/B; O) is O-torsion for B in C_O.
items.note: Planned in DD.0, with D_i(B/A;W) = H_i(L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B W). Every fact used in Lemma 5.10 follows from DD.0's material: Jacobi–Zariski from the transitivity triangle, D_i(O/P;O) = 0 for i ≠ 1 and D_1(B/P;O) = J/J² ⊗ O free from L ≃ J/J²[1] for regular quotients, and D_1 of a surjection. Mathlib has only the naive H_0/H_1 part.

items.name: Lemma 5.10: isomorphism criterion via Φ for maps onto a complete intersection
items.statement: Let ϕ: A → B be a surjective map in C_O(c) with B a complete intersection. If length_O Φ_A = length_O Φ_B, then ϕ is an isomorphism, and hence A is a complete intersection. (Generalizes DDT [22, Thm 5.21], the case c = 0; the proof shows D_2(O/B; O) = 0 for B a complete intersection in C_O(c).)
items.note: Missing; it generalizes DDT [22, Thm 5.21] to c ≥ 0. The proof needs D_2(O/B;O) = 0 for a CI B in C_O(c), which is planned in DD.0, plus Φ_A and C_O(c) from C1.

items.name: The Koszul complex A⟨X⟩ and the Tate construction A⟨X, Y⟩
items.statement: Let A = P/(f) be as in 5.1, with f a minimal generating set of I. Let A⟨X⟩ be the exterior algebra over A on X = {x1, …, xn}, |xi| = 1, made into a DG algebra by d(xi) = ti. This is the Koszul complex on t, which is a minimal generating set of pA. Write gi = Σ_j g′ij tj with g′ij ∈ (t). The elements zi := Σ_j uij xj + Σ_j g′ij xj (1 ≤ i ≤ m) are cycles of degree one; the paper misprints the first sum as Σ_j uij xi (sourceIssues E5). Since f minimally generates I, the classes of z1, …, zm minimally generate the O-module H1(A⟨X⟩). Adjoin divided-power variables Y = {y1, …, ym} of degree 2 with d(yi) = zi. The result, A⟨X, Y⟩, is the Tate construction of O over A. Up to isomorphism of DG algebras with divided powers, it does not depend on the choice of the minimal generating set of pA or of the minimal generating set of H1(A⟨X⟩). λA extends to a map of DG A-algebras A⟨X, Y⟩ → O sending X and Y to 0, and H1(A⟨X, Y⟩) = 0. Unless A is a complete intersection, A⟨X, Y⟩ has homology in higher degrees (Proposition 6.11).
items.note: Missing. The Koszul complex as a chain complex is planned (DD.1, IHG.6), but the DG-algebra structure and the Tate construction A⟨X,Y⟩ with its independence of choices are not. Misprint E5 applies: z_i = Σ_j (u_ij + g′_ij) x_j, as the item states. See sourceIssues E5.

items.name: The acyclic closure A⟨U⟩ ≃ O and Ext via acyclic closures
items.statement: Adjoining further exterior and divided-power variables extends A⟨X, Y⟩ to an acyclic closure ε: A⟨U⟩ →≃ O (Tate [52, Theorem 1]; Avramov [2, Construction 6.3.1]). Here A⟨U⟩ is the free A-algebra with divided powers on a graded set of variables U = {U_i}_{i≥1}, with U1 = X and U2 = Y. Its differential satisfies (6.2): d(A⟨X⟩) ⊆ (t)A⟨X⟩ and d(A⟨U⟩) ⊆ (ϖ, t)A⟨U⟩. The first inclusion holds by construction. The second says that A⟨U⟩ is a minimal free resolution of O over A. It holds because A → O is large, since it has the algebra section O → A ([4, Corollary 2.7]), and it is not used later. Since A⟨U⟩ is a free resolution of O over A, Ext*_A(O, O) = H*(End_A(A⟨U⟩)), where End_A(A⟨U⟩) = Hom_A(A⟨U⟩, A⟨U⟩) is a DG A-algebra under composition. This makes Ext*_A(O, O) a (typically non-commutative) O-algebra whose product agrees with the Yoneda product up to sign. ε induces a quasi-isomorphism Hom_A(A⟨U⟩, A⟨U⟩) → Hom_A(A⟨U⟩, O). For any A-module or A-complex M, Ext*_A(O, M) ≅ H*(Hom_A(A⟨U⟩, M)), functorially in M.
items.note: Missing. Mathlib computes Ext additively from any projective resolution and has the Yoneda product, but it has no acyclic closure, no DG Γ-structure and no identification of the product with composition in End_A(A⟨U⟩).

items.name: The Γ-derivations θ_i and the class θ_A ∈ Ext^c_A(O, O)
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c), c ≥ 1, presented with relations of the form (5.4), so the classes of t_{n−c+1}, …, t_n form a basis of (p_A/p_A²)^tf. By Iyengar [32, Proposition 1.4] there are A-linear maps θ_i: A⟨U⟩ → A⟨U⟩ (n−c+1 ≤ i ≤ n) that are Γ-derivations with θ_i(x_j) = δ_ij and dθ_i + θ_i d = 0, so each θ_i represents a class in Ext^1_A(O, O); the composite θ_A := ε ∘ θ_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ θ_{n−c+1}: A⟨U⟩ → O (6.4) is a chain map representing a class in Ext^c_A(O, O) with θ_A(x_{n−c+1}⋯x_n) = 1.
items.note: Missing. The construction rests on Iyengar 2001 (PAMS 129) Prop. 1.4, which neither library nor the atlas covers.

items.name: Lemma 6.5: a generator of F^c_A(O)
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and θ: A⟨U⟩ → O any A-linear chain map of upper degree c with θ(A⟨X⟩) = O. Then the class [θ] ∈ Ext^c_A(O, O) generates the free O-module F^c_A(O) (of rank one). In particular this applies to θ_A of (6.4).
items.note: Missing. The short proof needs the acyclic closure, the inclusion (6.2) d(A⟨U⟩) ⊆ (ϖ,t)A⟨U⟩, and C1's F^c_A(O) of rank one.

items.name: The graded O-algebra F*_A(O) and the map ξ_A: ∧_O F^1_A(O) → F*_A(O)
items.statement: F*_A(M) := {F^i_A(M)}_{i≥0}. The O-algebra structure of Ext*_A(O, O) descends to F*_A(O), and F*_A(M) is a graded F*_A(O)-module for every A-complex M. F*_A(O) embeds in Ext*_R(κ, κ) with R := A_{p_A} regular, which is an exterior algebra on Ext^1_R(κ, κ) (Gulliksen–Levin [28, p. 110]); hence F*_A(O) is strictly graded-commutative and there is a natural map of graded O-algebras ξ_A: ∧_O F^1_A(O) → F*_A(O) (6.7), bijective when c = 0.
items.note: Missing. The multiplicative structure of Ext*_A(O,O), its descent to F*, and the regular-local-ring input (Gulliksen–Levin, p. 110) are in neither library nor any layer. DGAInfinity Layer 11 covers only the graded Koszul-algebra analogue over a field.

items.name: Theorem 6.8(1): Ext^1_A(O, O) is the O-dual of the cotangent module
items.statement: For any A in C_O(c) there are isomorphisms of O-modules O^c ≅ Hom_O(p_A/p_A², O) ≅ Ext^1_A(O, O); in particular Ext^1_A(O, O) → F^1_A(O) is bijective.
items.note: Missing. It is a short consequence of Mathlib's Ext long exact sequence and Hom adjunction together with C1's C_O(c) and F^1, but it is not stated anywhere.

items.name: Theorem 6.8(2) (Theorem D): F*_A(O) is the exterior algebra on the dual cotangent module
items.statement: For any A in C_O(c), the map ξA: ∧_O F^1_A(O) → F*_A(O) of (6.7) is bijective. Combined with (1), this gives the natural isomorphism of O-algebras ∧_O Hom_O(pA/pA², O) ≅ (Ext*_A(O, O))^tf of Theorem D. Functoriality (6.9): let ϕ: A → B be a map in C_O. Let F*_ϕ(O): F*_B(O) → F*_A(O) be the map induced on torsion-free quotients by the O-algebra map Ext*_B(O, O) → Ext*_A(O, O) (restriction along ϕ), and let F^1_ϕ(O) be its degree-one component. Then F*_ϕ(O) ∘ ξB = ξA ∘ ∧_O F^1_ϕ(O), and ξA, ξB are isomorphisms.
items.note: Missing; this is the paper's Theorem D. The proof also has misprint E6 (Λ^{r−i}α should read Λ^{c−i}α). Functoriality (6.9) belongs with it. See sourceIssues E6.

items.name: Proposition 6.10: surjections that are isomorphisms at p_A induce isomorphisms on F*(O)
items.statement: Let ϕ: A → B be a surjective map in C_O(c) that is an isomorphism at p_A. Then F*_ϕ(O): F*_B(O) → F*_A(O) is an isomorphism of O-algebras; in particular F^c_ϕ(O) is bijective.
items.note: Missing. Mathlib supplies the exact sequence in the first step; the conclusion needs Theorem 6.8, which is missing.

items.name: Proposition 6.11: complete intersections via the Tate construction
items.statement: Let A be in C_O and A⟨X, Y⟩ its Tate construction. The following are equivalent: (a) A is a complete intersection; (b) A⟨X, Y⟩ → O is a quasi-isomorphism; (c) H_1(A⟨X⟩) is a free O-module and the natural map ∧_O(H_1(A⟨X⟩)) → H_*(A⟨X⟩) is bijective. ((a)⇒(b) Tate [52, Thm 4]; (b)⇔(c) Blanco–Majadas–Rodicio [6, Thm 1]; (c)⇔(a) λ_A is quasi-complete intersection, Avramov–Henriques–Şega [3, Prop. 7.7].)
items.note: Missing. All three implications are cited from the literature: Tate 1957, Blanco–Majadas–Rodicio 1998, Avramov–Henriques–Şega 2013. Misprint E7 (the regular sequence is t_1,…,t_n, not t_1,…,t_m) appears in the proof. See sourceIssues E7.

items.name: 6.12: Ext of a complete intersection in C_O(c)
items.statement: Let A in C_O(c) be a complete intersection. Write A = P/(f) with f = f1, …, fm a regular sequence of the form (5.4), by Theorem 5.6; then m = n − c and d1, …, dm < ∞. By Proposition 6.11, the Tate construction A⟨X, Y⟩ is the acyclic closure of O over A. So Ext*_A(O, O) ≅ H*(Hom_A(A⟨X,Y⟩, O)) ≅ H*(Hom_O(O⟨X,Y⟩, O)), where O⟨X,Y⟩ := O ⊗_A A⟨X,Y⟩ has d(xi) = 0 and d(yi) = ϖ^{di} xi for 1 ≤ i ≤ m. Dually, Hom_O(O⟨X,Y⟩, O) is isomorphic to the complex O⟨η1, …, ηn⟩ ⊗_O O[χ1, …, χm], with ηi exterior of upper degree 1 and χj polynomial of degree 2. Its differential is d(ηi) = ϖ^{di} χi for i ≤ m, d(ηi) = 0 for i > m, and d(χj) = 0. The paper's display of Ext*_A(O,O) as O[η_{m+1},…,ηn,χ]/(ϖ^{di}χi) is false in general (sourceIssues E2), and 'di = ∞ for c+1 ≤ i ≤ n' should read m+1 ≤ i ≤ n (E3). Nevertheless Ext^c_A(O, O) ≅ O·η_{m+1}⋯ηn ⊕ (torsion), so F^c_A(O) is generated by the class of η_{m+1}⋯ηn. The map λA is quasi-complete intersection, and Ext^i_A(O, A) ≅ O for i = c and 0 otherwise ([3, Theorem 2.5(4)]). The paper also asserts, omitting the details, that ΨA ≅ O/(ϖ^{d1+⋯+dm}), which with (5.5) gives δA(A) = 0. This is proved independently in Theorem 9.5; together with Theorem 2.5(3) it gives the displayed ΨA.
items.note: Missing. The item carries the corrected statement: E2 says the paper's display omits higher Koszul homology, and I checked that ϖ(χ₂η₁ − χ₁η₂) = ±d(η₁η₂), so Ext³ ⊇ O/ϖ in the E2 example; E3 fixes d_i = ∞ for i > m. Ext^i_A(O,A) comes from Avramov–Henriques–Şega Thm 2.5(4); Ψ_A ≅ O/ϖ^{Σd_i} is asserted with 'We omit details' and proved again in Theorem 9.5. See sourceIssues E2, E3.

items.name: The comparison map Ψ_ϕ(M): Ψ_B(M) → Ψ_A(M) for a surjection ϕ: A → B
items.statement: Let ϕ: A → B be a surjective map in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated B-module. The natural transformation Ext^i_B(O, −) → Ext^i_A(O, −) induces F^i_ϕ(M): F^i_B(M) → F^i_A(M); since p_A M = p_B M, naturality gives the commutative square (7.2), and for i = c the induced map on cokernels of the vertical maps is Ψ_ϕ(M): Ψ_B(M) → Ψ_A(M) (7.3).
items.note: Missing. The underlying map Ext^i_B(O,−) → Ext^i_A(O,−) comes from Mathlib: apply CategoryTheory.Functor.mapExtLinearMap to ModuleCat.restrictScalars ϕ, whose exactness instances are in ChangeOfRingsExact.lean. The torsion-free quotient F^i = Ext^i(O,−)^tf, the congruence module Ψ_A(M), the square (7.2) and the induced map Ψ_ϕ(M) on cokernels (7.3) are absent from both libraries and from the atlas.

items.name: Theorem 7.4 (Theorem E): invariance of domain for congruence modules
items.statement: Let ϕ: A → B be a surjective map of local rings in C_O(c). For any finitely generated B-module M with depth_B M ≥ c, the map Ψ_ϕ(M): Ψ_B(M) → Ψ_A(M) of (7.3) is bijective (Theorem E: Ψ_A(M) ≅ Ψ_B(M)), and hence length_O Ψ_A(M) = length_O Ψ_B(M). (The proof shows that both horizontal maps of (7.2) are bijective for i = c.) Consequently, with r := rank_{A_{p_A}}(M_{p_A}) = rank_{B_{p_B}}(M_{p_B}) (ϕ_{p_A}: A_{p_A} → B_{p_B} is an isomorphism), δ_A(M) − δ_B(M) = r·(length_O Φ_A − length_O Φ_B) ≥ 0. So δ_A(M) ≥ δ_B(M), and when r ≠ 0 equality holds iff length_O Φ_A = length_O Φ_B. (Corrected: the printed 'with equality if and only if length_O Φ_A = length_O Φ_B' fails when r = 0 — sourceIssues E4. Case c = 0: Brochard–Iyengar–Khare [12, Lemma 3.4].)
items.note: Missing. The item uses the corrected statement (sourceIssues E4): the equality 'iff length Φ_A = length Φ_B' needs M_{p_B} ≠ 0. The proof needs depth, Ext vanishing against m-power-torsion complexes (Rees in Mathlib covers only the module case), the isomorphism of regular local rings A_{p_A} ≅ B_{p_B}, and Proposition 6.10 (C3). None of these is in the libraries as a congruence-module statement. For c = 0 this is Brochard–Iyengar–Khare [12, Lemma 3.4]. See sourceIssues E4.

items.name: Lemma 7.5: passing to the image of A in End_A(M)
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module supported at p_A with grade(p_A, M) ≥ c; let A′ be the image of A → End_A(M). (1) A′ is in C_O(c) and A → A′ is an isomorphism at p_A; (2) Ass_A A′ ⊆ Ass_A M; (3) if f ∈ A is a non-zero-divisor on M, it is a non-zero-divisor on A′; (4) length_O Ψ_A(M) = length_O Ψ_{A′}(M) and length_O Φ_A ≥ length_O Φ_{A′}; hence δ_A(M) ≥ δ_{A′}(M), with equality iff Φ_A ≅ Φ_{A′}.
items.note: Missing. Part (3) follows from (2) by Mathlib's biUnion_associatedPrimes_eq_zero_divisors. Part (2), Ass A' ⊆ Ass M, can be composed from subset_of_injective and prod through A' ↪ End_A(M) ↪ M^n, although the paper cites Bruns–Herzog Ex. 1.2.27. Parts (1) and (4) need C_O(c), freeness of M at p_A (Lemma 3.1) and Theorem 7.4, all absent.

items.name: Theorem 8.2 (Theorem C): the Wiles defect is invariant under deformation
items.statement: Setting 8.1: fix A in C_O(c) for some c ≥ 1, and a finitely generated A-module M supported at p_A with grade(p_A, M) = c (the maximum possible, by Lemma 3.1). Let f ∈ p_A ∖ p_A^(2) be a non-zero-divisor on M, and set B := A/fA and N := M/fM, viewed as a B-module. Theorem 8.2: B is in C_O(c − 1) and δ_A(M) = δ_B(N). Moreover N is supported at p_B and grade(p_B, N) = grade(p_A, M) − 1. [Introduction, Theorem C (p. 5): let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module with depth_A M ≥ c + 1; let f ∈ p_A ∖ p_A^(2) be a non-zero-divisor on M. Then B := A/fA is in C_O(c − 1) and δ_A(M) = δ_B(M/fM). Theorem C has no support hypothesis. When M_{p_A} ≠ 0 it is the case grade(p_A, M) = c of Theorem 8.2 (Lemma 3.2(1)). When M_{p_A} = 0 both defects vanish, a case Theorem 8.2 does not cover (sourceIssues E24).]
items.note: Missing. This is the central result of §8 (Theorem C). It needs C_O(c), p^(2), grade, δ_A, Lemmas 3.4, 3.7, 7.5, 8.7 and 8.8, Theorem 7.4, and Theorem 6.8 (F*_A(O) is an exterior algebra). The proof's 'depth_A(p_A, M) = c' should read grade(p_A, M) = c (sourceIssues E9, a misprint). Misprints in the proof: sourceIssues E9, E26.

items.name: Corollary 8.3: non-negativity of the Wiles defect
items.statement: Let A be a local ring in C_O(c). If M is a finitely generated A-module with grade(p_A, M) ≥ c, then δ_A(M) ≥ 0.
items.note: Missing. The proof applies Theorem 8.2 along the regular sequence of Lemma 3.5 to reach c = 0, then uses Lemma 3.7 and Wiles's inequality (item wiles-inequality). All the ingredients are missing. The case M_{p_A} = 0 is not covered by the printed proof (sourceIssues E24).

items.name: Wiles's inequality in codimension zero: length Φ_A ≥ length Ψ_A
items.statement: For A in C_O(0), length_O Φ_A ≥ length_O Ψ_A (Φ_A = p_A/p_A², Ψ_A = O/λ_A(A[p_A])); i.e. δ_A(A) ≥ 0. (Wiles [56, Appendix, Proposition 1]; DDT [22, (5.2.3)].)
items.note: Missing. This is the classical codimension-zero inequality (Wiles 1995, Appendix, Prop. 1; DDT (5.2.3)), stated for A in C_O(0) with Φ_A = p_A/p_A² and Ψ_A = O/λ_A(A[p_A]). It is the base case of Corollary 8.3 and an ingredient of the codimension-zero criterion fkr-a1. Wiles [56], DDT [22] and Lenstra [41] are prerequisites the atlas does not cover.

items.name: 8.4: agreement with the Böckle–Khare–Manning Wiles defect
items.statement: 8.4 (remark): Theorem 8.2 reconciles the Wiles defect δ_A(A) of this paper with the one introduced by Böckle–Khare–Manning [8] (printed '[7]'; sourceIssues E30) when M = A is a Cohen–Macaulay ring. Both invariants remain unchanged on going modulo a suitable regular sequence: δ_A by Theorem 8.2, and the invariant of [8] essentially by definition, [8, §3.4] (printed '[7, §3.4]'). So it suffices to compare them when c = 0, where they are defined in the same way. (The invariant of [8] is defined only for O-flat Cohen–Macaulay A, [8, Def. 3.23]. The paper does not state the flatness.)
items.note: Missing. The comparison: for Cohen–Macaulay A in C_O(c), δ_A(A) equals BKM's Wiles defect [7, §3.4]. Both are unchanged on passing modulo a suitable regular sequence (by Theorem 8.2, respectively by BKM's definition), and they agree at c = 0. Formalising it needs BKM's definition, so [7] should be listed as a prerequisite. See sourceIssues E30.

items.name: The order ideal O(f) and ν_A(f)
items.statement: Let A be a local ring in C_O, with the natural pairing ⟨−,−⟩: Hom_O(p_A/p_A², O) × (p_A/p_A²)^tf → O. For f ∈ p_A let [f] be its residue class in (p_A/p_A²)^tf. The order ideal O(f) ⊆ O of [f] is the image of the induced map ⟨−, [f]⟩: Hom_O(p_A/p_A², O) → O, i.e. the set of elements α(f) as α ranges over O-linear maps p_A/p_A² → O. Set ν_A(f) := length_O(O/O(f)). (Corrected: the paper prints the domain of ⟨−,[f]⟩ as (p_A/p_A²)^tf — sourceIssues E25.)
items.note: Missing (a definition). It is expressible in Mathlib as the range of evaluation at [f] on Module.Dual O (p_A/p_A²), with ν_A(f) = Module.length of O/O(f). Neither the definition nor any API exists. See sourceIssues E25.

items.name: Lemma 8.7: change of Φ under cutting by f
items.statement: Setting 8.1: A in C_O(c) with c ≥ 1; M a finitely generated A-module supported at p_A with grade(p_A, M) = c; f ∈ p_A ∖ p_A^(2) a non-zero-divisor on M; B := A/fA. The maps A → B → O give an exact sequence of O-modules 0 → O → p_A/p_A² → p_B/p_B² → 0, where 1 ↦ the class of f. The left map is one-to-one because it is so after localizing at p_A, using f ∉ p_A^(2). Applying Hom_O(−, O) gives the exact sequence (8.6) 0 → Hom_B(p_B/p_B², O) → Hom_A(p_A/p_A², O) →ð¹ O, with ð¹ evaluation on the class of f. Its image is O(f), so length Coker(ð¹) = ν_A(f). Lemma 8.7: in the set-up of 8.1, B is in C_O(c − 1) and length_O Φ_B − length_O Φ_A = ν_A(f). (The proof uses only c ≥ 1 and f ∈ p_A ∖ p_A^(2).)
items.note: Missing, with partial library support. For B = A/fA with f ∈ p_A, the two Mathlib lemmas give exactness of O·[f] → p_A/p_A² → p_B/p_B² → 0 at the middle and right. Injectivity of O → p_A/p_A² (from f ∉ p_A^(2)), B ∈ C_O(c−1) (Lemma 3.4), the dual sequence (8.6), length Ext^1_O(p/p², O) = length Φ, and the identity length Φ_B − length Φ_A = ν_A(f) are absent.

items.name: Lemma 8.8: order ideals are unchanged by surjections that are isomorphisms at p
items.statement: With A and f as in 8.1, let π: A → A′ be a surjective map in C_O(c) that is an isomorphism at p_A. Then π(f) ∈ p_{A′} ∖ p_{A′}^(2) and ν_{A′}(π(f)) = ν_A(f).
items.note: Missing. It needs p^(2), the isomorphism (p_A/p_A²)^tf ≅ (p_{A'}/p_{A'}²)^tf for surjections that are isomorphisms at p_A ((5.9), a C3 item), and the order ideal ν. None of these exists.

items.name: The codimension-zero complete intersection criterion (Wiles–Lenstra, extended by Fakhruddin–Khare–Ramakrishna)
items.statement: For A in C_O(0) with depth A ≥ 1, A is a complete intersection iff length_O Φ_A = length_O Ψ_A (Wiles [56, Appendix, Proposition], Lenstra [41], as extended in Fakhruddin–Khare–Ramakrishna [26, Proposition A.1]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.5, p. 40 (citing [26, Prop. A.1])
items.note: Missing. This is the codimension-zero criterion: for A in C_O(0) with depth A ≥ 1, A is a complete intersection iff length Φ_A = length Ψ_A (Wiles 1995 Appendix; Lenstra 1995; Fakhruddin–Khare–Ramakrishna, JLMS 103 (2021), Prop. A.1). It needs a complete-intersection predicate, which is absent, and the Wiles inequality. Wiles [56], Lenstra [41] and FKR [26] are prerequisites the atlas does not cover.

items.name: Theorem 9.5: complete intersections are characterized by vanishing defect
items.statement: Let A be a local ring in C_O(c) with depth A ≥ c + 1. Then A is a complete intersection if and only if δ_A(A) = 0.
items.note: Missing. Theorem 9.5: for A in C_O(c) with depth A ≥ c + 1, A is a complete intersection iff δ_A(A) = 0. The proof reduces to c = 0 as in Corollary 8.3 and then invokes fkr-a1. It needs δ_A, Theorem 8.2, Lemma 3.5 and the complete-intersection predicate, all absent.

items.name: Theorem 9.6 (Theorem A): the higher-codimension Wiles–Lenstra–Diamond numerical criterion
items.statement: Let A be a local ring in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module with depth_A M ≥ c + 1 and µ := rank_{A_{p_A}}(M_{p_A}) ≠ 0. Then δ_A(M) = 0 if and only if A is a complete intersection and M ≅ A^µ ⊕ W with W_{p_A} = 0. When this holds and e_A(M) ≤ µ · e(A), M is free. (Extends Diamond [23, Theorem 2.4].)
items.note: Missing. This is Theorem A, the higher-codimension Wiles–Lenstra–Diamond criterion, extending Diamond [23, Thm 2.4]. It needs Theorem 9.5, Theorem 8.2, Lemma 7.5, Corollary 8.3, Lemma 5.10 (C3), and Lemma 9.3, Theorem 9.2 and the multiplicity e_A (C2). None exists in the libraries.

items.name: Corollary 9.7: numerical isomorphism criterion onto a complete intersection
items.statement: Let ϕ: A → B be a surjective map in C_O(c) with B a complete intersection. If δ_A(B) = 0, then ϕ is bijective and A is a complete intersection. (c = 0: Lenstra [41], DDT [22, Thm 5.8].)
items.note: Missing. Corollary 9.7: for a surjection ϕ: A → B in C_O(c) with B a complete intersection, δ_A(B) = 0 implies ϕ is bijective and A is a complete intersection. The case c = 0 is Lenstra [41] and DDT Thm 5.8, the classical ring-theoretic R = T criterion. The proof uses Theorems 9.5 and 7.4 and Lemma 5.10.

items.name: Theorem J: the Wiles defect of a patched quotient depends only on the patched data
items.statement: Let R∞ be a complete local noetherian O-algebra and λ: R∞ → O surjective with kernel p such that (R∞)_p is regular of dimension c. Let M∞ be an R∞-module with depth_{R∞} M∞ ≥ c + 1 and (M∞)_p ≠ 0. Let (y, ϖ) be an M∞-regular sequence with y = y_1, …, y_c ⊆ p; set R_y = R∞/(y), M_y = M∞/(y), p_y = p/(y) (so M_y is O-flat). If p_y/p_y² has finite length, then δ_{R_y}(M_y) depends only on R∞, M∞ and λ, not on y. (For M∞ = R∞ Cohen–Macaulay this is Böckle–Khare–Manning [8, Theorem 3.25].)
items.locator: Theorem J, Introduction p. 9 ('an easy corollary of Theorem C')
items.note: Missing. The paper calls Theorem J 'an easy corollary of Theorem C'. Finite length of p_y/p_y² means R_y ∈ C_O(0), so each y_i avoids the symbolic square at its step (Lemma 3.4), and repeated Theorem 8.2 gives δ_{R_y}(M_y) = δ_{R∞}(M∞). The statement is pure commutative algebra (depth and regularity at p) and does not need the patching construction. For M∞ = R∞ Cohen–Macaulay it is Böckle–Khare–Manning [8, Thm 3.25]. See sourceIssues E22 on the comparison with [8].

items.name: The auxiliary rings Λ_n = O[[y]]/I_n and the rings R_n
items.statement: Assume the residue field k of O is finite of characteristic ℓ. Fix O[[y]], y = y_1, …, y_r. For n ≥ 1 fix integers e(i,n) ≥ n and Λ_n := O[[y]]/I_n with I_n := ((1 + y_i)^{ℓ^{e(i,n)}} − 1 | 1 ≤ i ≤ r); these are flat O-algebras, augmented to Λ_0 = O, and complete intersections. For each n a Λ_n-algebra R_n, finite as a Λ_n-module, with R_n/(y)R_n = O ⊗_{Λ_n} R_n ≅ R_0; ϕ_n: Λ_n → R_n the structure maps.
items.note: P8 plans exactly these patching data: finite-level rings R_N over group rings O[Δ_N] of bounded rank and unbounded ℓ-power exponent, with their augmentations and residual rings. Here Λ_n = O[[y]]/((1+y_i)^{ℓ^{e(i,n)}} − 1) ≅ O[∏_i Z/ℓ^{e(i,n)}], and the claim that Λ_n is a complete intersection falls under R03.3's complete-intersection criteria. The libraries have only ingredients (MvPowerSeries, Noetherian in finitely many variables; group algebras; Module.Flat). They have no complete-intersection predicate and no presentation of O[Δ] as a quotient of a power-series ring.

items.name: Derived actions: the category D_R(Λ) of Λ-complexes with a derived R-action
items.statement: For a ring Λ, a Λ-complex M and a Λ-algebra R, M is a derived R-complex if there is a map of Λ-algebras ι: R → End_{D(Λ)}(M). D_R(Λ) is the category of pairs (M, ι) with morphisms the maps f: M → N in D(Λ) commuting with each r ∈ R. RHom_Λ(M, C) and RHom_Λ(C, M) inherit derived R-actions, and for Λ → Λ′, Λ′ ⊗^L_Λ M is a derived (R ⊗_Λ Λ′)-complex, giving a functor D_R(Λ) → D_{R′}(Λ′).
items.note: The notion is planned in three places. P9 has a finite S-algebra T 'acting through End in the bounded derived category' and localizes 'this derived action'. IHG.2 compares chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions of Hecke algebras on perfect complexes. P7 supplies the duals and derived tensor products along which 10.2 transports actions. It is not library: the datum R → End_{D(Λ)}(M) can be written with Mathlib's DerivedCategory (Λ-linear) and its Λ-algebra End X, but there is no RHom or derived tensor on D(Λ) and no category D_R(Λ); AUDIT-17 records derived actions in D(S) as absent. P9 restricts to finite T, while the paper allows any Λ-algebra R. Possible misprint on p. 42: 'Λ′ ⊗^L_Λ M in D(Λ)' should read D(Λ′). See sourceIssues E33.

items.name: Patching systems and the category PaSy
items.statement: Fix integers d and ℓ_0. A patching system is C = (C_n, α_n)_{n≥0} with (1) C_n a perfect Λ_n-complex; (2) H_i(k ⊗^L_{Λ_n} C_n) = 0 for i ∉ [d, d + ℓ_0]; (3) C_n a derived R_n-complex; (4) α_n: O ⊗^L_{Λ_n} C_n → C_0 an isomorphism in D_{R_n}(O) (R_n acting on C_0 through R_n → R_0). Morphisms are families f_n: C_n → D_n in D_{R_n}(Λ_n) compatible with the α_n.
items.note: P8 plans this input. Its ACC+ §6.4 node takes perfect complexes C_N in D(Λ[Δ_N]) with isomorphisms C_N ⊗^L Λ ≅ C_0 compatible with ring and Hecke data. The category PaSy, whose morphisms are compatible f_n in D_{R_n}(Λ_n), is P8's 'comparisons ... when actual compatible comparison data are supplied'. P7 owns perfectness and the Tor-amplitude window of condition (2). Neither library has anything here: AUDIT-17 finds no perfect complexes and no patching data.

items.name: Framing: extension of scalars to S∞ = O[[y, w]]
items.statement: S∞ := O[[y, w]] with w = w_1, …, w_j and n := (y, w). The framing functor (−)^□ sends a finitely generated O[[y]]-module M to M^□ := S∞ ⊗_{O[[y]]} M; since O[[y]] → S∞ is flat it extends to derived categories, derived complexes and patching systems over (Λ_n^□).
items.note: P8 plans the framings and keeps framing variables explicit, and its node takes 'T a power series ring over Λ (framings)'. Carrying flat base change to derived categories and derived complexes is P7's derived coefficient change. The libraries have ingredients only: MvPowerSeries is Noetherian and AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian makes adic completions of Noetherian rings flat, from which flatness of O[[y]] → O[[y,w]] can be derived. There is no framing functor and no derived base-change functor.

items.name: Ultraproducts of finite modules (Scholze's ultrapatching)
items.statement: Fix a non-principal ultrafilter F on N. For a finite local ring A, the map f: ∏_n A → A sending a sequence to the value taken on an F-large set is an A-algebra map; p := f^{-1}(m_A) is a maximal ideal and (∏ A)_p ≅ A. For A-modules (or algebras) M_n, (∏ M_n)_p is the ultraproduct; if the M_n are finite of uniformly bounded cardinality, (∏ M_n)_p ≅ M_i for an F-large (in particular infinite) set of i. (Scholze [48, §9]; Allen et al. [1, §6.4].)
items.note: P8 plans ultrapatching with a fixed non-principal ultrafilter. Its node defines C(J, ∞) = (∏_N S_∞/J)_{x_F} ⊗ ∏ C(J, N), the same localization of a product at the ultrafilter point. The ultraproduct-localization lemma that node relies on (GN22 Lemma 2.2.2) is a recorded gap, and the paper's own proof on p. 44 can fill it. The libraries have near misses only: Filter.hyperfilter, Filter.Product (no algebraic structure), ring and module structures on Filter.Germ (ultrapowers of a single ring or module) and Łoś's theorem. Neither (∏A)_p ≅ A for a finite local A nor the isomorphism with M_i on an F-large set for finite modules of bounded cardinality is stated.

items.name: Theorem 10.6: the ultrapatching functor P: PaSy → mod R∞
items.statement: Let r, ℓ_0 and j be the integers of 10.1, 10.3 and 10.4, and let PaSy be the category of patching systems over (Λ_n) (for fixed d, ℓ_0). Let R∞ be a complete local, flat, noetherian O-algebra of dimension r + j − ℓ_0 + 1 (so ℓ_0 = dim S∞ − dim R∞), equipped with surjective O-algebra morphisms π_n: R∞ ↠ R_n^□ for n ≥ 1, not assumed compatible. Then there is a homomorphism ϕ∞: S∞ → R∞ making R∞ a finite S∞-algebra, and a functor P: PaSy → mod R∞, such that: (1) P(C) is a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R∞-module, nonzero when C ≠ 0. (2) There is a surjection R∞/nR∞ ↠ R_0 and an isomorphism of R_0-modules P(C)/nP(C) ≅ H_d(C_0). (3) Treating P(C) as an S∞-module via ϕ∞: for any open ideal a ⊆ S∞ and for infinitely many n, there are isomorphisms (S∞/a) ⊗^L_{S∞} P(C)[d] ≅ (S∞/a) ⊗^L_{Λ_n^□} C_n^□ of derived R∞-complexes, where R∞ acts on C_n^□ via ι_n^□ π_n (ι_n: R_n → End_{D(Λ_n)}(C_n) is the derived action of 10.3(3)). (4) There is an isomorphism of R∞-algebras End_{D(S∞)}(P(C)) ≅ lim_a End_{D(S∞/a)}((S∞/a) ⊗^L_{S∞} P(C)). (5) Fix a map f: C → C in PaSy. If there is τ ∈ R∞ with π_n(τ) = f_n^□ as elements of End_{D(Λ_n^□)}(C_n^□) for all but finitely many n, then P(f) = τ in End_{R∞}(P(C)). (The proof shows that in (3) the set of good n lies in the ultrafilter F. The misprint 'proving (2)' at the end of the proof of (3) is E17.)
items.note: P8 plans this theorem, and its ACC+ §6.4 node covers parts (2)–(5); P9's codimension–amplitude lemma gives part (1). One step has no named layer: choosing ϕ∞ so that R∞ is finite over S∞, which adapts Böckle–Khare–Manning [8, Lemmas 3.6–3.7]; R03.4 is the nearest owner. The functoriality step the paper 'leave[s] to the reader' (homotopies are preserved) must be written out. The draft statement drops the framing: on p. 43, π_n: R∞ ↠ R_n^□, and parts (3) and (5) read ⊗^L_{Λ_n^□} C_n^□, ι_n^□ π_n and f_n^□ ∈ End_{D(Λ_n^□)}(C_n^□). Gaps in the proof: sourceIssues E34 (finiteness of R∞ over S∞), E35 (finiteness of R_n in 10.1), E17 (misprint).

items.name: Lemma 10.7: complexes of short amplitude with a derived action are maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules
items.statement: Let S be a Cohen–Macaulay local ring with residue field k and C in D^b(mod S) with a derived action of a noetherian local S-algebra R with dim R ≤ dim S and H_i(k ⊗^L_S C) = 0 for i ∉ [0, dim S − dim R]. Then C ≃ H_0(C) and the R-module H_0(C) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay. (Calegari–Geraghty [17, Lemma 6.2]; uses Christensen–Iyengar [19, Prop. 6] on the dimension of finite free complexes and the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula.)
items.note: P9 plans the Calegari–Geraghty balanced-dimension conclusions. Its node codimension-amplitude-lemma is CG Lemma 6.2, the lemma this one generalises, but over a regular local base; R03.3 plans Cohen–Macaulay modules and Auslander–Buchsbaum. The paper's version is more general: S is only Cohen–Macaulay, the amplitude is read from k ⊗^L C, and R acts only in D(S). Its proof uses Christensen–Iyengar's formula for the dimension of a finite free complex [19, Prop. 6], which no layer plans; the paper applies the lemma only with S = S∞ regular. The libraries have regular sequences, Rees's Ext criterion, projective dimension and regular local rings, but no depth, Cohen–Macaulay predicate, Auslander–Buchsbaum or perfect complexes.

items.name: Lemma 10.8: an endomorphism killed on H_0 and on H_0 of the dual is zero
items.statement: Let Λ be a noetherian local ring with residue field k and C in D^b(mod Λ) with H_i(k ⊗^L_Λ C) = 0 for i ≠ 0, 1 and projdim_Λ H_0(C) ≤ 1; set C† := RHom_Λ(C, Λ)[1]. If ϕ ∈ End_{D(Λ)}(C) satisfies H_0(ϕ) = 0 = H_0(ϕ†), then ϕ = 0.
items.note: No layer plans this. IHG.2's nilpotence bound, for derived endomorphisms acting trivially on all cohomology, is a different statement: here H_1(ϕ) need not vanish, and the second hypothesis is on H_0(ϕ†). P7 plans only the minimal representatives and duals the proof uses. The libraries have ingredients only: Tau Ceti's two-term minimal projective presentations and Mathlib's homotopy API. The paper uses the lemma in Proposition 14.2, which shows that the derived Hecke algebra acts faithfully on H_0. See sourceIssues E36.
