items.name: 11.1: three properties of dualizing complexes
items.statement: (1) If A is Gorenstein, M ∈ D^b(mod A) and F → M a free resolution, then ω_A(M) ≅ Hom_A(F, A)[dim A]; so ω_A(M) is perfect when M is. (2) If A → B is finite, ω_A(M) ≅ ω_B(M) for M ∈ D^b(mod B) (RHom_A(B, ω_A) ≅ ω_B, Stacks [51, Tag 0AX1]). (3) If A → B is flat with A, B Gorenstein and M ∈ D^b(mod A), then ω_A(M) ⊗_A B ≅ ω_B(B ⊗_A M)[dim A − dim B].
items.note: No layer plans dualizing complexes of local rings. P7 plans duals of perfect complexes and R03.3 plans Cohen–Macaulay modules, while FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.1 only inventories 'dualizing modules'. The other matches are geometric: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves, tauceti StableReduction Layer 2 and the draft AnalyticStacks:AS.1. Neither library has Gorenstein rings or dualizing complexes (the only 'Gorenstein' in either Lean tree is the group theorist D. Gorenstein). Mathlib's IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight, flat base change of Hom between finite free modules, is the termwise input for (3).

items.name: The dual patching system C†
items.statement: Let C = (C_n, α_n)_{n≥0} be a patching system over (Λ_n). Its dual is the patching system C† := (C_n†, α_n†)_{n≥0}, where C_n† := RHom_O(C_n, O)[2d + ℓ_0] = ω_O(C_n)[2d + ℓ_0 − 1]. Since Λ_n is Gorenstein of dimension 1, C_n† = ω_{Λ_n}(C_n)[2d + ℓ_0 − 1] ≅ RHom_{Λ_n}(C_n, Λ_n)[2d + ℓ_0]. So C_n† is a perfect Λ_n-complex, the shift makes H_i(k ⊗^L_{Λ_n} C_n†) vanish for i ∉ [d, d + ℓ_0], and C_n† inherits a derived R_n-action; thus 10.3(1)–(3) hold. Applying ω_O(−) to α_n gives an isomorphism ω_O(α_n): ω_O(C_0) ≅ O ⊗^L_{Λ_n} ω_{Λ_n}(C_n), compatible with the derived R_n-actions. α_n†: O ⊗^L_{Λ_n} C_n† ≅ C_0† is the suspension of its inverse by 2d + ℓ_0 − 1. (The paper prints '(2d + ℓ_0) suspension'; that shift is right only if one dualizes with RHom_O(−, O) instead of ω_O(−).) (−)† is a contravariant functor on PaSy, and biduality (−) ≅ ω²_{Λ_n}(−) gives a natural isomorphism C ≅ (C†)† in PaSy.
items.note: No layer plans duality of patching systems. P8 plans the patching construction and its compatibilities (augmentation, framings, Hecke actions) but no dual system, and P7's duals are duals of single perfect complexes. The construction needs the dualizing-complex facts of 11.1, which are missing, and the transport of derived actions through RHom from 10.2. Neither library has anything here. See sourceIssues E37 (the suspension of α_n^†).

items.name: Theorem 11.3: patching commutes with duality
items.statement: For C in PaSy there is a natural isomorphism of R∞-modules P(C†) ≅ P(C)^∨ (the Cohen–Macaulay dual (4.3) of the maximal Cohen–Macaulay R∞-module P(C)); for a morphism f: C → D in PaSy, P(f†) = P(f)^∨. (Extends Manning [44, Proposition 4.10].)
items.note: No layer plans this. None of the patching layers (P8, R03.5, R03.6, GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3, PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.4) mentions duality or self-duality of patched modules, and the Cohen–Macaulay dual (4.3) is itself unplanned (cluster C2). The theorem extends Manning [44, Proposition 4.10], the ℓ0 = 0 case. Its proof uses 11.1, Theorem 10.6(3) and derived limits of bounded finite free complexes (Stacks Section 06XY). Neither library has anything here. Gaps in the proof: sourceIssues E38, E39.

items.name: Remark 11.4: multiplicity 2^k for quaternionic manifolds over CM fields (conditional)
items.statement: (Remark, stated without proof and conditional.) Let F be a CM field in which ℓ does not ramify, and D a quaternion algebra over F. Let Y_K be the manifold attached to a compact open K ⊆ D^×(A_F^∞), analogous to §13. Assume appropriate analogues of Conjectures A, B and C. Let m be a non-Eisenstein ideal of the Hecke algebra of Y_K, corresponding to ρ̄_m: G_F → GL_2(k) satisfying certain 'Taylor–Wiles conditions'. As in §§13 and 15, the m-localized chain complexes of the Y_K give a patching system C, and P gives a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module M∞ over a ring R∞. By Theorem 10.6(2), M∞/𝔪_{R∞}M∞ ≅ H_d(Y_K, O)_m/𝔪_{R_0}H_d(Y_K, O)_m, where d is the lowest degree with H_*(Y_K, O)_m ≠ 0. R∞ is the same ring as in [44], since it is determined by local information at finite places. An analogue of Proposition 13.7 gives C† ≅ C, so Theorem 11.3 gives M∞^∨ ≅ M∞. Suppose H_1(Y_K, E)_m ≠ 0 (printed H_1; H_d is meant unless F is imaginary quadratic). Then multiplicity one gives M∞ generic rank 1. So [44, Theorem 3.1] gives dim_k M∞/𝔪_{R∞}M∞ = 2^k, hence dim_k H_1(Y_K, O)_m/𝔪_{R_0} = 2^k (again H_d), where k is the integer of [44, Theorem 1.1]; it depends only on the local behaviour of ρ̄_m at the places where D ramifies. Under the same assumption, [44, Theorem 3.1] also gives that τ_{M∞}: M∞ ⊗_{R∞} M∞ → ω_{R∞}, induced by the self-duality of M∞, is surjective. For ℓ_0 = 0 this yields a statement about the congruence module ([44, Theorem 1.2], [7, Theorem 3.2]); the paper says this argument does not generalize to ℓ_0 > 0. The observation is credited also to F. Calegari.
items.note: This is a conditional remark (analogues of Conjectures A, B and C are assumed) with a sketched proof. Nothing in the atlas plans multiplicity statements for ρ̄_m in the homology of quaternionic arithmetic manifolds. Its algebraic core, Manning [44, Theorem 3.1] (a self-dual maximal Cohen–Macaulay module of generic rank 1 over R∞ has dim M/m = 2^k), is not in the atlas. Y_K and its chain complexes would come from ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.1, and the self-duality C† ≅ C from ALS.5:finite-level-duality. See sourceIssues E40.

items.name: Global setting: ℓ > 2, ρ̄: G_F → GL_2(k) with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} absolutely irreducible, ψ, and the cases (PGL2) and (Wt1)
items.statement: Fix a prime ℓ > 2, a finite E/Q_ℓ with ring of integers O, uniformizer ϖ, residue field k; F a number field in which ℓ is unramified; a continuous ρ̄: G_F → GL_2(k) with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} absolutely irreducible and all eigenvalues of ρ̄(σ) in k; ψ: G_F → O^× lifting det ρ̄. Case (PGL2): F arbitrary, ψ = ε_ℓ (cyclotomic), ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} flat for v | ℓ. Case (Wt1): F = Q, ψ the Teichmüller lift of det ρ̄ (finite image), ρ̄ unramified at ℓ and odd.
items.note: The standing setup is planned across several layers. Continuous residual representations are in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1. Oddness and absolute irreducibility, including restriction to cyclotomic fields, are in R01.4. Fixed-determinant deformation data are in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1, and the finite-flat local condition at v|ℓ is in LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.4, built on FiniteFlatGroups R07.1. The libraries have only fragments: Mathlib's absolute Galois group and ℤ_p-valued cyclotomic character, and the Tau Ceti Teichmüller lift, which is what Case (Wt1) uses for ψ. There is no carrier for continuous GL_2(k)-valued Galois representations, and nothing on oddness, absolute irreducibility over F(ζ_ℓ) or flatness.

items.name: Local framed deformation rings R_v^□, R_v^fl, R_v^ur and R_v^min
items.statement: Fix a prime v of F and let ρ̄_v := ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}: G_{F_v} → GL_2(k). Let q_v = Nm(v) = #(O_F/v), let I_{F_v} ⊴ G_{F_v} be the inertia subgroup and P_{F_v} ⊴ I_{F_v} the wild inertia subgroup. Let ϕ_v ∈ G_{F_v} be a lift of arithmetic Frobenius Frob_v and σ_v ∈ G_{F_v} a lift of a topological generator of I_{F_v}/P_{F_v}, so that ϕ_vσ_vϕ_v^{−1} = σ_v^{q_v} in G_{F_v}/P_{F_v}. R_v^□ is the unrestricted framed deformation ring parametrizing lifts of ρ̄_v with determinant ψ|_{G_{F_v}}; ρ_v^□: G_{F_v} → GL_2(R_v^□) is the universal lift. (a) v | ℓ: if ρ̄_v is flat, and so is ψ|_{G_{F_v}} (as when ψ = ε_ℓ), then R_v^fl is the quotient of R_v^□ parametrizing flat deformations of ρ̄_v with determinant ε_ℓ. Since ℓ does not ramify in F, R_v^fl ≅ O[[x_1, …, x_{3+[F_v:Q_ℓ]}]] ([20, §2.4.1]). If ρ̄_v and ψ|_{G_{F_v}} are unramified at v, then R_v^ur is the quotient of R_v^□ parametrizing unramified lifts of ρ̄_v with determinant ψ|_{G_{F_v}}, and R_v^ur ≅ O[[x_1, x_2, x_3]]. This is stated in the v | ℓ paragraph and is used at ℓ in Case (Wt1). (b) v ∤ ℓ: R_v^□ is a reduced complete intersection, flat over O of relative dimension 3 ([50, Thm 2.5]). Because Ker(GL_2(R_v^□) → GL_2(k)) is pro-ℓ, the map ρ_v^□(P_{F_v}) → ρ̄_v(P_{F_v}) is an isomorphism, so ρ_v^□ is tamely ramified whenever ρ̄_v is. R_v^min is the quotient of R_v^□ parametrizing minimally ramified lifts of ρ̄_v ([20, Def. 2.4.14]), and R_v^min ≅ O[[x_1, x_2, x_3]] ([20, Lemma 2.4.19]).
items.note: Three layers plan these rings. R08.1 covers the unrestricted framed ring R_v^□ with fixed determinant. R08.2 covers the unramified and minimally ramified quotients away from p, with their dimension and smoothness, so R_v^ur and R_v^min ≅ O[[x1,x2,x3]]. The flat ring at v|ℓ with ℓ unramified is L7's Fontaine–Laffaille condition in the unramified small-weight range, computed there with formal smoothness (CHT §2.4.1), with R08.4 for finite-flat components. One caveat: no layer explicitly states Shotton's theorem [50, Thm 2.5] that R_v^□ for v∤ℓ is a reduced complete intersection, O-flat of relative dimension 3. R08.2's 'dimensions ... and irreducible components' for fixed inertial types is the closest. LanglandsParameterStacks LP1 proves flatness and the lci property of Z^1(W_E/P, Ĝ), but not reducedness, the fixed-determinant fibre, or completion at ρ̄. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E43.

items.name: Steinberg and unipotent quotients R_v^{St(ε_v)} and R_v^{uni(ε_v)} at level-raising places
items.statement: Let v ∤ ℓ with ρ̄_v unramified, q_v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), and ρ̄_v(Frob_v) having eigenvalues of ratio q_v; fix √(q_v ψ(ϕ_v)^{−1}) ∈ O^× (= 1 in Case (PGL2)), so ρ̄(ϕ_v) ~ diag(ψ(ϕ_v) ε_v √(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1}), ε_v √(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1})^{−1}) with ε_v ∈ {±1} (unique if q_v ≢ ±1). R_v^{St(ε_v)} is the unique O-torsion-free reduced quotient of R_v^□ whose L-points of the generic fibre are the lifts conjugate to (ψχ_v, ∗; 0, χ_v^{−1}) with χ_v unramified, χ_v(ϕ_v) = ε_v √(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1}); if q_v ≢ ±1 exactly one ε_v gives a nonzero ring, if q_v ≡ −1 both do. R_v^{uni(ε_v)} is the reduced quotient with Spec R_v^{uni(ε_v)} = Spec R_v^{St(ε_v)} ∪ Spec R_v^min.
items.note: R08.2 plans the Steinberg deformation condition away from p, with monodromy. It also plans the existence of the intended quotient, and its handoff requires the flat/reduced closure defined by a characteristic-zero point criterion, which is exactly how R_v^{St(ε_v)} is defined. Since ρ̄_v is unramified, R_v^{uni(ε_v)} (Spec = Spec R^St ∪ Spec R^min) is the fixed-inertial-type quotient for unipotent inertia, which R08.2 also names. L7 gives the rank-n Steinberg and minimally ramified analogues. The unipotent union is not named verbatim, and nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E18.

items.name: Proposition 12.1: explicit level-raising local deformation rings
items.statement: Let v ∤ ℓ, and assume ρ̄_v is unramified and q_v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ). (i) If the ratio of the eigenvalues of ρ̄_v(ϕ_v) is not q_v^{±1}, then R_v^□ = R_v^min ≅ O[[x_1, x_2, x_3]]. (ii) Now assume the eigenvalues of ρ̄_v(ϕ_v) have ratio q_v. If q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ), let ε_v be the unique element of {1, −1} with R_v^{St(ε_v)} ≠ 0; if q_v ≡ −1 (mod ℓ), let ε_v be either 1 or −1. Then R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ≅ O[[A_v, B_v, X_v, Y_v]]/(A_vB_v). The corresponding universal representation sends σ_v ↦ U^{−1}(1 A_v; 0 1)U, where U := (1 X_v; Y_v 1), and ϕ_v ↦ U^{−1} diag(ψ(ϕ_v)ε_v√(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1})(1+B_v)^{−1}, ε_v√(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1})^{−1}(1+B_v)) U. Moreover R_v^min = R_v^{uni(ε_v)}/(A_v) = O[[B_v, X_v, Y_v]] and R_v^{St(ε_v)} = R_v^{uni(ε_v)}/(B_v) = O[[A_v, X_v, Y_v]]. (iii) If q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ), then R_v^{uni(ε_v)} = R_v^□. (Attributed to the computations of Shotton [49, §5]; the paper gives no further proof.)
items.note: R08.2 plans computing the dimensions, smoothness and irreducible components of the Steinberg and minimally ramified conditions, with each residual hypothesis visible. Proposition 12.1 is exactly that computation for an unramified ρ̄_v with q_v ≢ 1. It gives R^min ≅ R^St ≅ O[[3 variables]], and R^uni ≅ O[[A,B,X,Y]]/(AB) as the union of those two smooth components, equal to R^□ when q_v ≢ ±1. When the eigenvalue ratio is not q_v^{±1}, R^□ = R^min. The roadmap's required check, comparing unramified and Steinberg lifts of the same ρ̄, is this situation. The explicit universal lift (the matrices U, σ_v, ϕ_v) is a sharper output than the layer text names, and nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Remark 12.2: supply of level-raising primes
items.statement: Remark 12.2. In the main results (e.g. Theorem 15.1), (non-minimal) ramification of lifts of ρ̄ is allowed only at the places of Proposition 12.1 whose eigenvalue ratio is q_v. These are the 'level raising' primes: v ∤ ℓ, ρ̄_v unramified, q_v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), and ρ̄_v(Frob_v) has eigenvalue ratio q_v. The restriction is made mainly for simplicity. The authors expect, without proof, that one could also treat without much trouble (i) unrestricted ramification at places v with q_v ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), ρ̄ unramified at v and ρ̄(Frob_v) having distinct eigenvalues, and (ii) unipotent ramification at places v with q_v ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), ρ̄ unramified at v and ρ̄(Frob_v) of order divisible by ℓ. Unipotent ramification at places trivial for ρ̄ would need more work. As printed, the Remark also claims: (a) if ρ̄ is odd at a real place of F with complex conjugation c ∈ G_F, then any v with ρ̄(Frob_v) conjugate to ρ̄(c) is a level raising prime, with q_v ≡ −1 (mod ℓ); (b) if the projective image of ρ̄ is PSL_2(k) (|k| ≥ 5) and [F(ζ_ℓ):F] > 2, then there are places v with ρ̄(Frob_v) having eigenvalue ratio q_v and q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ), and these are again level raising primes. Correction (sourceIssues E41, E42): (a) holds when det ρ̄ = ε̄_ℓ (e.g. Case (PGL2)); in general one must add the hypothesis q_v ≡ −1 (mod ℓ), i.e. Frob_v conjugate to c in Gal(F(ρ̄, ζ_ℓ)/F). (b) holds when ℓ ≥ 7 or [k:F_ℓ] is even, with k the field over which the projective image is PSL_2(k). It fails for ℓ = 5 with [k:F_5] odd. The Remark gives no proofs and is not used in later proofs.
items.note: No layer plans existence of level-raising primes (v∤ℓ, ρ̄ unramified at v, q_v ≢ 1, eigenvalue ratio q_v) over a general number field. GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 chooses only Taylor–Wiles primes (q ≡ 1 mod p^n). The closest special case is KW I Lemma 8.2 in the ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.4 decomposition node: over Q, with p ≡ 1 mod 4, non-solvable image and q ≡ −1 mod p. The inputs are planned elsewhere: Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev, layers 10 and 14, not built) and the GL2/PGL2 image facts (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4). Possible source error: the first sentence is true when det ρ̄ = ε̄_ℓ (Case (PGL2)) but not for general ψ. For example, in Case (Wt1) take the level-23 weight-one S3 form with ℓ = 5 and v = 11, which is inert in Q(√−23) and ≡ 1 mod 5: then ρ̄(Frob_11) ~ ρ̄(c), but q_v ≡ 1. One needs Frob_v ~ c in Gal(F(ρ̄,ζ_ℓ)/F). See sourceIssues E41, E42.

items.name: Global deformation functors D_Σ^𝔇, D_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 and their framed versions
items.statement: Let A_O (resp. CNL_O) be the category of Artinian (resp. complete local noetherian) O-algebras with residue field k. D: A_O → Sets sends A to the set of equivalence classes of continuous ρ: G_F → GL_2(A) with det ρ = ψ and G_F → GL_2(A) ↠ GL_2(k) equal to ρ̄, where ρ′ ~ ρ if ρ′ = γργ^{−1} for some γ ∈ 1 + M_2(m_A). Let S be the set of finite places v of F at which ρ̄ or ψ is ramified, or with v | ℓ. At each v ∈ S with v ∤ ℓ, assume one of the following ('non-vexing', following [16]): q_v ≢ −1 (mod ℓ), or ρ̄|_{I_v} is irreducible, or ρ̄|_{D_v} is reducible. Fix three pairwise disjoint finite sets T, 𝔇, Q of finite places of F. For v ∈ T ∪ 𝔇: ρ̄_v is unramified, v ∤ ℓ, q_v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), and the ratio of the eigenvalues of ρ̄_v(Frob_v) is q_v. For v ∈ Q: ρ̄_v is unramified, q_v ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), and ρ̄_v(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues in k. For each v ∈ T ∪ 𝔇, fix ε_v ∈ {1, −1} with R_v^{St(ε_v)} ≠ 0; it is unique if q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ). Let Σ ⊆ T. In the applications, Σ is a set of level-raising primes and Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes; 𝔇 is the discriminant of a Shimura curve over Q in Case (Wt1), and 𝔇 = ∅ in Case (PGL2). Define subfunctors D_Σ^𝔇 ⊆ D_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 ⊆ D. A class ρ lies in D_Σ^𝔇(A) iff all of the following hold. In Case (PGL2), ρ is flat at every v | ℓ. In Case (Wt1), ρ is unramified at ℓ. For every place v ∤ ℓ at which ρ̄ is ramified, ρ is minimally ramified at v. ρ is unramified at every v ∉ S ∪ Σ ∪ 𝔇, including v ∈ T∖Σ. For v ∈ 𝔇, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} arises from R_v^{St(ε_v)}. For v ∈ Σ with q_v ≡ −1 (mod ℓ), ρ|_{G_{F_v}} arises from R_v^{uni(ε_v)}. D_{Σ,Q}^𝔇(A) is defined by the same conditions, except that ρ need only be unramified outside S ∪ Σ ∪ 𝔇 ∪ Q. Hence there is no restriction on ramification at primes of Σ (resp. Σ ∪ Q) with q_v ≢ −1 (mod ℓ). Framed versions: D_Σ^{𝔇,□}(A) (resp. D_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□}(A)) is the set of tuples (ρ, (β_v)_{v∈S∪T∪𝔇}), with ρ as in D_Σ^𝔇(A) (resp. D_{Σ,Q}^𝔇(A)) and each β_v ∈ 1 + M_2(m_A). Two tuples (ρ, (β_v)) and (ρ′, (β′_v)) are equivalent if some γ ∈ 1 + M_2(m_A) has ρ′ = γργ^{−1} and β′_v = γβ_v for all v ∈ S ∪ T ∪ 𝔇. One may view β_v as a basis of A² lifting the standard basis of k². Framings are included at every v ∈ S ∪ T ∪ 𝔇, including v ∈ T∖Σ, but not at v ∈ Q.
items.note: R04.1 plans determinant-fixed deformation functors on Artinian O-algebras up to 1+M_2(m_A)-conjugacy, with framed variants. R04.3 plans global problems with prescribed local conditions. The local conditions come from R08.2 (minimally ramified, unramified, Steinberg, fixed unipotent type) and the flat/unramified conditions at ℓ from L7/R08.4. The paper's specific data (non-vexing hypothesis, sets T, 𝔇, Q, framings at S∪T∪𝔇 including T∖Σ but not Q) are an instance, not new theory. Nothing is in the libraries: the Schlessinger/framed machinery is audited as absent.

items.name: Representability and the maps from local to global deformation rings
items.statement: The functors D_Σ^𝔇, D_Σ^{𝔇,□}, D_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 and D_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□} are pro-representable, stated as well known, by rings R_Σ^𝔇, R_Σ^{𝔇,□}, R_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 and R_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□} in CNL_O. The superscript 𝔇 is dropped when clear or empty, as in Case (PGL2). For Σ_1 ⊆ Σ_2 ⊆ T, the inclusions D_Σ^𝔇 ⊆ D_{Σ,Q}^𝔇, D_{Σ_1}^𝔇 ⊆ D_{Σ_2}^𝔇 and D_{Σ_1,Q}^𝔇 ⊆ D_{Σ_2,Q}^𝔇 give a commutative square of surjections: R_{Σ_2,Q}^𝔇 ↠ R_{Σ_2}^𝔇, R_{Σ_2,Q}^𝔇 ↠ R_{Σ_1,Q}^𝔇, R_{Σ_2}^𝔇 ↠ R_{Σ_1}^𝔇 and R_{Σ_1,Q}^𝔇 ↠ R_{Σ_1}^𝔇. The framed analogues give the same square for the □-rings. The forgetful map (ρ, (β_v)) ↦ ρ induces formally smooth maps R_Σ^𝔇 → R_Σ^{𝔇,□} and R_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 → R_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□}. Hence there are non-canonical isomorphisms R_Σ^{𝔇,□} ≅ R_Σ^𝔇[[w_1, …, w_j]] and R_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□} ≅ R_{Σ,Q}^𝔇[[w_1, …, w_j]] respecting these squares, with j = 4|S ∪ T ∪ 𝔇| − 1. The paper prints 4|S ∪ T| − 1 here; this is corrected per E11 and agrees with §15. For v ∈ S ∪ T ∪ 𝔇, the map (ρ, (β_v)) ↦ β_v^{−1}ρ|_{G_{F_v}}β_v induces R_v^□ → R_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□} → R_Σ^{𝔇,□} (the paper prints R_v^{𝔇,□}). These maps induce, in Case (PGL2), R_{loc,Σ} := ⊗̂_{v|ℓ} R_v^fl ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈S, v∤ℓ} R_v^min ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈Σ} R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈T∖Σ} R_v^min → R_{Σ,Q}^□. In Case (Wt1) they induce R_{loc,Σ}^𝔇 := ⊗̂_{v|ℓ} R_v^ur ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈S, v∤ℓ} R_v^min ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈Σ} R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈T∖Σ} R_v^min ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈𝔇} R_v^{St(ε_v)} → R_{Σ,Q}^{𝔇,□}. For Σ_1 ⊆ Σ_2 ⊆ T, the natural surjection R_{loc,Σ_2}^𝔇 ↠ R_{loc,Σ_1}^𝔇 is given by the quotient map R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ↠ R_v^{uni(ε_v)}/(A_v) = R_v^min at every v ∈ Σ_2∖Σ_1 and the identity on the other factors. (The paper adds the qualifier 'q_v ≢ −1 (mod ℓ)'; it is spurious: sourceIssues E45.) With this surjection, the diagram with rows R_{loc,Σ_i}^𝔇 → R_{Σ_i,Q}^{𝔇,□} ↠ R_{Σ_i}^{𝔇,□} (i = 2 over i = 1) and vertical surjections commutes. The paper calls this 'easy to see' and gives no proof.
items.note: Representability and the framed/unframed comparison by power-series variables are R04.2. The map from the completed tensor product of local rings R_loc to the framed global ring is R04.3, with the completed tensor product and Schlessinger in R03.1/R03.2 and the presentation over R_loc as a reviewed R03.2 node. Compatibility under enlarging Σ (R_loc,Σ2 ↠ R_loc,Σ1 via R^uni ↠ R^uni/(A_v) = R^min) is change of problem in R04.4. The paper's variable count 4|S∪T|−1 should read 4|S∪T∪𝔇|−1, as recorded in draft issue E11. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E11, E44, E45.

items.name: Proposition 12.3: Taylor–Wiles deformations and the O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure
items.statement: For v ∈ Q (q_v ≡ 1 mod ℓ, ρ̄_v unramified with distinct eigenvalues γ_{v,1}, γ_{v,2} ∈ k), ρ^univ_{Σ,Q}|_{G_{F_v}} ≅ χ_{1,v} ⊕ χ_{2,v} with χ_{i,v}(Frob_v) ≡ γ_{v,i}, and χ_{1,v}|_{I_{F_v}} induces Δ_v := k(v)^×(ℓ) → (R_{Σ,Q}^𝔇)^×. With Δ_Q := ∏_{v∈Q} Δ_v, R_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 is an O[Δ_Q]-algebra via ∏χ_{1,v}, R_{Σ,Q}^𝔇 ⊗_{O[Δ_Q]} O = R_Σ^𝔇, and R_{Σ_2,Q}^𝔇 ↠ R_{Σ_1,Q}^𝔇 is an O[Δ_Q]-algebra map.
items.note: R04.5 plans Taylor–Wiles primes with prescribed Frobenius eigenvalues. The GlobalGaloisDeformations handoff requires 'for one Taylor–Wiles prime' the selected eigenline, diamond group and local condition together. That is the splitting ρ^univ|G_{F_v} ≅ χ_{1,v} ⊕ χ_{2,v}, the map Δ_v = k(v)^×(ℓ) → R^× via χ_{1,v}|I_v, and the resulting O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure. R04.6 packages the local-to-global data for patching. Two points are only implicit in the layer text: the augmentation isomorphism R_{Σ,Q}/a_Q ≅ R_Σ, and O[Δ_Q]-linearity of R_{Σ2,Q} ↠ R_{Σ1,Q}. For consistency, PAPER-VENKATESH-19/43 (the general-G 'deformations at TW primes are toral') was marked missing; here the GL_2 case is explicitly in R04.5's handoff.

items.name: Arithmetic manifolds Y_K for PGL_2/F and their chain complexes C_K
items.statement: For compact open K = ∏_v K_v ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) and a maximal compact K_∞ ⊆ PGL_2(F ⊗ R), Y_K := PGL_2(F)\PGL_2(A_F)/K K_∞, an orbifold of dimension 2r_1 + 3r_2. K is sufficiently small if gKg^{−1} ∩ PGL_2(F) is torsion-free for all g. C_K is the complex of singular chains on Y_K with O-coefficients, a perfect complex in D(O) computing H_*(Y_K, O).
items.note: Y_K is the case G = PGL₂ of ALS's X_K = G(F)\(X∞ × G(A_f)/K). ALS.0 builds the symmetric space (here ℍ^{r₁} × ℍ₃^{r₂}, of dimension 2r₁+3r₂) and the arithmetic components, ALS.2 the Borel–Serre compactification that gives finite-CW type, and ALS.1 the chain complexes and their bounded finite projective models, which is the perfectness of C_K. ALS works with cochains and keeps orbifold/groupoid models at general level; the paper takes singular chains of the coarse quotient and uses them only at sufficiently small level. Mathlib has PGL(n,R) as an abstract quotient group, the adele rings and singular chains, but no adelic quotient, symmetric space or perfectness statement. If F has a real place, K∞ contains PO(2), so Y_K need not be orientable (see prop-13-6); ALS.0 keeps the orientation local system.

items.name: Lemma 13.1: sufficiently small level gives manifolds and Galois coverings
items.statement: Let K ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) be sufficiently small. (1) For all g, Γ_{K,g} := gKg^{−1} ∩ PGL_2(F) acts freely on PGL_2(F ⊗ R)/K_∞, and Y_K is a smooth manifold of dimension 2r_1 + 3r_2. (2) If V = ∏V_v is a normal open compact subgroup of K, Y_V → Y_K is a Galois covering with group K/V. (Khare–Thorne [38, Lemma 6.1].)
items.note: Part (1) is ALS.0's 'proper discontinuity and, at neat level, freeness' for G = PGL₂. Part (2) is AA.4's 'finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels'. For Γ ⊆ PGL₂(F), torsion-free already means neat (use the faithful adjoint representation: an element whose eigenvalue ratio is a nontrivial root of unity has finite order), so the paper's 'sufficiently small' matches the atlas hypothesis. Mathlib and Tau Ceti give covering maps for free, properly discontinuous actions on locally compact Hausdorff spaces (a near miss); proper discontinuity of Γ_{K,g} on PGL₂(F⊗R)/K∞ and the deck group K/V are absent.

items.name: Double coset operators [K_2 α K_1]: C_{K_1} → C_{K_2} and the convolution algebras H(K_2\G/K_1)
items.statement: G := PGL_2(A_F^∞). C_c(G) is the group of compactly supported continuous f: G → Z. For compact open K_1, K_2 ⊆ G, H(K_2\G/K_1) := {f ∈ C_c(G) : f(k_2xk_1) = f(x) for all x ∈ G, k_i ∈ K_i}. It is the free abelian group on the indicator functions [K_2αK_1] of the distinct double cosets K_2αK_1 (α ∈ G). The convolution ∗: H(K_3\G/K_2) × H(K_2\G/K_1) → H(K_3\G/K_1) is (g∗f)(x) := Σ_{K_2y ∈ K_2\G} g(xy^{−1})f(y). It is bilinear and associative, with [K_2]∗f = f = f∗[K_1] for f ∈ H(K_2\G/K_1), so H(K\G/K) is a ring. Moreover [K_3βK_2] ∗ [K_2αK_1] = Σ c_γ[K_3γK_1], summed over all double cosets K_3γK_1 ⊆ G (the displayed index is misprinted 'K_1γK_3'). Here c_γ := #{(i,j) : β_jα_iK_1 = γK_1} for finite coset decompositions K_2αK_1 = ⊔_i α_iK_1 and K_3βK_2 = ⊔_j β_jK_2. For α ∈ G let L := αK_1α^{−1} ∩ K_2 (compact open). Define p_1: Y_L → Y_{K_1}, [x]_L ↦ [xα]_{K_1} (well defined because α^{−1}Lα ⊆ K_1), and p_2: Y_L → Y_{K_2}, [x]_L ↦ [x]_{K_2}. Both are finite-to-one maps, and covering maps when the K_i are sufficiently small (Lemma 13.1). They induce p_{i,∗}: C_L → C_{K_i} and p_i^∗: C_{K_i} → C_L. The double coset operator is [K_2αK_1] := p_{2,∗} ∘ p_1^∗ ∈ Hom_{D(O)}(C_{K_1}, C_{K_2}).
items.note: SR.1 plans the convolution algebra of compactly supported, locally constant bi-invariant functions on a locally profinite group, H(K₂\G/K₁) ⊆ C_c(G,ℤ) with G = PGL₂(A_F^∞). ALS.3 plans the operator [K₂αK₁] = p_{2,*}∘p₁^* through L = αK₁α⁻¹ ∩ K₂, including change of level; Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stage 5 supplies the transfer p₁^* for finite covers. The abstract mixed-level algebra is already in the libraries in Shimura's formal-sum model. Mathlib defines HeckeCosetModule, and Tau Ceti defines the convolution HeckeCosetModule.mul, whose structure constants DoubleCoset.multiplicity are exactly the paper's c_γ = #{(i,j) : β_jα_iK₁ = γK₁}, with associativity and units. Still missing: the identification with bi-invariant functions in C_c(G,ℤ), the topological group PGL₂(A_F^∞) with its compact opens, and the operator on chain complexes. See sourceIssues E46.

items.name: Lemma 13.2: the Hecke action on chain complexes is multiplicative
items.statement: [K_2αK_1] ↦ [K_2αK_1] defines an additive homomorphism H(K_2\G/K_1) → Hom_{D(O)}(C_{K_1}, C_{K_2}) carrying convolution to composition; in particular H(K\G/K) → End_{D(O)}(C_K) is a ring homomorphism. (Newton–Thorne [45, Lemma 2.19], stated there for K_1 = K_2.)
items.note: ALS.3 plans that the double-coset operators compose according to the double-coset algebra in the derived category, including change of level. For mixed levels K₁, K₂, K₃ that is exactly Lemma 13.2; Newton–Thorne, Lemma 2.19 prove only K₁ = K₂ (the paper's footnote 2). Only the algebra side exists (Tau Ceti HeckeCosetModule.mul_assoc, mixed levels); neither library has a Hecke action on a chain complex.

items.name: Hecke operators T_v, U_v, ⟨d⟩_v and the Hecke algebra T^S(K) ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K)
items.statement: Let K = ∏_v K_v ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) be compact open and S a finite set of places with K_v a maximal compact subgroup of PGL_2(F_v) for every v ∉ S (S need not be minimal). For v ∉ S, T_v := [K diag(ϖ_v,1) K] ∈ End_{D(O)}(C_K). Suppose K_1(v) ⊆ K_v ⊆ K_0(v); such v lie in S, and the paper misprints 'v ∉ S' (sourceIssues E47). Let d ∈ K_0(v)/K_v, a quotient of K_0(v)/K_1(v) ≅ (O_F/v)^× (printed '↪ (O_F/v)^×'). Then U_v := [K diag(ϖ_v,1) K] and ⟨d⟩_v := [K diag(d̃,1) K] in End_{D(O)}(C_K), for any lift d̃ ∈ O_{F,v}^× of d. T^S(K) := O[T_v | v ∉ S] ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K) is a finite commutative O-algebra. Assuming Conjecture A (p. 61), a maximal ideal m ⊆ T^S(K) is non-Eisenstein if ρ̄_m is absolutely irreducible. For compact open K′ ⊆ K, m ⊆ T^S(K′) also denotes the preimage of m under the map T^S(K′) ↠ T^S(K).
items.note: T_v, U_v and ⟨d⟩_v are ALS.3 double-coset operators for g = diag(ϖ_v,1) and diag(d̃,1). IHG.3 fixes T_v as the n = 2 case of T_{v,1}, with Hecke polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v) once T_{v,2} = 1 in PGL₂. T^S(K) ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K) is IHG.2's 'finite image algebra' of a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex; it is finite because End of a perfect O-complex is, and commutative because operators at distinct places commute. 'Non-Eisenstein' is defined through ρ̄_m from Conjecture A, whose statement is missing (conj-A). Tau Ceti's commutative GL_n and GL₂ Hecke rings are classical Hecke rings over ℚ, a near miss. See sourceIssues E47.

items.name: Conjecture A: Galois representations for Hecke eigenclasses in the (torsion) homology of Y_K
items.statement: (Assumed.) Let K = ∏_v K_v ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) be compact open and S a finite set of places with K_v maximal compact in PGL_2(F_v) for v ∉ S. (i) For every maximal ideal m of T^S(K) there is a semisimple ρ̄_m: G_F → GL_2(T^S(K)/m) such that for all v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ, ρ̄_m|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and ρ̄_m(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v). (ii) There is a lift ρ_K: G_F → GL_2(T^S(K)_m) of ρ̄_m such that for all v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ, ρ_K|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and ρ_K(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v). For F CM, (i) is known by Scholze's work and (ii) for sufficiently large ℓ ([45, Theorems 1.1, 1.3]); this is similar to [17, Conjecture A]. Remark 13.3: suppose ρ̄_m is irreducible. Then (ii) follows from a weaker assumption: for some T ∈ CNL_O with an inclusion T^S(K)_m ↪ T there is a lift ρ_K: G_F → GL_2(T) of ρ̄_m that is unramified at every v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ, with ρ_K(Frob_v) of characteristic polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v). The reason is Chebotarev: the traces of Frob_v (v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ) lie in T^S(K)_m.
items.note: Conjecture A is an open hypothesis for general F, and no layer states or proves it, not even for CM fields. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure builds the infrastructure of Scholze's argument but says it is 'not an additional requirement to formalize its final Galois-representation theorem'. IHG.5 gives determinant schemas modulo nilpotent ideals, AG2 covers characteristic zero only, and the Newton–Thorne removal of the nilpotent ideal for large ℓ (part (ii), from Newton–Thorne 2016) is planned nowhere; the atlas's NEWTON-THORNE source is the symmetric-power papers. Remark 13.3 (a lift over a larger T descends to T^S(K)_m) is covered by IHG.1's reconstruction over complete local rings under residual absolute irreducibility, together with Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev layer 10).

items.name: Lemma 13.4: independence of S for non-Eisenstein localizations
items.statement: Assume Conjecture A. For any finite set of places S′ ⊇ S, the natural map T^{S′}(K)_m → T^S(K)_m is an isomorphism when m is non-Eisenstein. This is a consequence of Chebotarev density; see Khare–Thorne [38, Lemma 6.20]. So for non-Eisenstein m the localization does not depend on S and is written T(K)_m. Separately, as shown in [38], for any maximal ideal m ⊆ T(K) the localization (C_K)_m is a direct summand of C_K, and H_∗(Y_K, O)_m = H_∗(C_K)_m = H_∗((C_K)_m).
items.note: No layer states this lemma, but it is a short application of planned results. The independence of S follows from Conjecture A(ii), from reconstruction over the trace subalgebra (IHG.1, Carayol/Chenevier) and from Chebotarev density (Tau Ceti Chebotarev layer 10). That (C_K)_m is a direct summand with H_*(Y_K,O)_m = H_*((C_K)_m) is IHG.2's 'localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings'. Neither library has Hecke algebras acting on complexes or Carayol's theorem.

items.name: Lemma 13.5: an auxiliary prime t making level subgroups sufficiently small
items.statement: Let ρ̄: G_F → GL_2(k) with ρ̄|_{F(ζ_ℓ)} irreducible. (i) There is a place t ∉ S with (tr ρ̄(Frob_t))²/det ρ̄(Frob_t) ≠ (1 + Nm(t))²/Nm(t), Nm(t) ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), and Nm(t) > 4^{[F:Q]}. (ii) For such t, R_t^□ = R_t^min is a power series ring over O of relative dimension 3. (iii) For such t, K_1(t²) = {(a b; c d) ∈ PGL_2(Ô_F) : c ∈ t², ad^{−1} ≡ 1 mod t²} is sufficiently small. (Jarvis [35, Lemma 12.3] for (i); corrected statement, sourceIssues E10.)
items.note: Only part (ii) is planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1–R08.2 give R_t^□ = R_t^min ≅ O[[x₁,x₂,x₃]] once H²(G_{F_t}, ad⁰ρ̄) = 0, which the eigenvalue-ratio condition guarantees. Part (i), from Jarvis, Lemma 12.3, applies Chebotarev to F(ρ̄,ζ_ℓ)/F, and no layer states it; R04.5 picks Taylor–Wiles primes with Nm(q) ≡ 1 mod ℓ^n, the opposite congruence. Part (iii), that Nm(t) > 4^{[F:Q]} makes K₁(t²) torsion-free, is planned nowhere. The printed (i) lacks the square on the trace (draft issue E10); the item uses the corrected (tr ρ̄(Frob_t))²/det ρ̄(Frob_t) ≠ (1+Nm(t))²/Nm(t). See sourceIssues E10.

items.name: Level subgroups K_0(N), K_1(N), K_Δ(N) (with auxiliary level t²) and Y_0(N), Y_{0,Δ}(N, Q)
items.statement: Fix t as in Lemma 13.5. For a nonzero ideal N ⊆ O_F let K_0(N) := {(a b; c d) ∈ PGL_2(Ô_F) : c ∈ Nt², ad^{−1} ≡ 1 mod t²} and K_1(N) := {(a b; c d) ∈ PGL_2(Ô_F) : c ∈ Nt², ad^{−1} ≡ 1 mod Nt²}. Then K_1(N) ⊴ K_0(N) and K_0(N)/K_1(N) ≅ (O_F/N)^× via (a b; c d) ↦ ad^{−1} mod N; this isomorphism needs t ∤ N, which holds in every use (sourceIssues E48). K_Δ(N) is the smallest intermediate subgroup K_1(N) ≤ K_Δ(N) ≤ K_0(N) with |K_0(N)/K_Δ(N)| a power of ℓ (printed 'an ℓth power': sourceIssues E49). For N = v^e, K_0(v^e), K_1(v^e), K_Δ(v^e) also denote the subgroups K_0(v^e) ∩ PGL_2(O_{F,v}), K_1(v^e) ∩ PGL_2(O_{F,v}), K_Δ(v^e) ∩ PGL_2(O_{F,v}) of PGL_2(F_v). Y_0(N) := Y_{K_0(N)}. For an ideal Q of O_F prime to N, Y_{0,Δ}(N, Q) := Y_{K_0(N) ∩ K_Δ(Q)}. C_0(N), C_{0,Δ}(N, Q) are the corresponding perfect complexes in D(O). Level structure at t is imposed on all these groups but suppressed from the notation.
items.note: These are specific compact open subgroups of PGL₂(Ô_F) with the t²-level built in: K₀(N), K₁(N), the isomorphism K₀(N)/K₁(N) ≅ (O_F/N)^× given by ad⁻¹, the ℓ-part K_Δ(N), and the spaces Y₀(N), Y_{0,Δ}(N,Q) with their complexes. ALS and AA plan arbitrary compact opens but define none of these, and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves uses quaternionic levels over totally real fields. The only library relatives are Mathlib's Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N) ⊆ SL(2,ℤ), a near miss (F = ℚ, SL₂, no adeles). See sourceIssues E48, E49.

items.name: Proposition 13.6: Verdier duality for the localized chain complexes
items.statement: Assume Conjecture A; fix a non-Eisenstein m ⊆ T^S(K_0(N_∅)) with N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅. For compact open K ⊆ K_0(N_∅) there is a natural derived T(K)_m-isomorphism (C_K)_m ≅ RHom_O((C_K)_m, O)[2r_1 + 3r_2] = (C_K)_m^† in D_{T(K)_m}(O); the adjoint of [K_2αK_1]: (C_{K_1})_m → (C_{K_2})_m is [K_1α^{−1}K_2]. (Newton–Thorne [45, Prop. 3.7, Thm 4.2].)
items.note: ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans Poincaré–Lefschetz/Verdier duality for perfect complexes with Hecke adjoint formulas; its contract says 'Hecke adjoints use inverse double cosets'. ALS.4 plans the boundary triangle and boundary vanishing after localization 'by an actual eigenvalue argument'; that step identifies homology with Borel–Moore homology at non-Eisenstein m, and is Newton–Thorne's condition ♠ (Conjecture A for GL₂, class field theory for GL₁). Neither library has any of this. A possible gap (not in issues_draft, not checked against Newton–Thorne 2016, which treats CM fields): if F has a real place, Y_K can be non-orientable. For F = ℚ, t = 5, (7 2; 25 7) ∈ PGL₂(ℚ) ∩ K₁(25) has det −1 and infinite order, so duality pairs C_K with the orientation-twisted complex, and the Poincaré pairing vanishes on H₁(Ỹ)⁺ = H₁(Y_K); a fix is K∞° or an orientation twist. See sourceIssues E65 (orientation at real places).

items.name: Proposition 13.7: a Hecke-equivariant self-duality twisted by Atkin–Lehner operators
items.statement: For K = ∏K_v ⊆ K_0(N_∅) with each K_v = PGL_2(O_{F,v}) or K_1(v) ≤ K_v ≤ K_0(v), let w_v := [K (0 −1; ϖ_v 0) K] (w_v = 1 if K_v maximal) and w_K := ∏_{v∈S} w_v (w_K² = 1). The isomorphism ϕ_K: (C_K)_m →(w_K) (C_K)_m ≅ (C_K)_m^† commutes with all T_v, U_v, ⟨d⟩_v, and the adjoint of [K_2αK_1] with respect to ϕ_{K_1}, ϕ_{K_2} is w_{K_1}[K_1α^{−1}K_2]w_{K_2}.
items.note: No layer plans the self-duality ϕ_K = (Proposition 13.6) ∘ w_K, twisted by the Atkin–Lehner operators w_v = [K(0 −1; ϖ_v 0)K] at Iwahori/K₁(v) level, or the adjoint formula w_{K₁}[K₁α⁻¹K₂]w_{K₂}. ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans only the untwisted inverse-double-coset adjoint. Tau Ceti's Atkin–Lehner material concerns Γ₀(N) ⊂ GL₂(ℚ) acting on modular forms, and the anti-involution used for commutativity of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring; that is a near miss. The matrix identities used (w_v normalizes K_v; w(a 0; 0 d)⁻¹w⁻¹ = (a 0; 0 d) in PGL₂(F_v)) are routine; the item inherits the orientation caveat of prop-13-6. See sourceIssues E50, E51.

items.name: Level-lowering maps π_{K,v} and the relation with U_v
items.statement: Let K ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) be a compact open subgroup as before, and v a place with K_v = PGL_2(O_{F,v}). Put L := K ∩ K_0(v). Define π_1 := [K 1 L] and π_2 := [K diag(ϖ_v,1) L], both (C_L)_m → (C_K)_m. Let π_{K,v} := π_1 ⊕ π_2: (C_L)_m → (C_K)_m^{⊕2}, and let π_{K,v}^†: (C_K)_m^{⊕2} → (C_L)_m be its adjoint with respect to ϕ_K and ϕ_L. With U_v = [L diag(ϖ_v,1) L] one has π_1 ∘ U_v = Nm(v)·π_2 and π_2 ∘ U_v = T_v ∘ π_2 − π_1, i.e. π_{K,v} ∘ U_v = (0 Nm(v); −1 T_v) ∘ π_{K,v} as morphisms (C_L)_m → (C_K)_m^{⊕2}. The paper prints the matrix (T_v −1; Nm(v) 0), which is the relation for π_2 ⊕ π_1 (sourceIssues E53).
items.note: The maps π₁ = [K 1 L] and π₂ = [K diag(ϖ_v,1) L] are ALS.3 change-of-level double-coset operators, which is planned. The level-lowering map π_{K,v}, its adjoint for ϕ_K, and the identity π_{K,v} ∘ U_v = (T_v −1; Nm(v) 0) ∘ π_{K,v} are planned nowhere for PGL₂/F; the analogous degeneracy maps appear only for modular curves (ModularCurvesPartII R14.1). The identity is a computation in the mixed-level Hecke module H(K\G/L), which Tau Ceti's HeckeCosetModule.mul could host once the coset decompositions in PGL₂(F_v) exist. See sourceIssues E53.

items.name: Localized Hecke algebras T_Σ, T_{Σ,Q}, full Hecke algebras and maximal ideals m_{Σ,Q}
items.statement: Pick disjoint finite sets T and Q of places satisfying the conditions of 12.2 (so every element of T ∪ Q is prime to N_∅). For Σ ⊆ T put N_Σ := N_∅∏_{v∈Σ} v. Assume T ∪ Q ⊆ S and that S contains all primes dividing N_∅ and the place t. Let K_Σ := K_0(N_Σ) and K_{Σ,Q} := K_0(N_Σ) ∩ K_Δ(Q), so K_{Σ,∅} = K_Σ. Let m ⊆ T^S(K_0(N_∅)) be non-Eisenstein with ρ̄_m|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} absolutely irreducible; for K ⊆ K_0(N_Σ), m ⊆ T^S(K) denotes its preimage. T_Σ := T^S(K_Σ)_m and T_{Σ,Q} := T^S(K_{Σ,Q})_m. The full Hecke algebras are T̃^S(K_Σ) := T^S(K_Σ)[{U_v}_{v∈Σ}] ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_{K_Σ}) and T̃^S(K_{Σ,Q}) := T^S(K_{Σ,Q})[{U_v}_{v∈Σ∪Q}, {⟨d⟩_v}_{v∈Q, d∈Δ_v}] ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_{K_{Σ,Q}}) (printed with T^S(K_Σ)). They are commutative O-algebras, finite over T^S(K_Σ), resp. T^S(K_{Σ,Q}), and T̃^S(K_{Σ,∅}) = T̃^S(K_Σ). m_{Σ,Q} ⊆ T̃^S(K_{Σ,Q}) is the ideal over m ⊆ T^S(K_{Σ,Q}) containing U_v − ε_v (v ∈ Σ) and U_v − γ_{1,v} (v ∈ Q). It is maximal and lies over m_{Σ,∅} ⊆ T̃^S(K_Σ), and for Σ_1 ⊆ Σ_2, m_{Σ_2,Q} lies over m_{Σ_1,Q}. Write m_Σ := m_{Σ,∅}, C_Σ := (C_{K_Σ})_{m_Σ} and C_{Σ,Q} := (C_{K_{Σ,Q}})_{m_{Σ,Q}}. These are not (C_{K_Σ})_m or (C_{K_{Σ,Q}})_m, since the localization is at a larger ring. One has C_Σ ∈ D_{T_Σ}(O) and C_{Σ,Q} ∈ D_{T_{Σ,Q}}(O).
items.note: This item defines the Taylor–Wiles-level full Hecke algebras T̃^S(K_{Σ,Q}), with U_v (v ∈ Σ ∪ Q) and ⟨d⟩_v (v ∈ Q), the maximal ideals m_{Σ,Q} containing U_v − ε_v and U_v − γ_{1,v}, and the localized complexes C_Σ and C_{Σ,Q}. The generic ingredients are planned (ALS.3 operators; IHG.2 image algebras and localization). The analogous constructions are planned only in other settings: GL2ModularityLifting R22.1/R22.2 for quaternionic Hecke modules over totally real fields, and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.4 for GL_n over CM fields. Nothing covers PGL₂ over an arbitrary number field, and no library has it. See sourceIssues E54.

items.name: Conjecture B: local–global compatibility, R_{Σ,Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q}
items.statement: (Assumed.) For any Σ and Q, the representations ρ_{Σ,Q}: G_F → GL_2(T_{Σ,Q}) coming from Conjecture A arise from the universal representation G_F → GL_2(R_{Σ,Q}) via surjections R_{Σ,Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q}, and satisfy the following. (1) tr ρ_{Σ,Q}(Frob_v) = T_v for all v ∉ S. (2) Give R_{Σ,Q} the O[Δ_Q]-structure of Proposition 12.3. Then the composite R_{Σ,Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q} → T̃^S(K_{Σ,Q})_{m_{Σ,Q}} is an O[Δ_Q]-algebra homomorphism, and χ_{1,v}(ϕ_v) maps to U_v for v ∈ Q, for a suitable lift ϕ_v of Frob_v. (3) For v ∈ Σ, let B_v ∈ T_Σ^□ be the image of B_v ∈ R_v^{uni(ε_v)} under R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ↪ R_{Σ,loc} → R_Σ^□ ↠ T_Σ^□. Then (B_v) = (ε_vU_v − 1) as ideals of T_Σ^□. (T_Σ^□ is not defined in the paper; presumably T_Σ ⊗_{R_Σ} R_Σ^□.) (4) For Σ_1 ⊆ Σ_2 ⊆ T, two squares commute, with the natural surjections as vertical maps: R_{Σ,Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q} over R_Σ ↠ T_Σ, and R_{Σ_2,Q} ↠ T_{Σ_2,Q} over R_{Σ_1,Q} ↠ T_{Σ_1,Q}. Many cases are known up to a nilpotent ideal ([1, §3, §4]). Because T_{Σ,Q} is a quotient of R_{Σ,Q}, ρ_{Σ,Q} satisfies the local–global compatibility conditions built into R_{Σ,Q} (e.g. flatness at v | ℓ).
items.note: This is the assumed local–global compatibility: surjections R_{Σ,Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q} that are O[Δ_Q]-linear, send χ_{1,v}(ϕ_v) ↦ U_v, satisfy (B_v) = (ε_vU_v − 1), and are compatible in Σ and Q. It is open for general F. Analogues are planned elsewhere, but no layer states this conjecture: the deformation-to-Hecke surjection for quaternionic modules (R22.1), characteristic-zero local–global compatibility (AG2.5), and for CM fields ACC+'s torsion versions modulo a nilpotent ideal (PA.1/PA.2 and the §3 inputs routed to AG2/IHG). R_{Σ,Q}, R_v^{uni(ε_v)} and B_v come from the paper's §12 (cluster C6). See sourceIssues E55 (B(3) is needed at every level).

items.name: Lemma 13.8: the full Hecke algebra equals T_{Σ,Q} after localization
items.statement: Assuming Conjecture B, T̃^S(K_{Σ,Q})_{m_{Σ,Q}} = T^S(K_{Σ,Q})_m = T_{Σ,Q}; so U_v (v ∈ Σ ∪ Q) and ⟨d⟩_v (v ∈ Q) lie in T_{Σ,Q}, which becomes an O[Δ_Q]-algebra.
items.note: A short consequence of Conjecture B: U_v (v ∈ Σ ∪ Q) and ⟨d⟩_v (v ∈ Q) lie in T_{Σ,Q}, which makes T_{Σ,Q} an O[Δ_Q]-algebra. No layer or library states it. See sourceIssues E55.

items.name: Proposition 13.9: Taylor–Wiles level complexes are perfect over O[Δ_Q]
items.statement: For each Σ ⊆ T and Q: C_{Σ,Q} is a perfect complex of O[Δ_Q]-modules via O[Δ_Q] → T_{Σ,Q} → End_{D(O)}(C_{Σ,Q}); T_{Σ,Q} ⊗_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ T_Σ; and C_{Σ,Q} ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ C_Σ in D_{T_Σ}(O). (Khare–Thorne [38, §5]; Calegari–Geraghty [17, Lemma 9.5].)
items.note: The proposition has three parts: C_{Σ,Q} is perfect over O[Δ_Q]; T_{Σ,Q} ⊗_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ T_Σ; and C_{Σ,Q} ⊗ᴸ_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ C_Σ (Khare–Thorne §5, Calegari–Geraghty Lemma 9.5). The unlocalized covering-space part is planned, because Y_{K_{Σ,Q}} → Y₀(N_Σ Q) is Galois with group Δ_Q: ALS.6 (finite-cover descent), Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stage 5 (C_*(E)_G ≅ C_*(B)) and ALS.1 (finite models). DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8 expects ALS to supply 'group-algebra freeness at auxiliary level', but no ALS stage states it. The Taylor–Wiles comparison after localizing at m_{Σ,Q} against m_Σ (the γ_{1,v}-eigenspace of U_v at Iwahori level against spherical level) is planned only for CM GL_n (PA.4) and quaternionic modules (R22.2, R18.3).

items.name: Proposition 13.10: self-duality of C_{Σ,Q} and π_v ∘ π_v^† = U_v² − 1
items.statement: Fix v ∈ T ∖ Σ. Take K = K_{Σ,Q}, so that L = K ∩ K_0(v) = K_{Σ∪{v},Q}, and let U′_v be the operator (0 Nm(v); −1 T_v) on (C_{K_{Σ,Q}})^{⊕2}_{m_{Σ,Q}}. The paper prints (T_v −1; Nm(v) 0) (sourceIssues E53). Then π_{K,v} ∘ U_v = U′_v ∘ π_{K,v} and U′_v² − T_vU′_v + Nm(v) = 0. Localize (C_{K_{Σ,Q}})^{⊕2}_{m_{Σ,Q}} at the maximal ideal m′_{Σ,Q} := (m_{Σ,Q}, U′_v − ε_v) of T_{Σ,Q}[U′_v]/(U′_v² − T_vU′_v + Nm(v)). The result is isomorphic as a T_{Σ,Q}-module to C_{Σ,Q}. This gives a Hecke-equivariant (for T_{Σ∪{v},Q}) map π_v: C_{Σ∪{v},Q} → C_{Σ,Q}, on which U′_v acts as U_v ∈ T_{Σ,Q} (via Lemma 13.8 and T_{Σ∪{v},Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q}). Proposition 13.10: there is a family of isomorphisms ϕ_{Σ,Q}: C_{Σ,Q} ≅ C_{Σ,Q}^† in D_{T_{Σ,Q}}(O) compatible with C_{Σ,Q} ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ C_Σ. For v ∈ T ∖ Σ, let π_v^†: C_{Σ,Q} ≅ C_{Σ,Q}^† → C_{Σ∪{v},Q}^† ≅ C_{Σ∪{v},Q} be the adjoint of π_v under ϕ_{Σ,Q} and ϕ_{Σ∪{v},Q}. Then π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ U_v² − 1 in End_{D(O)}(C_{Σ,Q}) and π_v^† ∘ π_v ≃ U_v² − 1 in End_{D(O)}(C_{Σ∪{v},Q}), where ≃ means equality up to units of T_{Σ,Q}, resp. T_{Σ∪{v},Q}.
items.locator: 13.6 (construction of π_v, p. 65) and Proposition 13.10, pp. 65–66
items.note: The proposition gives the self-duality ϕ_{Σ,Q} of the Taylor–Wiles complexes, compatible with ⊗ᴸ_{O[Δ_Q]} O, and the level-raising identities π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ U_v² − 1 ≃ π_v^† ∘ π_v up to units, which is Ribet's computation (Ribet 1984, Proposition 3.3) transported to complexes. It is not planned. Level change and level raising are planned only for modular curves (ModularCurvesPartII R14.1, R14.4) and Shimura curves (R18.4, 'degeneracy-map properties'). The item builds on the missing Proposition 13.7, the level-lowering maps and T_{Σ,Q}, and inherits the orientation caveat of prop-13-6. See sourceIssues E53.

items.name: Conjecture C: concentration of non-Eisenstein homology in degrees [r_1 + r_2, r_1 + 2r_2]
items.statement: (Assumed.) If K ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) is any compact open subgroup and m is a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, then H_i(Y_K, k)_m = 0 for i ∉ [r_1 + r_2, r_1 + 2r_2]. The paper prints X_K; see E14. Consequently H_i(Y_K, O)_m = 0 for i < r_1 + r_2 (p. 66). Known for F imaginary quadratic: then Y_K is a 3-dimensional manifold, and H_i(Y_K, k)_m = 0 for i = 0, 3 because m is non-Eisenstein.
items.note: This is Calegari–Geraghty-type vanishing of non-Eisenstein mod-ℓ homology outside [r₁+r₂, r₁+2r₂]. It is open in general and known for F imaginary quadratic, where H₃ of the non-compact 3-manifold vanishes and H₀ is Eisenstein. No layer plans it for PGL₂/F: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.7 plans the analogous localized concentration for unitary Shimura varieties (Caraiani–Scholze), and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9 only the algebraic consequences of an amplitude bound. The printed 'X_K' should read Y_K (draft issue E14). See sourceIssues E14.

items.name: Conjecture D: Ihara's lemma in the lowest degree
items.statement: (Assumed.) For K, v as in 13.5 and non-Eisenstein m ⊆ T^S(K), the level-lowering map induces a surjection H_{r_1+r_2}(π_{K,v}): H_{r_1+r_2}(Y_{K∩K_0(v)}, O)_m → H_{r_1+r_2}(Y_K, O)_m^{⊕2}. Lemma 13.11: if Conjecture D holds for K = K_{Σ,Q}, then H_{r_1+r_2}(π_v): H_{r_1+r_2}(C_{Σ∪{v},Q}) → H_{r_1+r_2}(C_{Σ,Q}) is surjective.
items.note: The item combines Ihara's lemma in the lowest degree r₁+r₂ (as a hypothesis on H_{r₁+r₂}(π_{K,v})) with Lemma 13.11, its immediate localization to C_{Σ,Q}. Ihara's lemma is planned only for modular curves (ModularCurvesPartII R14.4); ACC+'s derived Ihara avoidance (P9, PA.3) is designed to avoid needing this statement. The library audit for R14.4 found no Ihara lemma in either library.

items.name: Theorem 13.12: Ihara's lemma for Bianchi manifolds
items.statement: When F is imaginary quadratic and ℓ > 3, Conjecture D holds: H_1(π_{K,v}): H_1(Y_{K∩K_0(v)}, O)_m → H_1(Y_K, O)_m^{⊕2} is surjective (consequence of the congruence subgroup property of SL_2(O_F[1/v]); Calegari–Venkatesh [18, §4.1], Klosin [40]).
items.note: Ihara's lemma for Bianchi manifolds (F imaginary quadratic, ℓ > 3) is a consequence of the congruence subgroup property of SL₂(O_F[1/v]) (Serre), following Calegari–Venkatesh §4.1 and Klosin 2008; ℓ > 3 avoids the finite congruence kernel. It is not planned: ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 is restricted to modular curves, where the tree/CSP route for SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) is the analogue that PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25 routed there. No layer or roadmap document plans the congruence subgroup property for SL₂ over S-integers. Neither library has Ihara's lemma, Bruhat–Tits trees or the congruence subgroup property.

items.name: Shimura curves X_K^𝔇 over Q and their integral models
items.statement: Standing setting of §14 (Case (Wt1), F = Q): 𝔇 is a finite set of primes of even cardinality (𝔇 also denotes the product of its primes). ℓ > 3 is a prime with ℓ ∉ 𝔇 and v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ) for all v ∈ 𝔇. E, O, ϖ, k are as before. Theorem H for 𝔇 = ∅ is Calegari [16]; in the proofs of §14 one assumes 𝔇 ≠ ∅. D_𝔇 is the quaternion algebra over Q ramified exactly at the primes of 𝔇; it is indefinite because |𝔇| is even. Let K = ∏_q K_q ⊆ D_𝔇^×(A_Q^∞) be a compact open subgroup such that: K_q is the maximal compact subgroup of D_𝔇^×(Q_q) for q ∈ 𝔇; K_ℓ is a maximal compact subgroup of D_𝔇^×(Q_ℓ) ≅ GL_2(Q_ℓ) (printed 'of PGL_2(Q_ℓ)', see E15); K is sufficiently small, i.e. gKg^{−1} ∩ D_𝔇^×(Q) is torsion free for all g ∈ D_𝔇^×(A_Q^∞); and the determinant map K → ∏_q Z_q^× is surjective. A typical example is K^𝔇_{H,Δ}(N_Σ, Q) of 14.2. Set X_K^𝔇 := D^×(Q)\(D^×(A_Q^∞) × ℋ^±)/K, where ℋ^± := C ∖ R. It is a compact Riemann surface, given its canonical structure as an algebraic curve over Q. 𝒳_K^𝔇 is a minimal integral model of X_K^𝔇 over O, and 𝒳^𝔇_{K,A} is its base change to an O-algebra A.
items.note: R18.1 plans the canonical Shimura curve, with its level and stabilizers, of a quaternion algebra over a totally real field that is split at one specified real place. Over F = Q with D_𝔇 indefinite, that is this curve. R18.2 plans its integral models at good places, and PELModuli M2 plans the good-prime PEL moduli space with its universal abelian scheme (quaternionic factors explicitly allowed), which supplies 𝒜 → 𝒳_{K,A}. The existence of D_𝔇 ramified exactly at 𝔇 (#𝔇 even) comes from Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 (exists_br_of_sum_eq_zero) and Layer 14 (parity). The QM (fake elliptic curve) PEL instance is not among PELModuli M5's listed examples, so R18.2/M2 must specialise to it. Printed 'K_ℓ … of PGL_2(Q_ℓ)' should read GL_2(Q_ℓ) (issue E15). See sourceIssues E15.

items.name: The weight-one sheaf ω and integral coherent homology H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_O)
items.statement: For A = O, E, O/ϖ^nO, ω_A is the sheaf on X_K^𝔇 obtained by applying an idempotent e as in Diamond–Taylor [25, §4] (satisfying e^∗ = e for a Rosati involution ∗) to π_∗Ω_{𝒜/𝒳^𝔇_{K,A}}, where π: 𝒜 → 𝒳^𝔇_{K,A} is the universal abelian surface. For n ≥ 1 the coherent homology (as in [17, §7.2]) is H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_{O/ϖ^nO}) := Hom_O(H^i(X_K^𝔇, ω_{O/ϖ^nO}), E/O), and H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_O) := lim_{←n} H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_{O/ϖ^nO}). Define ω_{E/O} := lim_{→n} ω_{ϖ^{−n}O/O}; then H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_O) = Hom_O(H^i(X_K^𝔇, ω_{E/O}), E/O). The Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism gives ω_A^{⊗2} ≅ Ω_A, the canonical sheaf of the Shimura curve. It is used together with Serre duality in the proofs of Propositions 14.3 and 14.7 and Theorem 14.10.
items.locator: 14.1, p. 67 (Kodaira–Spencer: proofs of Proposition 14.3, p. 69, Proposition 14.7, p. 73, and Theorem 14.10, p. 74)
items.note: No layer plans any of three things: the ℓ-integral weight-one sheaf ω_A = e·π_*Ω_{𝒜/𝒳_{K,A}} on a quaternionic Shimura curve (with the Diamond–Taylor idempotent e = e^*), the Pontryagin-dual coherent homology H_i(X, ω_O) := lim Hom_O(H^i(X, ω_{O/ϖ^n}), E/O), or the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω on the Shimura curve. The nearest layers do less. AutomorphicBundles B2/B4 work in characteristic zero over canonical models, with explicit weights only for GL₂, Hilbert, Siegel and unitary PEL. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1 covers the Hodge bundle and Kodaira–Spencer on modular curves only, per its reviewed decomposition node. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 ('identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration') and PELModuli M6 ('universal abelian scheme and its Hodge line') are generic ingredients. Tau Ceti defines only the groups Hⁱ(X, M).

items.name: Proposition 14.1: perfect complexes computing weight-one coherent homology
items.statement: Let K ⊆ D_𝔇^×(A_Q^∞) be a compact open subgroup satisfying the hypotheses of 14.1. (1) There is a perfect complex C_K^𝔇 in D(O) such that for all i: (a) H_i(C_K^𝔇 ⊗^L_O k) = 0 for i ∉ [0,1]; (b) H_i(C_K^𝔇 ⊗^L_O O/ϖ^n) ≅ H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_{O/ϖ^nO}) for all n ≥ 1 (printed n ≥ 0); (c) H_i(C_K^𝔇) ≅ H_i(X_K^𝔇, ω_O). (2) Let K_Δ ⊆ D_𝔇^×(A_Q^∞) be another compact open subgroup satisfying the same hypotheses, with K_Δ ⊴ K and Δ := K/K_Δ a finite abelian group of ℓ-power order. Then there is a perfect complex C^𝔇_{K_Δ} in D(O[Δ]) such that for all i: (a) H_i(C^𝔇_{K_Δ} ⊗^L_{O[Δ]} k) = 0 for i ∉ [0,1]; (b) H_i(C^𝔇_{K_Δ} ⊗^L_{O[Δ]} O/ϖ^n[Δ]) ≅ H_i(X^𝔇_{K_Δ}, ω_{O/ϖ^nO}) as O[Δ]-modules for all n; (c) H_i(C^𝔇_{K_Δ}) ≅ H_i(X^𝔇_{K_Δ}, ω_O) as O[Δ]-modules; (d) C^𝔇_{K_Δ} ⊗^L_{O[Δ]} O ≅ C_K^𝔇 in D(O). The O[Δ]-module structures on H_i(X^𝔇_{K_Δ}, ω_{O/ϖ^nO}) and H_i(X^𝔇_{K_Δ}, ω_O) are induced by the action of Δ on X^𝔇_{K_Δ}. Part (1) is part (2) with K_Δ = K. Proof sketch: X^𝔇_{K_Δ} → X^𝔇_K is étale Galois with group Δ. Čech complexes as in Calegari–Geraghty [17, §7.2] give perfect complexes C^𝔇_{K_Δ,n} over (O/ϖ^n)[Δ], and these are assembled by Khare–Thorne [38, Lemmas 2.13, 2.14].
items.note: The geometric input is not planned: Čech complexes of ω_{O/ϖ^n} for the étale Galois cover X_{K_Δ} → X_K (group Δ), giving perfect (O/ϖ^n)[Δ]-complexes with the stated base-change isomorphisms and amplitude [0,1] mod ϖ. Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layers B–C and StableReduction Layer 2 plan the ingredients: Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme, vanishing above degree one on a curve, and base change over a locally Noetherian base. The algebraic step from the compatible system to a perfect O[Δ]-complex (Khare–Thorne [38, Lemmas 2.13–2.14]) falls within DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7. The Δ-equivariant construction on the Shimura curve is planned nowhere. See sourceIssues E58.

items.name: Hecke operators and the Hecke algebra T^S(K) on C_K^𝔇
items.statement: Double coset operators act on the complexes C_K^𝔇 by the procedure of Calegari–Geraghty [17, §7.2]. The actions on C^𝔇_{K,n} are lifted to C_K^𝔇 using Khare–Thorne [38, §2.4]. Let S be a set of primes containing the primes of 𝔇, the primes v for which K_v is not maximal compact, and ℓ. For v ∉ S, T_v := [K (ϖ_v 0; 0 1) K] ∈ End_{D(O)}(C_K^𝔇). Now let v ∈ S ∖ 𝔇 with v ≠ ℓ, K_1(v) ≤ K_v ≤ K_0(v), and d ∈ K_0(v)/K_v ↪ (Z/v)^×. Then U_v := [K (ϖ_v 0; 0 1) K] and ⟨d⟩_v := [K (d̃ 0; 0 1) K] ∈ End_{D(O)}(C_K^𝔇) for any lift d̃ ∈ Z_v^× of d. This is as printed; with K_1(v) = {c ≡ 0, d ≡ 1 mod v} as in K_1^𝔇(N), the intended operator is [K (1 0; 0 d̃) K] (sourceIssues E56). T^S(K) := O[T_v | v ∉ S] ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K^𝔇) is a finite commutative O-algebra.
items.note: No layer constructs the double-coset operators T_v, U_v, ⟨d⟩_v on the integral coherent complexes C_K^𝔇 of a Shimura curve, or the algebra T^S(K) ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K^𝔇). HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.2 ('prove extension of Hecke maps') and AutomorphicBundles B5 (Hecke pullback and trace on automorphic bundles over canonical models) supply pieces. So do IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 (image algebras of a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex; sole owner per RS-24) and P7 (Hecke actions through inverse limits, cf. [38, §2.4]). Mathlib's abstract HeckeRing is a near miss: it is a double-coset convolution ring, not an action on any complex. See sourceIssues E56.

items.name: Proposition 14.3: Serre duality for C_K^𝔇
items.statement: For each K there is a natural derived T^S(K)-equivariant isomorphism C_K^𝔇 ≅ RHom_O(C_K^𝔇, O)[1] = (C_K^𝔇)^† in D_{T^S(K)}(O), where (−)^† := RHom_O(−, O)[1]. Proof: Serre duality for the sheaves ω_A together with the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω_A^{⊗2} = Ω_A, following Boxer–Pilloni [11, §3.2]; then as in the proof of Proposition 13.6.
items.note: Serre duality itself is planned in Tau Ceti roadmaps: JacobianChallenge Layer B over a field, and the shared 'J-B / SR-2' relative dualizing-sheaf interface of StableReduction Layer 2 for proper flat Gorenstein curves over a locally Noetherian base (hence over O and O/ϖ^n). Not planned is the derived, T^S(K)-equivariant self-duality C_K^𝔇 ≅ RHom_O(C_K^𝔇, O)[1]. That also needs the Shimura-curve Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω and the behaviour of the Hecke correspondences under duality (Boxer–Pilloni [11, §3.2]). Neither library has a dualizing sheaf or Serre duality. See sourceIssues E59.

items.name: Proposition 14.2: the derived Hecke algebra acts faithfully on H_0
items.statement: The ring T^S(K) ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K^𝔇) acts faithfully on H^0(C_K^𝔇) = H_0(C_K^𝔇) ≅ H_0(X_K^𝔇, ω_O) = H^0(X_K^𝔇, ω_{E/O})^∗. Hence T^S(K) agrees with the classical Hecke algebra, the subring of End_O(H^0(X_K^𝔇, ω_{E/O})). The proof deduces this from Proposition 14.3 and Lemma 10.8: if f acts trivially on H^0(C_K^𝔇), then f^† acts trivially on H^0((C_K^𝔇)^†) ≅ H^0(C_K^𝔇).
items.note: Proposition 14.2 is Proposition 14.3 combined with Lemma 10.8 (item lemma-10-8, cluster C5); Proposition 14.3 is missing, so this is missing too. IHG.2 plans the comparison of derived and cohomological Hecke actions only up to a nilpotent ('ghost') ideal. That is strictly weaker than faithfulness on H_0 and does not identify T^S(K) with the classical Hecke algebra on H^0(X, ω_{E/O}). The paper prints H^0(C_K^𝔇) in cohomological indexing, which is H_0 in the homological indexing of Proposition 14.1.

items.name: Lemma 14.4: the Hasse invariant on Shimura curves and its Hecke equivariance
items.statement: Let X = X_K^𝔇. There is an element Ha ∈ H^0(X_k, ω^{⊗(ℓ−1)}), a Hasse invariant, which has simple zeros at all the supersingular points of X_k. Multiplication by Ha, H^0(X_k, ω^{⊗κ}) → H^0(X_k, ω^{⊗(κ+ℓ−1)}), is equivariant for the Hecke operators T_r and U_r for all primes r ≠ ℓ and all weights κ ≥ 1, and also for U_ℓ if κ ≥ 2 (Buzzard [15, §5]). Ha lifts to a section H̃a ∈ H^0(X_O, ω^{⊗(ℓ−1)}) (Kassaei [37, §7], using ℓ > 3). For all m ≥ 1 and all weights κ ≥ 1, multiplication by H̃a^{ℓ^{m−1}}, H^0(X_{O/ϖ^m}, ω^{⊗κ}_{O/ϖ^m}) → H^0(X_{O/ϖ^m}, ω^{⊗(κ+(ℓ−1)ℓ^{m−1})}_{O/ϖ^m}), is equivariant for T_r for all r ∉ S. The proof follows the argument of Boxer [9, Prop. 7.2.1]: the image of H̃a^{ℓ^{m−1}} in H^0(X_{O/ϖ^m}, ω^{⊗(ℓ−1)ℓ^{m−1}}) does not depend on the choice of lift.
items.note: Hasse invariants are planned only in three other settings: modular curves (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.3, via q-expansions), Hilbert–Blumenthal ordinary loci (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2), and Ekedahl–Oort strata in the Igusa/perfectoid setting (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2). None constructs Ha ∈ H^0(X_k, ω^{⊗(ℓ−1)}) on a quaternionic Shimura curve over Q with simple zeros exactly at the supersingular points. None proves its Hecke equivariance (T_r and U_r for r ≠ ℓ; U_ℓ in weight ≥ 2), Kassaei's lift H̃a for ℓ > 3, or that H̃a^{ℓ^{m−1}} mod ϖ^m is independent of the lift and Hecke-equivariant (Boxer [9, Prop. 7.2.1]). The reviewed audit (AUDIT-13) finds no Hasse invariant in either library.

items.name: Theorem 14.5: Galois representations for weight-one Hecke eigenclasses on Shimura curves (Conjecture A in weight one)
items.statement: (i) For every maximal ideal m of T^S(K) there is a semisimple ρ̄_m: G_Q → GL_2(T^S(K)/m), unramified at v ∉ S, v ≠ ℓ, with tr ρ̄_m(Frob_v) = T_v mod m, and unramified at ℓ. (ii) There is a lift ρ_K: G_Q → GL_2(T^S(K)_m), unramified at v ∉ S ∪ {ℓ} with char. poly x² − T_v x + ψ(Frob_v) (ψ the Teichmüller lift of det ρ̄_m), and unramified at ℓ. (Proof: the doubling method of Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11], with injectivity of the doubling map proved without q-expansions via Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni [10, §5.1].)
items.note: No layer plans the doubling argument, for modular or for Shimura curves: Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11], with the q-expansion-free injectivity through the supersingular locus of [10, §5.1]. The partial inputs are AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2 (quaternionic and Hilbert Galois representations in cohomological weight), R19.6 (determinant law and representation over a localised Hecke algebra) and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.4 (determinants through finite quotients). R19.1 and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.5 give Deligne–Serre in characteristic zero, which does not reach torsion weight-one Hecke algebras or unramifiedness at ℓ. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.1 only 'Organize[s] Deligne-Serre Artin representations, weight-one modularity in proved cases'. See sourceIssues E57 (the determinant at Taylor–Wiles level) and E16 (misprint).

items.name: Level subgroups K_0^𝔇(N), K_1^𝔇(N), K_Δ^𝔇(N), K_H^𝔇(N) and X_{Σ,Q}^𝔇
items.statement: From 14.2 on, fix ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) with ρ̄|_{Q(ζ_ℓ)} absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_ℓ} unramified. Let N_∅ = N(ρ̄) be its conductor and ψ: G_Q → O^× the Teichmüller lift of det ρ̄. T and Q are finite sets of primes, disjoint from each other and from 𝔇, satisfying the conditions of 12.2. t is an auxiliary prime not in T ∪ Q ∪ 𝔇 satisfying the conditions of Lemma 13.5 for ρ̄. Identify D_𝔇(Z_v) = GL_2(Z_v) for v ∉ 𝔇. For an integer N ≥ 1 with (N, 𝔇) = 1: K_0^𝔇(N) := {(a b; c d) ∈ D_𝔇^×(Ẑ) : c ≡ 0 (mod Nt²), d ≡ 1 (mod t²)} and K_1^𝔇(N) := {(a b; c d) ∈ D_𝔇^×(Ẑ) : c ≡ 0 (mod Nt²), d ≡ 1 (mod Nt²)}. Then K_1^𝔇(N) ⊴ K_0^𝔇(N) with K_0^𝔇(N)/K_1^𝔇(N) ≅ (Z/NZ)^×, and both are sufficiently small. K_Δ^𝔇(N) and K_H^𝔇(N) are the smallest intermediate subgroups K_1^𝔇(N) ≤ K_Δ^𝔇(N), K_H^𝔇(N) ≤ K_0^𝔇(N) such that |K_0^𝔇(N)/K_Δ^𝔇(N)| is a power of ℓ and |K_0^𝔇(N)/K_H^𝔇(N)| is prime to ℓ. Set K^𝔇_{H,Δ}(N, M) := K_H^𝔇(N) ∩ K_Δ^𝔇(M). For Σ ⊆ T let N_Σ := N_∅·∏_{v∈Σ} v (printed 'N_φ Σ'). Set K^𝔇_{Σ,Q} := K^𝔇_{H,Δ}(N_Σ, Q) and K^𝔇_Σ := K^𝔇_{Σ,∅} = K^𝔇_H(N_Σ). Set X^𝔇_{Σ,Q} := X^𝔇_{K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}}, ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q} := ρ_{K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}} (from Theorem 14.5), X^𝔇_Σ := X^𝔇_{Σ,∅} and ρ^𝔇_Σ := ρ^𝔇_{Σ,∅}. By Proposition 14.1, C^𝔇_{K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}} is a perfect complex of O[Δ_Q]-modules. This O[Δ_Q]-action agrees with the one given by the diamond operators ⟨d⟩_v, v ∈ Q. S is a finite set of primes containing T ∪ Q ∪ 𝔇, all primes dividing N_∅, and t. Standing assumption: ρ̄ arises, in the sense of Theorem 14.5, from a maximal ideal m of T^S(K^𝔇_∅) acting on H^1(X^𝔇_∅, ω_O) ≅ H^0(X^𝔇_∅, ω_{E/O})^∗. Finally, T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} := T^S(X^𝔇_{Σ,Q})_m, i.e. T^S(K^𝔇_{Σ,Q})_m.
items.note: The item consists of level data specific to the paper's patching: K_0^𝔇(N) and K_1^𝔇(N) ⊆ D_𝔇^×(Ẑ) with the auxiliary t², the intermediate subgroups K_Δ^𝔇(N) (ℓ-power index) and K_H^𝔇(N) (prime-to-ℓ index), K_{H,Δ}^𝔇(N, M), X_{Σ,Q}^𝔇, and the localized coherent Hecke algebras T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}. Shimura curves at these levels are instances of R18.1, and Taylor–Wiles auxiliary levels are planned in GL2ModularityLifting R22.2, but only for Betti/étale Hecke modules. Neither these subgroups nor the coherent Hecke algebras are planned. The §13 analogue is item level-subgroups-13-4 (cluster C7) and should be routed consistently with it. See sourceIssues E48, E49, E57, E60.

items.name: Theorem 14.6: Conjecture B in weight one (R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q})
items.statement: For any Σ ⊆ T, any Q, and 𝔇, the representations ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}: G_Q → GL_2(T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) from Theorem 14.5 (with K = K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) arise from the universal representation G_Q → GL_2(R^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) via surjections R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}. The printed text reads 'ρ^𝔇_Σ: G_F → GL_2(T^𝔇_Σ)', a misprint (sourceIssues E61); see also E57 on the determinant at Taylor–Wiles level. These satisfy: (1) tr ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}(Frob_v) = T_v for all v ∉ S. (2) There is a natural O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure on T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}, defined as in §13 via the full Hecke algebra, which makes R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} an O[Δ_Q]-algebra homomorphism. (3) For v ∈ Σ, let B_v ∈ T_Σ^{𝔇,□} be the image of B_v ∈ R_v^{uni(ε_v)} under R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ↪ R_{Σ,loc} → R_Σ^□ ↠ T_Σ^{𝔇,□} (printed with R_v^□). Then (B_v) = (ε_v√(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1}) U_v − 1) as ideals of T_Σ^{𝔇,□}. (4) For Σ_1 ⊆ Σ_2 ⊆ T the following squares commute: R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} → T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} over R^𝔇_Σ → T^𝔇_Σ, and R^𝔇_{Σ_2,Q} → T^𝔇_{Σ_2,Q} over R^𝔇_{Σ_1,Q} → T^𝔇_{Σ_1,Q}. Proof: a variant of the doubling method used for Theorem 14.5.
items.note: This is Conjecture B in weight one: surjections R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} with trace compatibility, the O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure, the ideal condition (B_v) = (ε_v√(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1})U_v − 1) at v ∈ Σ, and compatibility in Σ and Q. GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 plans deformation-to-Hecke maps only for weight ≥ 2 Betti/étale Hecke algebras. Nothing plans them for weight-one coherent Hecke algebras. The printed statement has ρ^𝔇_Σ: G_F → GL_2(T^𝔇_Σ) where ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}: G_Q → GL_2(T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) is meant (misprint, affects nothing). See sourceIssues E57, E61.

items.name: Proposition 14.7: self-duality of C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} and π_v ∘ π_v^† = q_vU_v² − ψ(ϕ_v)
items.statement: There are isomorphisms ϕ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}: C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ≅ (C^𝔇_{Σ,Q})^† in D_{T_{Σ,Q}}(O) compatible with C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ C^𝔇_Σ; for v ∈ T ∖ Σ the level-lowering map π_v: C^𝔇_{Σ∪{v},Q} → C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} and its adjoint satisfy π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ q_vU_v² − ψ(ϕ_v) and π_v^† ∘ π_v ≃ q_vU_v² − ψ(ϕ_v) up to units in the Hecke algebras.
items.note: This is the coherent analogue of Proposition 13.10. It needs the Serre-duality self-duality at Taylor–Wiles level (compatible with ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O) and the identity π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ q_vU_v² − ψ(ϕ_v), both ways round, for the coherent level-lowering maps. The (−)^† and adjoint formalism is algebra in the paper's §§10–11 (other clusters). The geometric duality and the degeneracy-map computation on weight-one coherent cohomology are planned nowhere; HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.4 plans degeneracy maps only for Betti/étale cohomology.

items.name: Proposition 14.8: Ihara's lemma for weight-one forms on Shimura curves
items.statement: (Analogue of Conjecture D.) For v ∈ Σ, the map H^0(π_v): H^0(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_{E/O})^∗_{m_Σ} → H^0(X_{Σ∖{v}}^𝔇, ω_{E/O})^∗_{m_{Σ∖{v}}} is surjective. This is H_0 of the localized level-lowering map π_v: C^𝔇_Σ → C^𝔇_{Σ∖{v}}. Proof: by duality it suffices that the kernel of H^0(X^𝔇_{Σ∖{v}}, ω_k)² → H^0(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_k) is Eisenstein, so that it vanishes after localizing at m_Σ; this is Diamond–Taylor [25, Prop. 5]. Also (analogue of Conjecture C, 14.3): coherent cohomology of a curve vanishes outside degrees 0 and 1, so H_i(C_K^𝔇 ⊗^L_O k) = 0 for i ∉ [0,1].
items.note: Ihara's lemma is planned in only two forms. ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 covers modular curves in Betti/étale form. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9 and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.3 give algebraic 'derived Ihara-avoidance' lemmas. The weight-one coherent statement on Shimura curves is not planned: the kernel of H^0(X^𝔇_{Σ∖{v}}, ω_k)² → H^0(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_k) is Eisenstein (Diamond–Taylor [25, Prop. 5]). The accompanying Conjecture C (amplitude [0,1]) needs only prop-14-1 and the planned Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B vanishing 'H²= 0 on a curve'.

items.name: Theorem 14.9 (Theorem H): integral R = T for weight-one forms on Shimura curves
items.statement: (Theorem 14.9 = Theorem H; proved in §15 as the Case (Wt1) instance of Theorem 15.1.) Setting of §14.2: ℓ > 3; 𝔇 is a finite set of primes of even cardinality with ℓ ∉ 𝔇 and v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ) for v ∈ 𝔇. In §14, 𝔇 ≠ ∅; for 𝔇 = ∅ the result is Calegari [16]. ρ̄ = ρ̄_m: G_Q → GL_2(k) has ρ̄|_{Q(ζ_ℓ)} absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_ℓ} unramified, with N_∅ = N(ρ̄) and ψ the Teichmüller lift of det ρ̄. T, Q and t are as in 14.2, and m is a (non-Eisenstein) maximal ideal of T^S(K^𝔇_∅) from which ρ̄ arises. Then for every Σ ⊆ T, the surjection R^𝔇_Σ ↠ T^𝔇_Σ of Theorem 14.6 is an isomorphism. Here T^𝔇_Σ = T^S(K^𝔇_Σ)_m is the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_O)_m ≅ H^0(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_{E/O})^∗_m, and R^𝔇_Σ is the global deformation ring of 12.2 (deformations of ρ̄_m with determinant ψ that are in particular unramified at ℓ). Theorem H (p. 8) reads: 'Let X_Σ^𝔇 be a Shimura curve arising from an indefinite quaternion algebra D_𝔇 over Q that ramifies only at a finite set of primes 𝔇 and assume ℓ > 3. Let T_Σ^𝔇 be the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_O)_m and R_Σ^𝔇 the corresponding deformation ring which parametrizes deformations of ρ̄_m that are in particular unramified at ℓ. The surjective map R_Σ^𝔇 ↠ T_Σ^𝔇 is an isomorphism.'
items.note: This is Theorem H, the main weight-one integral R = T theorem on Shimura curves. No layer plans an integral R = T for weight-one coherent cohomology: GL2ModularityLifting R22.x covers weight ≥ 2 Betti/étale settings, and ML.1 only registers 'weight-one modularity in proved cases'. Correction to the draft: as printed (p. 8, Theorem H; pp. 72–73), T^𝔇_Σ acts on the cohomology H^1(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_O)_m, which the paper identifies with H^0(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_{E/O})^*, i.e. H_0(C^𝔇_Σ). The draft's H_1(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_O) is by Serre duality the torsion-free H^0(X, ω_O), which is a different module.

items.name: Theorem 14.10 (Theorem I): a torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence in weight one
items.statement: Standing setting of §14: ℓ > 3; 𝔇 ≠ ∅ of even cardinality; ℓ ∉ 𝔇; v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ) for v ∈ 𝔇. Let ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) be a residual representation that arises from a maximal ideal m_𝔇 of the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_O), and assume ρ̄|_{Q(ζ_ℓ)} is irreducible. (1) ρ̄ also arises from a maximal ideal m_∅ of the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X^∅_{Σ∪𝔇}, ω_O). (2) Let Σ be any set of level-raising primes satisfying the conditions of 12.2. Let T^∅_{Σ∪𝔇} and T^𝔇_Σ be the Hecke algebras acting on H^1(X^∅_{Σ∪𝔇}, ω_O) and H^1(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_O), localized at m_∅ and m_𝔇 respectively. Then there is a natural surjection T^∅_{Σ∪𝔇} ↠ T^𝔇_Σ whose kernel is generated by q_vU_v² − ψ(Frob_v) for v ∈ 𝔇. Proof of (1): multiply by the Hasse invariant to reach weight ℓ. H^1(X_O, ω_O^{⊗ℓ}) = 0 lifts the class to a classical weight-ℓ form. Apply the classical Jacquet–Langlands correspondence to the modular curve, then level and weight optimisation there, using the companion forms of Gross [27] and Coleman–Voloch [21]. Proof of (2): Theorem 14.9 (for 𝔇) and Calegari [16] (for ∅) give R ≅ T at both levels; then compare R^∅_{Σ∪𝔇} → R^𝔇_Σ.
items.note: This is Theorem I, the torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence in weight one. It combines Theorem 14.9 and Calegari's 𝔇 = ∅ theorem (calegari-wt1) with three planned inputs: classical Jacquet–Langlands (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3), level and weight optimisation (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2/R20.3) and companion forms (item companion-forms, partly planned). It also uses the vanishing H^1(X_O, ω^{⊗ℓ}) = 0 for ℓ > 2, via Serre duality and Kodaira–Spencer. The torsion correspondence itself is planned nowhere. As printed (pp. 8, 73–74) the Hecke algebras act on H^1(X, ω_O), not the H_1 of the draft.

items.name: Remark 14.11: companion forms on Shimura curves would give the converse
items.statement: Suppose companion-form results were available for mod ℓ representations on Shimura curves, i.e. results lowering the weight from ℓ to 1 when the mod ℓ representation is unramified at ℓ, analogous to Gross [27] and Coleman–Voloch [21] on modular curves. Then one could show that if ρ̄ arises from H^1(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_O), it also arises from H^1(X^{𝔇′}_{Σ∪𝔇∖𝔇′}, ω_O) for all 𝔇′ ⊆ 𝔇, not just 𝔇′ = ∅. The lack of such results is also the obstruction to going from a maximal ideal m_∅ (printed 'm_Σ') of the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X^∅_{Σ∪𝔇}, ω_O) to a maximal ideal m_𝔇 of the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_O). This direction requires the necessary assumption that the primes in 𝔇 are level-raising primes for the ρ̄ arising from m_∅.
items.note: This is a conditional remark. Companion-form theorems for mod ℓ representations on Shimura curves (analogues of Gross [27] and Coleman–Voloch [21]) are not proved in the paper and not planned in the atlas. The converse of Theorem 14.10(1) and the passage to intermediate 𝔇′ ⊆ 𝔇 depend on them. It should be recorded as an open or conditional statement, not a formalisation target. The draft writes H_1(X, ω_O); the paper prints H^1(X, ω_O). See sourceIssues E62.

items.name: Proposition 15.2: Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Assume ρ̄_m|_{F(ζ_ℓ)} absolutely irreducible. There are integers r, g ≥ 1 such that for every n ≥ 1 there is a set Q_n of finite places with |Q_n| = r, Q_n ∩ (S ∪ T ∪ 𝔇) = ∅, Nm(v) ≡ 1 (mod ℓ^n) and ρ̄_m unramified with distinct eigenvalues of ρ̄_m(Frob_v) for v ∈ Q_n, and R_{loc,T} → R^□_{T,Q_n} extending to a surjection R_{loc,T}[[x_1, …, x_g]] ↠ R^□_{T,Q_n} (hence compatible surjections R_{loc,Σ}[[x_1,…,x_g]] ↠ R^□_{Σ,Q_n}); moreover dim R_{loc,T}[[x_1,…,x_g]] = dim R_{loc,T} + g = (1 + j + r) − ℓ_0. (Calegari–Geraghty [17, Prop. 5.2].)
items.note: The paper does not prove this; it cites Calegari–Geraghty [17, Prop. 5.2]. The atlas plans Taylor–Wiles auxiliary primes for global deformation problems over number fields at GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5, and the global-to-local presentation with its numerical terms at R04.6. Those layers are written against KW II, so their blueprint still has to record this form of the result: GL₂ over an arbitrary number field F; the T-framed local ring R_{loc,T}, which includes the level-raising places and the places in 𝔇; the hypothesis that ρ̄|_{F(ζ_ℓ)} is absolutely irreducible; and the positive-defect count dim = (1 + j + r) − ℓ₀, where ℓ₀ = r₂, or ℓ₀ = 1 for the weight-one problem unramified at ℓ. Neither library has it: Tau Ceti has only Chebotarev auxiliaries.

items.name: Patched rings R_{Σ,∞}, S∞, Λ_n = O[Δ_{Q_n}] and patching systems 𝔆_Σ
items.statement: Setup of §15 (Cases (PGL2) and (Wt1) in parallel). S is the set of finite places of F at which ρ̄_m ramifies or which divide ℓ, as in 12.2 (printed 'ρ̄_𝔭'). Set j := 4|S ∪ T ∪ 𝔇| − 1, so that R^□_Σ ≅ R_Σ[[w_1,…,w_j]] and R^□_{Σ,Q} ≅ R_{Σ,Q}[[w_1,…,w_j]] for all Σ ⊆ T and Q. Let r, g and Q_n be as in Proposition 15.2. For Σ ⊆ T set R_{Σ,∞} := R_{loc,Σ}[[x_1,…,x_g]] and S∞ := O[[y, w]] = O[[y_1,…,y_r, w_1,…,w_j]]. Then dim R_{Σ,∞} = dim S∞ − ℓ_0 = c + 1 for all Σ, where c := j + r − ℓ_0. For v ∈ T, let A_v, B_v ∈ R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ⊆ R_{T,∞} be the elements of Proposition 12.1 (R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ≅ O[[A_v,B_v,X_v,Y_v]]/(A_vB_v)). For Σ ⊆ T and v ∈ T∖Σ, R_{Σ∪{v},∞}/(A_v) = R_{Σ,∞}. For n ≥ 1, Λ_n := O⟦Δ_{Q_n}⟧ (= O[Δ_{Q_n}]). Since |Q_n| = r, Δ_{Q_n} ≅ ∏_{i=1}^r Z/ℓ^{e(i,n)}Z with integers e(i,n) ≥ n, so Λ_n = O[[y]]/I_n with I_n = ((1+y_i)^{ℓ^{e(i,n)}} − 1 : 1 ≤ i ≤ r) as in 10.1. Set R_{Σ,n} := R_{Σ,Q_n}, C_{Σ,n} := C_{Σ,Q_n}, R_{Σ,0} := R_Σ and C_{Σ,0} := C_Σ. C_{Σ,n} is regarded as an object of D_{R_{Σ,n}}(Λ_n) via R_{Σ,n} ↠ T_{Σ,Q_n} ↪ End_{D(Λ_n)}(C_{Σ,n}). α_{Σ,n}: C_{Σ,n} ⊗^L_{Λ_n} O ≅ C_{Σ,0} is the isomorphism of Proposition 13.9 (and its §14 analogue). H_*(k ⊗^L_{Λ_n} C_{Σ,n}) vanishes outside [d, d + ℓ_0], where d := r_1 + r_2 and ℓ_0 := r_2 in Case (PGL2) (by Conjecture C), and d := 0 and ℓ_0 := 1 in Case (Wt1).
items.note: The abstract ingredients are planned. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8 plans S_N as a finite quotient of O[Δ_N], S_∞ = O[[z]], the patched local deformation base R_∞ and the augmentation isomorphism; GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 and R04.6 plan the Taylor–Wiles data and dimensions; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.4 plans the analogous arithmetic verification for the ACC+ tower over CM fields. No layer plans this Σ-indexed family: R_{Σ,∞} = R_{loc,Σ}[[x]] over R_{T,∞}, with A_v, B_v ∈ R_v^{uni(ε_v)} and R_{Σ∪{v},∞}/(A_v) = R_{Σ,∞}, and the complexes C_{Σ,n} ∈ D_{R_{Σ,n}}(Λ_n) with α_{Σ,n}, built from the PGL₂/F arithmetic manifolds (Conjectures A–D) or the weight-one Shimura-curve complexes. Neither library has any patching, derived-action or deformation-ring construction. See sourceIssues E63.

items.name: Lemma 15.3: the patching systems 𝔆_Σ are self-dual
items.statement: For each Σ ⊆ T, 𝔆_Σ = (C_{Σ,n}, α_{Σ,n})_{n≥0} is a patching system, and there is an isomorphism of patching systems 𝔆_Σ^† ≅ 𝔆_Σ (printed 𝔆_Σ^∨; sourceIssues E12). Consequently M_{Σ,∞} := P(𝔆_Σ) is a self-dual maximal Cohen–Macaulay R_{T,∞}-module on which R_{T,∞} acts through R_{Σ,∞}, with M_{Σ,∞} ⊗_{S∞} O ≅ H_d(C_Σ) (Theorems 10.6, 11.3).
items.note: Abstract patching (P8) and the depth and amplitude conclusions (P9) are planned, and PA.4 plans the analogous 'is a patching system' check for the ACC+ tower. No layer plans compatibility of patching with Grothendieck duality (Theorem 11.3) or the arithmetic self-duality 𝔆_Σ^† ≅ 𝔆_Σ, which comes from Props. 13.6, 13.7 and 13.9, or from Prop. 14.7. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans only the finite-level Poincaré–Verdier duality that feeds Prop. 13.6. The printed 𝔆_Σ^∨ should be the dual patching system 𝔆_Σ^† (E12). See sourceIssues E12.

items.name: Proposition 15.5: patched level-lowering maps and π_v ∘ π_v^∨ = u_vB_v
items.statement: For Σ ⊆ T and v ∈ T ∖ Σ, the maps π_v: C_{Σ∪{v},n} → C_{Σ,n} induce a morphism 𝔆_{Σ∪{v}} → 𝔆_Σ and an R_{T,∞}-module map π_v: M_{Σ∪{v},∞} → M_{Σ,∞}, which is surjective (Conjecture D via Lemma 13.11, resp. Proposition 14.8, and Nakayama); with π_v^∨ the dual map under the self-dualities, there are units u_v, u′_v ∈ R_{T,∞}^× with π_v ∘ π_v^∨ = u_vB_v and π_v^∨ ∘ π_v = u′_vB_v.
items.note: The finite-level inputs belong to other clusters: the formulas π_v∘π_v^† = U_v² − 1 (Prop. 13.10) or q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v) (Prop. 14.7), Conjecture D via Lemma 13.11 or Prop. 14.8, and Conjecture B(3)/Theorem 14.6(3). No atlas layer plans patched level-lowering maps, their surjectivity by Nakayama, or the identities π_v∘π_v^∨ = u_vB_v and π_v^∨∘π_v = u′_vB_v in R_{T,∞}. The nearest plans are ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 (Ihara's lemma on modular curves), SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 (old/new sequences and congruence modules at finite level) and P9 (derived Ihara avoidance, the opposite strategy). See sourceIssues E55.

items.name: Lemma 15.6: level-raising maps are isomorphisms at the augmentation
items.statement: Choose an augmentation λ: R_{T,∞} ↠ R_{∅,∞} ↠ O with λ(A_v) = 0 and λ(B_v) ≠ 0 for all v ∈ T; then each (R_{Σ,∞}, λ) is in C_O(c) (p := Ker λ), µ := rank_p M_{∅,∞} ≥ 1 and M_{∅,∞} ≅ R_{∅,∞}^µ (Auslander–Buchsbaum). For each Σ ⊆ T and v ∈ T ∖ Σ, π_v: M_{Σ∪{v},∞} → M_{Σ,∞} is an isomorphism at p; in particular rank_p M_{Σ,∞} = µ for all Σ.
items.note: One ingredient is planned: the Auslander–Buchsbaum step M_{∅,∞} ≅ R_{∅,∞}^µ, for a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over the regular ring R_{∅,∞}. It sits in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3, and the R03.6 decomposition node has Calegari–Geraghty's 'formally smooth ⇒ free'. The choice of an augmentation λ with λ(A_v) = 0 and λ(B_v) ≠ 0, the membership (R_{Σ,∞}, λ) ∈ C_O(c), and the conclusion that π_v is an isomorphism at p with constant rank µ are planned nowhere. Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing, but no depth invariant, Auslander–Buchsbaum formula or maximal Cohen–Macaulay notion, and no proof that power-series rings over a DVR are regular.

items.name: The cotangent torsion of R_{Σ,∞}: Φ_{R_{Σ,∞}} ≅ ∏_{v∈Σ} O/λ(B_v)O
items.statement: Let λ: R_{T,∞} ↠ R_{∅,∞} ↠ O be the augmentation chosen before Lemma 15.6 (λ(A_v) = 0 and λ(B_v) ≠ 0 for all v ∈ T). For each Σ ⊆ T, §12.2 and Proposition 15.2 show that R_{Σ,∞} is a power series ring over ⊗̂_{v∈Σ} R_v^{uni(ε_v)}. By Proposition 12.1 it is therefore a power series ring over ⊗̂_{v∈Σ} O[[A_v, B_v]]/(A_vB_v). In particular R_{Σ,∞} is a complete intersection, Φ_{R_{Σ,∞}} ≅ ∏_{v∈Σ} O/λ(B_v)O, and length_O Φ_{R_{Σ,∞}} = Σ_{v∈Σ} ν_O(λ(B_v)).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 15.4, p. 79 (λ from p. 78)
items.note: Mathlib has I/I² (Ideal.Cotangent) and multivariate power series. It has no completed tensor product, no complete-intersection predicate and no torsion-of-cotangent invariant Φ_A.
