The atlas plans completed tensor products over O (R03.1) and 'the exact complete-intersection criteria used in patching' (R03.3), but neither Φ_A nor this computation. I checked the paper's 'easy computation' and it holds: with λ(A_v) = 0 and λ(B_v) = b_v ≠ 0, p/p² is spanned by the classes of A_v and B_v − b_v, subject to the single relation b_v·A_v ≡ A_vB_v = 0. So the torsion is ⊕_v O/b_v, and the power-series variables add free summands.

items.name: Theorem 15.4: patched modules have a free summand of constant rank
items.statement: There is an integer µ ≥ 1 such that for each Σ ⊆ T, M_{Σ,∞} ≅ R_{Σ,∞}^µ ⊕ W_{Σ,∞} for some R_{Σ,∞}-module W_{Σ,∞}. (Proof: by Proposition 4.4, Theorem 7.4 and Proposition 15.5, length_O Ψ_{R_{Σ,∞}}(M_{Σ,∞}) = µ Σ_{v∈Σ} ν_O(λ(B_v)) = µ · length_O Φ_{R_{Σ,∞}}, so δ_{R_{Σ,∞}}(M_{Σ,∞}) = 0; conclude by Theorems 9.2 and 9.5.)
items.note: This is the Wiles/Diamond induction on the level, run on the patched modules. It rests on the numerical criterion (Theorems 9.2 and 9.5), the change of congruence modules (Prop. 4.4) and invariance of domain (Theorem 7.4), all from the paper's commutative-algebra clusters, and no atlas layer plans a numerical-criterion or free-summand argument for patched modules. The nearest plans are GL2ModularityLifting R22.4 (non-minimal levels, integral R = T) and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6. Both follow KW II and Calegari–Geraghty support and component arguments, not congruence modules, and have ℓ₀ = 0 or characteristic-zero conclusions. Neither library has anything.

items.name: Theorem 15.1: integral non-minimal R = T with a free summand
items.statement: Setting (§15, pp. 75–76). Case (PGL2): F is a number field in which ℓ (> 2) is unramified; the notation of §13 is used and Conjectures A, B, C and D are assumed. m ⊆ T^S(K_0(N_∅)) is a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal with residue field k and N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅. T is a finite set of level-raising places as in §§12.2 and 13.6. For Σ ⊆ T, R_Σ ↠ T_Σ is the surjection of Conjecture B and C_Σ ∈ D_{T_Σ}(O). Here d = r_1 + r_2 and ℓ_0 = r_2, H_i(k ⊗^L_O C_Σ) = 0 for i ∉ [d, d+ℓ_0] (Conjecture C), and H_d(C_Σ) = H_{r_1+r_2}(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ}. Case (Wt1): F = Q and the notation of §14 is used (ℓ > 3, ℓ ∉ 𝔇, v ≢ 1 mod ℓ for v ∈ 𝔇; the discriminant 𝔇 is fixed and suppressed, with 𝔇 ≠ ∅ assumed for convenience). m ⊆ T^S(K^𝔇_∅) is a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal with residue field k and N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅, and R_Σ ↠ T_Σ is the surjection of Theorem 14.6. Here d = 0 and ℓ_0 = 1, H_i(k ⊗^L_O C_Σ) = 0 for i ∉ [0, 1], and H_0(C_Σ) = H^0(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_{E/O})^*_{m_Σ}. Theorem 15.1: Assume that ρ̄_m|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} is absolutely irreducible. Then there exists an integer µ ≥ 1 such that for each Σ ⊆ T there exist an R_Σ-module W_Σ and an isomorphism of R_Σ-modules H_d(C_Σ) ≅ R_Σ^µ ⊕ W_Σ. In particular, R_Σ acts faithfully on H_d(C_Σ), and so the map R_Σ ↠ T_Σ is an isomorphism for all Σ. (This is Theorem F in Case (PGL2) and Theorem H in Case (Wt1); it is deduced from Theorem 15.4.)
items.note: The theorem follows from Theorem 15.4 by specialising along S_∞ → O. Only the surjection R_{Σ,∞}/n ↠ R_Σ is justified in the paper (gap E13), but that surjection suffices for the conclusion. GL2ModularityLifting R22.4 plans non-minimal levels and an integral R = T strengthening, but for the KW II setting: ℓ₀ = 0 and Hilbert or quaternionic modules. No layer plans R = T for the torsion homology of PGL₂/F arithmetic manifolds (Case PGL2) or for weight-one coherent cohomology of Shimura curves (Case Wt1, Theorem H). Neither library has any R = T statement. The isomorphism R_{Σ,∞} ⊗_{S∞} O ≅ R_Σ asserted before Theorem 15.4 is only a consequence (sourceIssues E13).

items.name: Theorem F: integral R = T in positive defect for PGL_2 over a number field (conditional)
items.statement: Standing assumptions (Introduction p. 6; §§12–13): F is a number field in which ℓ is unramified. ρ̄_m, Σ ⊆ T (T a finite set of level-raising places as in §§12.2 and 13.6) and N_Σ are as in §13, and Y_0(N_Σ) carries auxiliary level structure at a prime t ∤ N_Σ (Lemma 13.5). Theorem F: Assume Conjectures A, B, C and D hold for F and assume ℓ > 3. Let m be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T(K_0(N_∅)) such that N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅ and ρ̄_m|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} is absolutely irreducible. Then there exists an integer µ ≥ 1 such that for all Σ there is an isomorphism of R_Σ-modules H_{r_1+r_2}(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ} ≅ R_Σ^µ ⊕ W_Σ for some R_Σ-module W_Σ. In particular, R_Σ acts faithfully on H_{r_1+r_2}(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ}, and so the map R_Σ ↠ T_Σ from Conjecture B is an isomorphism for all Σ.
items.locator: Theorem F, Introduction p. 7 (standing assumption p. 6; = Theorem 15.1, Case (PGL2))
items.note: This is Case (PGL2) of Theorem 15.1, conditional on Conjectures A, B, C and D, with the Introduction's extra hypothesis ℓ > 3. No atlas layer states conditional R = T theorems for PGL₂ over an arbitrary number field. The conjectural inputs themselves are the cluster C7 items. Neither library has anything. For F with a real place see sourceIssues E65.

items.name: Theorem G: integral R = T for Bianchi manifolds assuming Conjecture B
items.statement: Standing assumption (Introduction p. 6): ℓ is unramified in F. Let F be an imaginary quadratic field and assume Conjecture B holds for F. Let m be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T(K_0(N_∅)) such that N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅ and ρ̄_m|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} is absolutely irreducible. For ℓ > 20 there exists an integer µ ≥ 1 such that for all Σ (Σ ⊆ T as in §13) there is an isomorphism of R_Σ-modules H_1(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ} ≅ R_Σ^µ ⊕ W_Σ for some R_Σ-module W_Σ. In particular, R_Σ acts faithfully on H_1(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ}, and so the map R_Σ ↠ T_Σ from Conjecture B is an isomorphism for all Σ. (This is deduced from Theorem F. Conjecture A holds by Newton–Thorne [45, Theorem 1.3] for ℓ sufficiently large, and ℓ > 20 suffices when [F:Q] = 2 (footnote 1, citing [45, (1.2)]). Conjecture C holds because Y_K is a 3-manifold and H_i(Y_K, k)_m = 0 for i = 0, 3 when m is non-Eisenstein. Conjecture D is Theorem 13.12, which needs ℓ > 3.)
items.locator: Theorem G and footnote 1, Introduction pp. 7–8 (standing assumption p. 6)
items.note: This is Theorem F for imaginary quadratic F. Conjecture A comes from Newton–Thorne [45, Thm 1.3] (ℓ > 20), Conjecture C is automatic for 3-manifolds and Conjecture D is Theorem 13.12; the theorem remains conditional on Conjecture B. The atlas plans neither Bianchi R = T nor Newton–Thorne's torsion Galois representations in the derived category: TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure builds the library under Scholze's theorem but 'not … its final Galois-representation theorem', and ACC+'s nilpotent-ideal local–global compatibility is infrastructure only. Neither library has anything. See sourceIssues E64: the cited Newton–Thorne theorems do not give Conjecture A(ii) for trivial coefficients.

items.name: Derived Hom and tensor, Ext and Tor over A, D^b(mod A)
items.statement: For a ring A: the derived category D(A), RHom_A(−,−), − ⊗^L_A −, Ext^i_A = H^i RHom_A, Tor^A_i = H_i(− ⊗^L_A −), suspension [−], and D^b(mod A) (complexes with bounded, finitely generated homology). Used throughout, e.g. RHom_A(O, M) ≅ RHom_B(B ⊗^L_A O, M) for B-modules M (adjunction), RHom_A(B, X) ≅ (B ⊗^L_A X)[−1] when B = A/fA with f a non-zero-divisor, and the tensor evaluation RHom_A(P, A) ⊗^L_A M ≅ RHom_A(P, M) for P perfect.
items.note: Mathlib has D(A) (`DerivedCategory` with shift), Ext between modules, and Tor as a left-derived functor on modules; its Tor docstring says 'For now we have almost nothing to say about it!'. RHom and ⊗^L on D(A) are not in the libraries (P7 audit). They are planned by tauceti DGAInfinity layer 5 (derived Hom, derived tensor, derived extension ⊣ restriction), which gives the adjunction RHom_A(O,M) ≅ RHom_B(B ⊗^L O, M). P7 plans derived tensor products and duals of perfect complexes over complete local O-algebras (tensor evaluation for perfect P). D^b(mod R) is used in tauceti StablePeriodicCurved layer 2. The identity RHom_A(A/f,X) ≅ (A/f ⊗^L X)[−1] for a non-zero-divisor f is not stated anywhere and must be proved by the consumer.

items.name: Regular local rings and the facts used about them
items.statement: A noetherian local ring R with maximal ideal m and residue field κ is regular if edim R := dim_κ m/m² equals dim R (always dim R ≤ edim R) [13, §2.2]. Facts used, for R a regular local ring: (a) for 0 ≠ f ∈ m, R/fR is regular iff f ∉ m², and then dim R/fR = dim R − 1 ([13, Prop. 2.2.4]); (b) κ has a finite free (Koszul) resolution, so RHom_R(κ, R) ⊗^L_R N ≃ RHom_R(κ, N) for every R-module N, and RHom_R(κ, R) ≃ κ[−dim R] (proof of Lemma 2.6); (c) Ext*_R(κ, κ) is the exterior algebra on Ext^1_R(κ, κ) ([28, p. 110], used in 6.6); (d) R is a domain, Cohen–Macaulay and a complete intersection; (e) a finitely generated R-module of depth ≥ dim R is free (Auslander–Buchsbaum). The ranks rank_{A_p} M_p used in the paper make sense because A_{p_A} is a domain.
items.note: The definition (edim = dim) is in Mathlib, but the facts used are mostly absent. Partly planned: Cohen–Macaulay and complete-intersection properties, Auslander–Buchsbaum and 'regular iff finite global dimension' in R03.3; Koszul complexes with their exactness in IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6. Planned nowhere: R/fR regular iff f ∉ m² with dim R/fR = dim R − 1 (BH 2.2.4); regular local rings are domains; RHom_R(κ,R) ≃ κ[−dim R]; and Gulliksen–Levin, Ext*_R(κ,κ) ≅ ⋀ Ext¹_R(κ,κ) (Mathlib has `ExteriorAlgebra`, but no Ext-algebra statement). The status is missing because those parts are neither in the libraries nor in any layer.

items.name: The Auslander–Buchsbaum formula and consequences
items.statement: For a noetherian local ring R and a nonzero finitely generated R-module M of finite projective dimension, projdim_R M + depth_R M = depth R ([13, Theorem 1.3.3]). Consequences used: (i) over a regular local ring of dimension c, every finitely generated module of depth ≥ c is free. This is applied to M_{p_A} over A_{p_A} in Lemma 3.1(3) and Introduction p. 4, and in §15 to get M_{∅,∞} ≅ R_{∅,∞}^µ. (ii) If a finitely generated module H over a local ring S has a finite free resolution of length ≤ ℓ, then depth_S H ≥ depth S − ℓ; this gives depth_S H_0(C) ≥ dim R in Lemma 10.7.
items.locator: Lemma 3.1(3), p. 18; Introduction p. 4; Lemma 10.7, p. 48; §15, p. 78 (citing [13, Thm 1.3.3])
items.note: Neither library has the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula (AUDIT-17: 'Absent') or depth; Mathlib has projective dimension and pd_R(R/(x)) = n for a regular sequence. The formula is planned explicitly in R03.3 and in its accepted decomposition node. That node also plans 'regular iff finite global dimension', which is how the consequence 'over a regular local ring of dimension c, depth ≥ c ⇒ free' follows. The depth bound of Lemma 10.7 from a finite free complex is the same formula applied to H_0.

items.name: Prime avoidance (including the coset form)
items.statement: If an ideal I of a commutative ring is contained in a finite union of ideals P_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ P_n, all but at most two of them prime, then I ⊆ P_i for some i (Kaplansky [36, Theorem 81]); and if x ∈ R, J an ideal and (x) + J is not contained in any of the primes P_1, …, P_n, then x + j ∉ P_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ P_n for some j ∈ J ([36, Theorem 124]; [13, Lemma 1.2.2]).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 3.5, Theorem 5.6, Lemma 9.4, Theorem 9.6 (citing [36, Thms 81, 124])
items.note: The first form (Kaplansky Thm 81: at most two non-prime ideals allowed) is exactly `Ideal.subset_union_prime`. The coset form (Kaplansky Thm 124; BH Lemma 1.2.2), 'if (x) + J ⊄ P_i for all i then x + j ∉ ⋃ P_i for some j ∈ J', is in neither library and in no layer. Lemma 3.5 uses only the first form; the coset form is cited in Thm 5.6, Lemma 9.4 and Thm 9.6 (other clusters). The status is missing because of the coset form.

items.name: Minimal free complexes over local rings
items.statement: Over a noetherian local ring Λ, every perfect complex (every complex in D^b(mod Λ) of finite Tor-amplitude) is quasi-isomorphic to a minimal bounded complex of finite free modules, unique up to isomorphism; a quasi-isomorphism between minimal free complexes is an isomorphism; the ranks satisfy rank_Λ C_i = dim_k H_i(k ⊗_Λ C) (Roberts [47, Ch. 2, Thm 2.4]).
items.note: P7 plans minimal representatives over local rings, and its node gives minimal complexes with terms R^{d_i}, d_i = dim_κ H^i(K ⊗^L κ), unique up to isomorphism. The paper also uses, for α_n on p. 45, that every quasi-isomorphism between minimal complexes is an isomorphism (Roberts, Ch. 2, Thm 2.4); the P7 blueprint should state this explicitly. The libraries have near misses only: Tau Ceti's IsMinimalProjectivePresentation (two terms, unique up to isomorphism, existence only over semiprimary rings) and Mathlib's criterion that a quasi-isomorphism of K-projective complexes is a homotopy equivalence. AUDIT-17 records minimal complexes of arbitrary length as absent.

items.name: Limits of compatible systems of perfect complexes (Khare–Thorne)
items.statement: Given a compatible system of minimal finite free complexes C(m^s S∞, ∞) over the finite quotients S∞/m^s with S∞/a ⊗ C(b, ∞) ≅ C(a, ∞) for b ⊆ a, C∞ := lim_s C(m^s S∞, ∞) is a minimal complex of finite free S∞-modules with S∞/a ⊗ C∞ ≅ C(a, ∞), H_i(C∞) ≅ lim_s H_i(C(m^s S∞, ∞)), and End_{D(S∞)}(C∞) ≅ lim_a End_{D(S∞/a)}(C(a, ∞)); morphisms of systems lift uniquely up to homotopy (Khare–Thorne [38, Lemmas 2.13, 2.14]). Also used to build C_K^𝔇 from the finite-level complexes (Proposition 14.1).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 10.6, pp. 45–46; Proposition 14.1 (citing [38, Lemmas 2.13, 2.14])
items.note: P8's ACC+ §6.4 node states this: C_∞ is the limit of minimal complexes over the finite quotients, with C_∞ ⊗ S_∞/J ≅ C(J, ∞) and End_{D(S_∞)}(C_∞) = lim End(C(J, ∞)). P7 plans passing to inverse limits so that morphisms, homotopies and Hecke actions survive. Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.13 itself is a recorded unread gap of P7 and P8. The use in Proposition 14.1, building C_K^𝔇, is the same lemma. Neither library has lim¹, derived limits or inverse limits of complexes (AUDIT-17).

items.name: The classical Jacquet–Langlands correspondence (input to Theorem 14.10)
items.statement: (External input; the paper cites it only by name.) As used in the proof of Theorem 14.10(1): a classical weight-ℓ Hecke eigenform f on the Shimura curve X^𝔇, with K_q maximal at q ∈ 𝔇, is sent by the classical Jacquet–Langlands correspondence to a classical weight-ℓ eigenform f_∅ on the modular curve X^∅_𝔇. f_∅ has level divisible by the primes of 𝔇, is new (special) there, and has the same Hecke eigenvalues away from the level, hence the same residual representation ρ̄. Paper's wording (p. 74): 'we can now apply the classical Jacquet–Langlands correspondence to f and get a classical weight ℓ form f_∅ on X^∅_𝔇 with residual representation ρ̄'.
items.note: R17.3, narrowed but kept by RS-21, plans global quaternionic transfer and its converse, preserving Hecke eigenvalues at split places, with 'the definite and indefinite cases needed by R18/R22'; this is the correspondence used. Moving between weight-ℓ sections of ω^{⊗ℓ} on X^𝔇 and automorphic representations of D_𝔇^× uses AutomorphicBundles B4's generic definition of classical forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions. B4's worked examples are GL₂, Hilbert, Siegel and unitary; the quaternionic instance is not spelled out. PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 likewise recorded Jacquet–Langlands as planned at R17.1/R17.3, and neither library has it (AUDIT-14).

items.name: Companion forms and weight lowering for mod ℓ modular forms unramified at ℓ (Gross; Coleman–Voloch)
items.statement: (External input, cited.) Companion forms and weight lowering on modular curves (Gross [27], Coleman–Voloch [21]), as used in the proof of Theorem 14.10(1). If an irreducible ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) (ℓ > 2) arises from a mod ℓ eigenform of weight ℓ and level prime to ℓ on a modular curve, and ρ̄ is unramified at ℓ, then ρ̄ arises from a mod ℓ (Katz) eigenform of weight 1 (of the same prime-to-ℓ level). The paper states only that these results are used 'to lower the weight from ℓ to 1 using that the mod ℓ representation ρ̄ that f_∅ gives rise to is unramified at ℓ'. The exact hypotheses of [27] and [21] are not recorded in the paper.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 14.10(1) and Remark 14.11, p. 74 (citing [27], [21])
items.note: Gross's companion-form theorem enters the atlas through Edixhoven's Theorem 4.5. RS-06 and the reviewed AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4 node assign its proof to SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3. That gives the weight-one conclusion k(ρ̄) = 1 only when ρ̄ is non-exceptional, i.e. ρ̄|G_ℓ is not an extension of an unramified character by itself. The exceptional case (Frob_ℓ acting by a scalar) is needed by Theorem 14.10(1) and supplied by Coleman–Voloch [21] for ℓ > 2, but it is not planned; R20.5 even says 'Do not claim this layer proves the general Katz weight-one refinement'. Suggest splitting: Gross's non-exceptional case is planned at R20.3; Coleman–Voloch is missing.

items.name: Level and weight optimisation on modular curves (input to Theorem 14.10)
items.statement: (External input.) As used in the proof of Theorem 14.10(1): start from the classical weight-ℓ form f_∅ on the modular curve X^∅_𝔇 with residual representation ρ̄ (irreducible and unramified at ℓ). Level optimisation (down to the Serre conductor N(ρ̄)) and weight optimisation from ℓ to 1 via companion forms ([27], [21]) produce a maximal ideal m_∅ of the weight-one Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X^∅_{Σ∪𝔇}, ω_O) that gives rise to ρ̄. Paper's wording: 'One can then apply level and weight optimization on the modular curve to get the desired maximal ideal m_∅ producing ρ̄.'
items.note: R20.2 plans level lowering to the prime-to-ℓ Artin conductor (Mazur, Ribet, Diamond). R20.3, as narrowed by RS-06, plans Edixhoven/Serre weight optimisation under a supplied modularity witness, here the weight-ℓ form f_∅, and R20.5 assembles the two. The last step to weight one is item companion-forms, of which only the non-exceptional case is planned. So is the maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra on H^1(X^∅_{Σ∪𝔇}, ω_O) that the item ends with, which needs the Part II's weight-one objects. Correction: the draft writes H_1(X^∅_{Σ∪𝔇}, ω_O); the paper prints H^1.

items.name: Calegari's non-minimal weight-one modularity lifting on modular curves (the case 𝔇 = ∅)
items.statement: For modular curves (𝔇 = ∅), Theorem H was proved by Calegari [16]: with ℓ > 3, the surjections R^∅_Σ ↠ T^∅_Σ are isomorphisms, where T^∅_Σ is the Hecke algebra acting on H^1(X^∅_Σ, ω_O)_m. The proof uses the q-expansion principle to show that, in the non-minimal patched situation, M_∞ is not only faithful over R_∞ but free over the patched Hecke algebra, hence free over R_∞. This argument does not work for Shimura curves, which have no cusps. The result is used in the case 𝔇 = ∅, at level Σ ∪ 𝔇, in the proof of Theorem 14.10(2).
items.locator: Introduction p. 8; §14 opening p. 67; proof of Theorem 14.10(2), p. 74 (citing [16])
items.note: Calegari [16] (J. Reine Angew. Math. 740 (2018), 41–62) proves R^∅_Σ ≅ T^∅_Σ in weight one on modular curves for ℓ > 3. He uses q-expansions to show the patched module is free over the patched Hecke algebra. No layer plans it: ML.1's 'weight-one modularity in proved cases' is a registry that names no such source, and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1–R15.3 plan only the Katz-form and q-expansion inputs on modular curves. The Hecke module is H^1(X^∅_Σ, ω_O)_m (printed H^1), not the H_1 of the draft.

items.name: Regularity of A detected by Φ_A and Ψ_A (Iyengar–Khare–Manning–Urban)
items.statement: (Iyengar–Khare–Manning–Urban [34, Theorem 2.6], cited but not proved in this paper.) For (A, λ_A) in C_O, A is regular if and only if Φ_A = 0, if and only if Ψ_A(A) = 0 (Introduction p. 4; restated before Theorem 9.5, p. 40).
items.locator: Introduction p. 4; restated before Theorem 9.5, p. 40
items.note: Cited, not proved here: Iyengar–Khare–Manning–Urban, PNAS 121 (2024), Theorem 2.6. The paper quotes it before Theorem 9.5 as the global counterpart of Theorem 2.5; it is used in no proof. Missing from both libraries and the atlas.

items.name: Localization of Ext^i_A(O, −) at p_A and ranks of F^i_A
items.statement: Let λ_A: A → O be as in 2.2, p := p_A, and k(p) := Frac(O), which is also the residue field of A_p. For every finitely generated A-module M and every integer i there is an isomorphism of k(p)-vector spaces Ext^i_A(O, M)_p ≅ Ext^i_{A_p}(k(p), M_p). Hence rank_O F^i_A(M) = dim_{k(p)} Ext^i_{A_p}(k(p), M_p). A map of finitely generated O-modules has nonzero rank iff its localization at p is nonzero, and a map between torsion-free O-modules that is injective after localizing at p is injective. Consequences recorded in the paper: (a) Ext^i_A(O, O) has nonzero rank for 0 ≤ i ≤ c, because Ext^i_{A_p}(k(p), k(p)) ≠ 0 there ('This observation will be used in what follows', p. 14). (b) If A is regular at p and M_p is free of rank µ, then F^c_A(M) is free of rank µ, µ = rank_O (M/p_A M)^tf, and F^c_A(λ_A(M)) is injective.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 2.5 (p. 14), Lemma 2.6 (p. 15), Lemma 3.7 (p. 20), Lemma 3.10(1) (p. 20)
items.note: Used implicitly throughout §§2–3 (Theorem 2.5, Lemmas 2.6, 3.7, 3.10). Mathlib has Ext over ModuleCat and localization of modules but no compatibility of Ext with localization in this form; missing.

items.name: Ext^c_A(O, M^∨) as the O-dual of (M/p_A M)^tf
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a Cohen–Macaulay A-module of dimension c + 1. There are natural isomorphisms Ext^c_A(O, M^∨) ≅ Hom_{D(A)}(O, M^∨[c]) ≅ Hom_{D(A)}(O, ω_A(M)[−1]) ≅ Hom_{D(A)}(M[1], ω_A(O)) ≅ Hom_{D(A)}(M[1], O[1]) ≅ Hom_A(M, O) ≅ Hom_O(M/p_A M, O) ≅ Hom_O((M/p_A M)^tf, O). The third is a composition of two adjunctions; the fourth uses ω_A(O) ≅ O[1]. Hence Hom_O(Ext^c_A(O, M^∨), F^c_A(O)) ≅ F^c_A(O) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf. Under this identification, the map adjoint to (4.6) is the map Ext^c_A(O, M) → F^c_A(O) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf induced by M → M/p_A M.
items.note: The computation behind Proposition 4.7 (proof, p. 23), using ω_A(O) ≅ O[1]. Missing: needs the dualizing complex and CM duals (routed to R03.3).

items.name: RHom_A(O, A) for Gorenstein A in C_O(c)
items.statement: If A in C_O(c) is Gorenstein, then RHom_A(O, A) ≅ Ext^c_A(O, A)[−c], i.e. Ext^i_A(O, A) = 0 for i ≠ c, and Ext^c_A(O, A) ≅ O. Consequently, for a finitely generated A-module M, Tor^A_{−i}(M, RHom_A(O, A)) = 0 for i ≥ c + 1, and Tor^A_{−c}(M, RHom_A(O, A)) ≅ Ext^c_A(O, A) ⊗_A M.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.9, p. 24 (printed with ω_A(O) and 'i ≤ c + 1'; see E8)
items.note: Input to Proposition 4.9 (proof, p. 24), where it is printed with ω_A(O) and 'i ≤ c + 1' (sourceIssues E8). Missing; for Gorenstein A it follows from Avramov–Henriques–Şega [3, Thm 2.5(4)]-type vanishing, which the paper cites in 6.12.

items.name: Short exact sequences of Cohen–Macaulay modules of dimension c+1 dualize to short exact sequences
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and 0 → L → M → N → 0 an exact sequence of A-modules induced by a surjection π: M → N, with M, N Cohen–Macaulay of dimension c + 1 and π not an isomorphism. Then c + 1 ≤ depth_A L ≤ dim L ≤ dim M = c + 1, so L is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension c + 1. The sequence induces an exact sequence 0 → N^∨ → M^∨ → L^∨ → 0, whose first map is π^∨.
items.note: The structural step of Proposition 4.4 (proof, p. 22). General Cohen–Macaulay duality (Bruns–Herzog §3.3); missing from both libraries.

items.name: Claim in Lemma 9.4: nonzero η̃_N forces a free summand
items.statement: Let S be a Gorenstein local ring with residue field k and Krull dimension c, and let N be a maximal Cohen–Macaulay S-module. If the natural map η̃_N: Ext^c_S(k, S) ⊗_S N → Ext^c_S(k, N) is nonzero, then N has a free S-summand. Proof as in the paper: take x in m_S regular on S and on N (of length c), set S' = S/xS and N' = N/xN. [13, Lemma 3.1.16] identifies η̃_N with Soc(S') ⊗_{S'} N' → Soc(N'), so Soc(S')N' ≠ 0. Choosing a ∈ N' with Soc(S')a ≠ 0, the map S' → N', 1 ↦ a, is split injective, and Lemma 9.3 lifts the summand from N' to N.
items.note: The dimension-reduction core of Lemma 9.4 (the 'Claim', p. 39). Missing. The sequence x must have length r = c = dim S (sourceIssues).

items.name: Change of rings modulo x with λ(x) = ϖ (reduction in Lemma 9.4)
items.statement: Let λ: R → O be surjective and x ∈ R with λ(x) = ϖ, x a non-zero-divisor on R and on M; set S := R/xR. For an S-module V, Ext^n_R(O, V) ≅ Ext^n_S(k, V) by adjunction, since O ⊗^L_R S ≃ k. For an R-module U on which x is a non-zero-divisor, U → U/xU induces maps Ext^n_R(O, U) → Ext^n_S(k, U/xU), natural in U and compatible with η̃_R and η̃_S. If M is maximal Cohen–Macaulay with M_p ≠ 0 (p = Ker λ, c = height p), then Ext^c_R(O, M) ≠ 0 by localizing at p. Moreover Ext^c_R(O, M) → Ext^c_S(k, M/xM) is nonzero: its kernel is ϖ·Ext^c_R(O, M), so Nakayama's lemma applies.
items.note: The reduction in the proof of Lemma 9.4 (p. 39): the choice of x uses coset prime avoidance (item prime-avoidance). Missing.

items.name: Additivity of the Wiles defect; modules not supported at p_A
items.statement: For A in C_O(c) and finitely generated A-modules M, N: δ_A(M ⊕ N) = δ_A(M) + δ_A(N), so δ_A(A^µ ⊕ W) = µ·δ_A(A) + δ_A(W). If W_{p_A} = 0, then Ψ_A(W) = 0 and δ_A(W) = 0 (the paper cites Lemma 3.7).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.2, p. 40 (converse direction, via Lemma 3.7)
items.note: Used in the converse of Theorem 9.2 and in Theorem 9.6 (p. 40). Missing.

items.name: Quasi-complete intersection homomorphisms and the facts cited from Avramov–Henriques–Şega
items.statement: In the sense of [3, 1.1], the surjection λA: A → O is quasi-complete intersection exactly when condition (c) of Proposition 6.11 holds. That is, H1(A⟨X⟩) is a free O-module and the natural map ∧_O H1(A⟨X⟩) → H*(A⟨X⟩) is bijective, where A⟨X⟩ is the Koszul complex on the minimal generators t of pA. Results cited: since O is a complete intersection, λA is quasi-complete intersection if and only if A is a complete intersection ([3, Proposition 7.7]). If A and O are complete intersections, λA is quasi-complete intersection, and for A in C_O(c), Ext^i_A(O, A) ≅ O for i = c and 0 otherwise ([3, Theorem 2.5(4)]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.11, (c)⇔(a), p. 31; 6.12, p. 31 (citing [3, 1.1], [3, Proposition 7.7], [3, Theorem 2.5(4)])
items.note: Avramov–Henriques–Şega, Pure Appl. Math. Q. 9 (2013), 1.1, Prop. 7.7, Thm 2.5(4), as cited in Proposition 6.11 and 6.12. Missing from the libraries and the atlas.

items.name: Γ-derivations on DG algebras with divided powers (Iyengar [32, 1.1, Prop. 1.4])
items.statement: The acyclic closure A⟨U⟩ is a DG A-algebra with divided powers. A Γ-derivation θ: A⟨U⟩ → A⟨U⟩, in the sense of [32, 1.1], is an A-linear graded derivation compatible with the divided powers. In [32] such derivations commute with the differential up to the usual sign, which for the degree −1 maps of 6.3 is condition (b), dθ + θd = 0. Iyengar [32, Proposition 1.4] is the result used to extend prescribed values θi(xj) = δij on X to Γ-derivations of the whole of A⟨U⟩. The paper does not reproduce the Leibniz and divided-power rules; see [32, 1.1].
items.note: Iyengar, Proc. AMS 129 (2001), 1.1 and Proposition 1.4, as used in 6.3. Missing: Mathlib's DividedPowerAlgebra is ungraded and has no DG structure or Γ-derivations.

items.name: Height, grade and dimension in the Cohen–Macaulay ring P = O[[t]]
items.statement: P = O[[t1, …, tn]] is regular, hence Cohen–Macaulay, of dimension n + 1. For any ideal I of P: height I = grade(I, P), the length of any maximal P-regular sequence in I; and height I = dim P − dim P/I ([13, Corollary 2.1.4]). In particular, for A = P/I, height I = n + 1 − dim A.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 5.3 (p. 24) and Theorem 5.6 (p. 25), citing [13, Corollary 2.1.4]
items.note: Bruns–Herzog Cor. 2.1.4, used in Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.6. R03.3 plans Cohen–Macaulay rings with their 'depth and dimension formulas'; height = grade in Cohen–Macaulay rings is the standard entry. Mathlib has only Krull-type inequalities.

items.name: The classes of the θi form a basis of Ext^1_A(O,O), and ξA(Λ^c) = F^c_A(O)
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c), c ≥ 1, with relations of the form (5.4), and let θi (n−c+1 ≤ i ≤ n) be as in 6.3. Then the classes [θi] form a basis of the free O-module Ext^1_A(O, O) = F^1_A(O) = Λ^1, where Λ := ∧_O F^1_A(O). Consequently, by Lemma 6.5 applied to θA, ξA(Λ^c) = F^c_A(O). Moreover ξA becomes bijective after localising at pA (tensoring with Frac O, since A_{pA} is regular), so ξA is injective with O-torsion cokernel. The paper asserts the basis claim without proof. It checks out: in Hom_A(A⟨U⟩, O) the degree-1 cocycles are the functionals f on ⊕ A xj with Σ_j ukj f(xj) = 0, which under (5.4) means f(xk) = 0 for k ≤ n − c; the coboundaries are 0; and ε∘θi = xi*.
items.note: The step of Theorem 6.8(2) (pp. 29–30) turning Lemma 6.5 into bijectivity of ξ_A; asserted in the paper without proof and checked here (the degree-1 cocycles of Hom_A(A⟨U⟩, O) are the functionals vanishing on the torsion classes of (5.4)). Missing.

items.name: Ext^c comparison along a surjection in C_O(c) (key step of Theorem 7.4)
items.statement: Let ϕ: A → B be a surjective map in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated B-module. (a) ϕ_{p_A}: A_{p_A} → B_{p_B} is an isomorphism: it is a surjection of regular local rings of the same dimension c. (b) The kernel of Ext^c_B(O, M) → Ext^c_A(O, M) is O-torsion, so F^c_ϕ(M): F^c_B(M) → F^c_A(M) is injective, with no hypothesis on M. (c) If depth_B M ≥ c, then Ext^c_B(O, M) → Ext^c_A(O, M) is surjective, so F^c_ϕ(M) is bijective. Proof of (c): RHom_A(O, M) ≅ RHom_B(B ⊗^L_A O, M), and the map is induced by B ⊗^L_A O → O. Take the exact triangle J → B ⊗^L_A O → O → J[1] in D(B). Then H_i(J) = 0 for i ≤ 0, and H_i(J) is O-torsion for all i, hence m_B-power torsion since the B-action factors through λ_B. Depth ≥ c gives Ext^i_B(W, M) = 0 for i ≤ c − 1 and every m_B-power-torsion W, so Ext^i_B(J, M) = 0 for i ≤ c. (d) F^c_B(M/p_B M) → F^c_A(M/p_A M) is bijective for every M, by (2.4) and Proposition 6.10. Hence both horizontal maps of (7.2) with i = c are bijective.
items.note: The substance of the proof of Theorem 7.4 (pp. 32–33). Missing.

items.name: Change of rings modulo an A-regular element: F^i_A(X) ≅ F^{i−1}_B(B ⊗^L_A X)
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c), f ∈ p_A a non-zero-divisor on A, and B := A/fA. Since 0 → A →f A → 0 is a finite free resolution of B, for every A-complex X there are natural isomorphisms RHom_A(B, X) ≅ RHom_A(B, A) ⊗^L_A X ≅ (B ⊗^L_A X)[−1] in D(B), and RHom_A(O, X) ≅ RHom_B(O, RHom_A(B, X)) ≅ RHom_B(O, (B ⊗^L_A X)[−1]). Hence F^i_A(X) ≅ F^{i−1}_B(B ⊗^L_A X) for every integer i, naturally in X. If f is also a non-zero-divisor on an A-module M, then B ⊗^L_A M → H_0(B ⊗^L_A M) ≅ M/fM is a quasi-isomorphism, so F^i_A(M) ≅ F^{i−1}_B(M/fM).
items.note: Proof of Theorem 8.2, p. 36. Missing: RHom and ⊗^L on D(A) are planned in P7 and tauceti DGAInfinity layer 5, this consequence is not.

items.name: Claim: Coker(η_N) ≅ Coker(η_M), and reduction of Theorem 8.2 to M = A
items.statement: In the setting of 8.1, suppose f is also a non-zero-divisor on A. Let B = A/fA and N = M/fM. Since f ∈ p_A, the surjection M → N induces M/p_A M ≅ N/p_B N, so rank_{A_{p_A}}(M_{p_A}) = rank_{B_{p_B}}(N_{p_B}) (8.9). The isomorphisms F^c_A(A) ⊗_O (M/p_A M)^tf ≅ F^{c−1}_B(B) ⊗_O (N/p_B N)^tf and F^c_A(M) ≅ F^{c−1}_B(N) (previous item) commute with η_M and η_N of (3.6). Hence Coker(η_N) ≅ Coker(η_M) as O-modules. With Lemma 3.7, δ_A(M) = δ_B(N) reduces to δ_A(A) = δ_B(B). By Lemma 8.7 this is equivalent to (8.10): length_O Ψ_B − length_O Ψ_A = ν_A(f). Also in this proof: reducing to f A-regular by passing to the image A′ of A → End_A(M) and B′ = A′/fA′ gives δ_A(M) − δ_B(N) = δ_{A′}(M) − δ_{B′}(N) (Lemmas 7.5, 8.7, 8.8 and Theorem 7.4).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2, pp. 35–36 ((8.9) and the first Claim)
items.note: The first Claim in the proof of Theorem 8.2 (pp. 35–36), with (8.9). Missing.

items.name: Key claim for (8.10): diagram (8.11) and the map F^{c−1}_B(B ⊗^L_A O) → F^{c−1}_B(O)
items.statement: In the setting of 8.1 with f also a non-zero-divisor on A (B = A/fA), consider the canonical maps B → B ⊗^L_A O → O, whose composite is λ_B. With the change-of-rings isomorphisms they give the commutative diagram (8.11): F^c_A(A) → F^c_A(O) on top, F^{c−1}_B(B) → F^{c−1}_B(B ⊗^L_A O) → F^{c−1}_B(O) below, and vertical isomorphisms. Claim: F^{c−1}_B(B ⊗^L_A O) → F^{c−1}_B(O) is one-to-one and its cokernel has length ν_A(f). Injectivity comes from the exact triangle O[1] → B ⊗^L_A O → O → O[2] in D(B), which gives the exact sequence Ext^c_B(O,O) → Ext^{c−1}_B(O, B ⊗^L_A O) → Ext^{c−1}_B(O,O) →χ Ext^{c+1}_B(O,O), where χ is the Eisenbud–Gulliksen cohomology operator. Ext^i_B(O,O) is O-torsion for i ≥ c (Lemma 2.6, since B ∈ C_O(c−1)). Hence F^{c−1}_B(B) ↪ F^{c−1}_B(B ⊗^L_A O) ↪ F^{c−1}_B(O), so length Ψ_B = length Ψ_A + ν_A(f), which is (8.10).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2, p. 37 ((8.11) and the second Claim)
items.note: The second Claim in the proof of Theorem 8.2 (p. 37), with (8.11). χ is the Eisenbud–Gulliksen cohomology operator (Avramov [2, §9.1]). Missing.

items.name: The connecting map ð*: F*_A(O) → F^{*−1}_B(O) and its F*_B(O)-linearity
items.statement: In the setting of 8.1 with f A-regular (B = A/fA), consider the connecting map Ext*_A(O,O) ≅ Ext^{*−1}_B(O, B ⊗^L_A O) → Ext^{*−1}_B(O,O). It is Ext*_B(O,O)-linear, with the source an Ext*_B(O,O)-module via the natural map Ext*_B(O,O) → Ext*_A(O,O). The paper asserts this equivariance without proof. Hence the induced ð*: F*_A(O) → F^{*−1}_B(O) is F*_B(O)-linear. ð¹: F¹_A(O) = Hom_A(p_A/p_A², O) → O is the evaluation map of (8.6), with image O(f). By Theorem 6.8 and (8.6), the image of F¹_B(O) in F¹_A(O) is a direct summand of rank c − 1. So F^{c−1}_B(O)·F¹_A(O) = F^c_A(O) and ð^c(F^c_A(O)) = F^{c−1}_B(O)·ð¹(F¹_A(O)) = ϖ^{ν_A(f)} F^{c−1}_B(O). Therefore Coker(ð^c: F^c_A(O) → F^{c−1}_B(O)) has length ν_A(f), which is the cokernel half of the previous claim.
items.note: Proof of Theorem 8.2, p. 37. The F*_B(O)-linearity of the connecting map is asserted without proof; it follows from naturality of the triangle O[1] → B ⊗^L_A O → O → O[2] under the Ext*_B(O,O)-action. Missing.

items.name: Claim in the proof of Theorem 9.6: reduction to depth A ≥ 1
items.statement: Let A be in C_O(c) and M a finitely generated A-module with depth_A M ≥ c + 1, M_{p_A} ≠ 0 and δ_A(M) = 0. Let A′ be the image of A → End_A(M). Then depth_{A′} M = c + 1, and 0 = δ_A(M) ≥ δ_{A′}(M) ≥ 0 by Lemma 7.5 and Corollary 8.3. So δ_{A′}(M) = 0 and length_O Φ_A = length_O Φ_{A′} (Lemma 7.5). If A′ is a complete intersection then A ≅ A′ by Lemma 5.10. Hence the 'only if' part of Theorem 9.6 holds for all A in C_O(c) once it holds for those with depth A ≥ 1. That depth A′ ≥ 1 follows from Ass_A A′ ⊆ Ass_A M (Lemma 7.5(2)) and depth M ≥ 1; the paper leaves this implicit.
items.note: The Claim in the proof of Theorem 9.6 (pp. 40–41). Missing.

items.name: Complete intersections along a regular element ([13, Theorem 2.3.4])
items.statement: (As cited from Bruns–Herzog [13, Theorem 2.3.4].) For a noetherian local ring R and an R-regular sequence x in its maximal ideal, R is a complete intersection if and only if R/xR is a complete intersection.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.6, p. 41; implicit in the reduction for Theorem 9.5, p. 40
items.note: Bruns–Herzog Theorem 2.3.4, used in Theorems 9.5 and 9.6. R03.3 plans complete intersections and 'the exact complete-intersection criteria used in patching'; this basic stability property belongs there.

items.name: Associated primes of Hom and zero-divisors (used in Lemma 7.5)
items.statement: For a noetherian ring A and finitely generated A-modules M and N: Ass_A Hom_A(M, N) = Supp M ∩ Ass N, so in particular Ass_A End_A(M) = Ass_A M. Ass of a submodule is contained in Ass of the module. The set of zero-divisors on a finitely generated module is the union of its associated primes.
items.note: Bruns–Herzog Ex. 1.2.27, used in Lemma 7.5 and Theorem 9.6. R03.3 plans 'associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules'. Mathlib has associated primes and biUnion_associatedPrimes_eq_zero_divisors but not Ass Hom_A(M, N) = Supp M ∩ Ass N.

items.name: The patched complex C∞ and the patching functor P, P̂ (construction)
items.statement: Work in the framed context. For a patching system C, replace each C_n by its minimal finite free Λ_n-resolution and α_n by an isomorphism of O-complexes O ⊗_{Λ_n} C_n ≅ C_0. The integers c_i := rank_{Λ_n}(C_n)_i = dim_k H_i(k ⊗_O C_0) are independent of n. For an open ideal a ⊆ S∞, set C(a, ∞) := (∏_n S∞/a ⊗_{Λ_n} C_n)_p, with the factor taken to be 0 when I_n ⊄ a (finitely many n). This is a minimal complex of finite free S∞/a-modules of ranks c_i. It is isomorphic to S∞/a ⊗_{Λ_n} C_n for infinitely many n (an F-large set). Also S∞/a ⊗_{S∞/b} C(b, ∞) ≅ C(a, ∞) for b ⊆ a ([1, Prop. 6.4.10]). C∞ := lim_s C(𝔪^s_{S∞}, ∞) is a minimal finite free S∞-complex with S∞/a ⊗ C∞ ≅ C(a, ∞) ([38, Lemma 2.13]). The maps R∞ → R(s, a, ∞) → End_{D(S∞/a)}(C(a, ∞)), for s ≫ 0 and compatible in a, induce ι∞: R∞ → End_{D(S∞)}(C∞). Composed with ϕ∞ this gives the natural S∞-action, so C∞ is a derived R∞-complex. Define P(C) := H_d(C∞) ∈ mod R∞. For f: C → D, the f_n (chosen as chain maps) induce f_{a,∞}: C(a, ∞) → D(a, ∞), which lift to f∞: C∞ → D∞, unique up to homotopy ([38, Lemma 2.13(3)]). Set P(f) := H_d(f∞), which is R∞-linear. P̂: PaSy → D_{R∞}(S∞), C ↦ C∞, f ↦ f∞, satisfies P(C) = H_d(P̂(C)).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 10.6, pp. 44–46; used as P̂ in the proof of Theorem 11.3, p. 50
items.note: The DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8 decomposition node 'ultrapatching-of-perfect-complexes' (ACC+ §6.4) constructs exactly C(J,∞), C∞ = lim C(m^r,∞) and End_{D(S∞)}(C∞) = lim End(C(J,∞)); the functor on morphisms of patching systems (homotopies preserved) is left to the reader in the paper and is a P8 obligation.

items.name: The patched rings R(s, a, ∞) and the choice of ϕ∞: S∞ → R∞
items.statement: For an open ideal a ⊆ S∞ and s ≥ 0, set R(s, a, ∞) := (∏_n S∞/a ⊗_{Λ_n} R_n/𝔪^s_{R_n})_p, with the factor taken to be 0 when I_n ⊄ a (finitely many n). As in [1, Remark 6.4.14], there are surjections R∞ ↠ R(s, a, ∞) inducing R∞ ↠ lim_{s,a} R(s, a, ∞). ϕ∞: S∞ → R∞ is a lift of the structure map S∞ → lim_{s,a} R(s, a, ∞). [1, Lemma 6.4.15] gives R∞/nR∞ = O ⊗_{S∞} R∞ ↠ R_0. Let R′ be the image of R∞ in End_{S∞}(P(C)). R′ is finite over S∞, and dim R′ = dim R∞ because P(C) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay. Adapting [8, Lemmas 3.6, 3.7], the lift can be chosen so that R∞ is a finite S∞-module.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 10.6, p. 44 and pp. 46–47
items.note: P8 plans 'the patched local deformation base R_∞' and the choice of S_∞ → R_∞ ('after choosing S_∞ → R_∞ by formal smoothness' in its ACC+ node). Finiteness of R∞ over S∞ by adapting Böckle–Khare–Manning Lemmas 3.6–3.7 is a recorded gap (sourceIssues).

items.name: Dimension of a complex and [19, Proposition 6]
items.statement: For an S-complex X with bounded, finitely generated homology, dim_S X := max{dim_S H_i(X) − i}. For the finite free complex C concentrated in [0, dim S − dim R] this is dim_S Hom_S(C, S) := max{dim_S H_i(Hom_S(C, S)) − i | i ∈ [dim R − dim S, 0]}. The paper applies this with S a Cohen–Macaulay local ring and C a finite free S-complex with H(C) ≠ 0: max{i | H_i(C) ≠ 0} = dim_S Hom_S(C, S) − dim S ([19, Proposition 6]).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 10.7, p. 48 (citing [19, (2)] and [19, Proposition 6])
items.note: Christensen–Iyengar, Contemp. Math. 773 (2021), Proposition 6, the key input to Lemma 10.7. Missing; P9's codimension–amplitude lemma (Calegari–Geraghty Lemma 6.2) is the regular-base analogue.

items.name: Level-raising prime (for ρ̄)
items.statement: A finite place v of F is a level raising prime for ρ̄ (in the sense of the paper) if v ∤ ℓ, ρ̄_v is unramified, q_v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), and the ratio of the eigenvalues of ρ̄_v(Frob_v) is q_v. At such v one fixes ε_v ∈ {1, −1} with R_v^{St(ε_v)} ≠ 0 (unique if q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ)). These are exactly the places at which non-minimal ramification is allowed (sets T ⊇ Σ, and 𝔇).
items.locator: Remark 12.2 and 12.2, p. 55 (glossary p. 80: 'Σ level raising primes, 55')
items.note: Named notion used in §§12–15 and Theorem 14.10(2). GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 chooses Taylor–Wiles primes (q ≡ 1 mod ℓ^n) only; missing.

items.name: The duality functor (−)^† used in Section 13
items.statement: In §13 the paper works in Case (PGL2): F is any number field in which ℓ is unramified, and r_1, r_2 are its numbers of real and complex places. The notation of §§10–11 is used with d = r_1 + r_2 and ℓ_0 = r_2. For C ∈ D(O), C^† := RHom_O(C, O)[2d + ℓ_0] = RHom_O(C, O)[2r_1 + 3r_2]. If C is a derived A-complex for an O-algebra A, this induces a derived A-complex structure on C^†, so (−)^† is a contravariant functor D_A(O) → D_A(O).
items.note: The duality functor of §13 (p. 58); the shift 2r_1+3r_2 = 2d + ℓ_0 matches 11.2. Missing; ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans Verdier duality of the complexes but not this normalization.

items.name: Weight-one complexes C^𝔇_{Σ,Q}, their O[Δ_Q]-perfectness, and the level-lowering maps π_v
items.statement: For Σ ⊆ T, Q, and v ∈ T ∖ Σ, the complex C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ∈ D_{T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}}(O) and the level-lowering map π_v: C^𝔇_{Σ∪{v},Q} → C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} are defined as in §13, by localizing C^𝔇_{K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}} at an appropriate maximal ideal of an extension of T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}. C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} is a perfect complex of O[Δ_Q]-modules, and C^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ C^𝔇_Σ in D_{T_Σ}(O). The O[Δ_Q]-structure on C^𝔇_{K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}} coming from Proposition 14.1(2) agrees with the one given by the diamond operators ⟨d⟩_v for v ∈ Q.
items.locator: 14.2, p. 72 (after Theorem 14.6); first paragraphs of 14.2 on p. 72
items.note: Weight-one analogue of Proposition 13.9 and of the construction of π_v in 13.6 (14.2, p. 72), with (−)^† := RHom_O(−, O)[1], d = 0, ℓ_0 = 1 (14.1, p. 68). Missing.

items.name: Injectivity of the weight-one doubling map on Shimura curves
items.statement: Let X = X_K^𝔇 and m ≥ 1. Let A be the power H̃a^{ℓ^{m−1}} (weight n − 1 = (ℓ−1)ℓ^{m−1}). The doubling map H^0(X, ω_{E/O})²[ϖ^m] → H^0(X, ω^{⊗n}_{E/O}), (f, g) ↦ Af + AT_ℓ(g) − U_ℓ(Ag), is equivariant for T_r for r ∉ S, where T_ℓ on H^0(X, ω_{E/O}) is defined as in Boxer–Pilloni [11, §3.1]. It is injective. Injectivity reduces to m = 1, i.e. to injectivity of H^0(X, ω_k)² → H^0(X, ω_k^{⊗ℓ}), (f, g) ↦ Ha·f + Ha·T_ℓ(g) − U_ℓ(Ha·g). This holds without q-expansions. Write SS for the supersingular locus. Restriction to SS and the isomorphism H^0(SS, ω_k) ≅ H^0(SS, ω^{⊗ℓ}) ([10, (5.1.1)]) force g|_SS = 0. Hence g = Ha·h with h ∈ H^0(X, ω_k^{⊗(2−ℓ)}) = 0 because ℓ > 2, so (f, g) = 0.
items.note: The one step where the Shimura-curve proof of Theorem 14.5 differs from Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11]: q-expansions are replaced by restriction to the supersingular locus as in Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni [10, §5.1]. Missing.

items.name: Serre-duality identification H^1(X, ω_O) ≅ H^0(X, ω_{E/O})^* = H_0(C)
items.statement: For the Shimura curve X = X_K^𝔇, Serre duality with the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω gives H^0(X, ω_{E/O})^∗ = H^1(X, ω_O), where (−)^∗ = Hom_O(−, E/O). The left side is H_0(X, ω_O) ≅ H_0(C_K^𝔇) by Proposition 14.1. Also H^0(X, ω_k) = H^0(X, ω_{E/O})[ϖ]. Consequently the Hecke algebras 'acting on H^1(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_O)' in Theorems H, I, 14.9 and 14.10 are the algebras T^𝔇_Σ acting on H_0(C^𝔇_Σ) = H_d(C_Σ) with d = 0.
items.locator: 14.2, p. 72 ('H^1(X^𝔇_∅, ω_O) (which is isomorphic to H^0(X^𝔇_∅, ω_{E/O})^∗)'); proof of Theorem 14.10, p. 74; §15, p. 76 ('H_d(C_Σ) = H^0(X_Σ^𝔇, ω_{E/O})^∗_{m_Σ}')
items.note: Links the main theorems (stated for H^1(X, ω_O)) with the machinery (H_0(C_K^𝔇)). Serre duality over a field is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge layer B; this integral Pontryagin-dual form on Shimura curves is not.

items.name: Vanishing of H^1(X_O, ω_O^{⊗ℓ}) and lifting of weight-ℓ mod ϖ forms
items.statement: For X = X_Σ^𝔇 and ℓ > 2, H^1(X_O, ω_O^{⊗ℓ}) = 0. By Serre duality and ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω_X, this follows from H^0(X_k, ω_k^{⊗(2−ℓ)}) = 0. Hence H^1(X_O, ω_O^{⊗ℓ})[ϖ] = 0, and from the long exact sequence of 0 → ω_O^{⊗ℓ} →(ϖ) ω_O^{⊗ℓ} → ω_k^{⊗ℓ} → 0, every mod ϖ weight-ℓ eigensystem lifts to a classical weight-ℓ form in H^0(X, ω_O^{⊗ℓ}).
items.note: Step of Theorem 14.10(1) (p. 74), with the coefficient misprint ω_O for ω_k (sourceIssues). Missing.

items.name: Growth of patched congruence modules under level raising (inductive step of Theorem 15.4; Remark 15.7)
items.statement: Let λ, p = Ker λ and µ = rank_p M_{∅,∞} be as chosen before Lemma 15.6. For Σ ⊆ T and v ∈ T∖Σ: length_O Ψ_{R_{Σ∪{v},∞}}(M_{Σ∪{v},∞}) = length_O Ψ_{R_{Σ∪{v},∞}}(M_{Σ,∞}) + µ·ν_O(λ(B_v)) = length_O Ψ_{R_{Σ,∞}}(M_{Σ,∞}) + µ·ν_O(λ(B_v)). For the first equality, apply Proposition 4.4 over A = R_{Σ∪{v},∞} to the surjection π_v: M_{Σ∪{v},∞} → M_{Σ,∞}. Both modules are Cohen–Macaulay of dimension c+1 and self-dual, and both have rank µ at p (Lemma 15.6). The endomorphism F^c(M_{Σ,∞}) ≅ F^c(M_{Σ,∞}^∨) → F^c(M_{Σ∪{v},∞}^∨) ≅ F^c(M_{Σ∪{v},∞}) → F^c(M_{Σ,∞}) induced by π_v ∘ π_v^∨ = u_vB_v is multiplication by λ(u_vB_v) on F^c(M_{Σ,∞}) ≅ O^µ, so its determinant is λ(u_v)^µλ(B_v)^µ. The second equality is invariance of domain (Theorem 7.4, used implicitly) for R_{Σ∪{v},∞} ↠ R_{Σ,∞}. Base case: R_{∅,∞} is formally smooth, so Φ_{R_{∅,∞}} = 0 and Ψ_{R_{∅,∞}}(M_{∅,∞}) = 0, since M_{∅,∞} ≅ R_{∅,∞}^µ. By induction, length_O Ψ_{R_{Σ,∞}}(M_{Σ,∞}) = µ·Σ_{v∈Σ} ν_O(λ(B_v)) for every Σ ⊆ T. Remark 15.7: Lemma 15.6 alone only needs some α_v ∈ R_{Σ∪{v},∞} that annihilates Ker π_v and has λ(α_v) ≠ 0; α_v = B_v works, because π_v^∨ ∘ π_v = u′_vB_v. The growth formula, however, needs the exact equality of ideals (π_v ∘ π_v^∨) = (B_v) of R_{Σ,∞}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 15.4, p. 78; Remark 15.7, p. 78
items.note: The core of §15 (proof of Theorem 15.4 and Remark 15.7): the patched form of Ribet's and Diamond's Ihara-lemma argument, from Proposition 4.4, Theorem 7.4 and Proposition 15.5. Missing.

items.name: B_v versus the level-raising operator q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v) (key computation in the proof of Proposition 15.5)
items.statement: Let Σ ⊆ T and v ∈ T∖Σ. By Conjecture B(3) in Case (PGL2) and Theorem 14.6(3) in Case (Wt1), applied at level Σ∪{v} (printed at level Σ; sourceIssues E55), the image of B_v ∈ R_v^{uni(ε_v)} in the Hecke algebra is w_v(ε_v√(q_vψ(φ_v)^{-1})U_v − 1) for some unit w_v. Hence w_v^{-1}B_v(2 + w_v^{-1}B_v) maps to (ε_v√(q_vψ(φ_v)^{-1})U_v − 1)(ε_v√(q_vψ(φ_v)^{-1})U_v + 1) = q_vψ(φ_v)^{-1}U_v² − 1, using ε_v = ±1. In Case (PGL2) this is U_v² − 1, since ψ(φ_v) = q_v. Moreover ψ(φ_v) ∈ O^× and 2 + w_v^{-1}B_v ∈ R_{T,∞}^×, because B_v ∈ m_{R_{T,∞}} and 2 ∈ O^× (ℓ > 2). So q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v) equals a unit times B_v. Combined with π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v) and π_v^† ∘ π_v ≃ q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v) (Propositions 13.10 and 14.7) and P(π_v^†) = P(π_v)^∨ (Theorem 11.3), this yields π_v ∘ π_v^∨ = u_vB_v and π_v^∨ ∘ π_v = u′_vB_v.
items.note: The local–global computation in the proof of Proposition 15.5 (pp. 77–78). The paper applies Conjecture B(3)/Theorem 14.6(3) for v ∈ T ∖ Σ and at Taylor–Wiles level, beyond their printed scope (sourceIssues). Missing.

items.name: Torsion automorphy consequence of R = T (Introduction)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem F (resp. Theorem G), R_Σ ≅ T_Σ. Hence every torsion Galois representation ρ: G_F → GL_2(O/ϖ^n) lifting ρ̄_m that is of type Σ, i.e. comes from an O-algebra map R_Σ → O/ϖ^n, is 'automorphic': it arises by specialising the universal modular deformation ρ_T: G_F → GL_2(T_Σ), hence from torsion Hecke eigenclasses in H_{r_1+r_2}(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ} (H_1 for Bianchi manifolds), even if ρ has no lift to characteristic 0. The paper states this informally ('This addresses torsion Galois representations ρ: G_K → GL_2(O/ω^n) that may not lift to characteristic 0. Our results show that such a ρ is automorphic …') and does not spell out the local conditions defining Σ.
items.note: The Introduction's stated consequence (p. 7) of Theorems F and G. A torsion ρ must satisfy the local conditions defining R_Σ for the conclusion to apply. Missing.

routes.title: Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching, Part II: congruence modules, Wiles defects and the numerical criterion in higher codimension
routes.brief:
Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) plans the following:
- R03.1: complete local coefficient categories;
- R03.3: depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules, complete intersections and Auslander–Buchsbaum;
- R03.5–R03.6: module patching and support;
- P7: perfect complexes;
- P8–P9: patching of complexes, amplitude and depth.
It has no congruence modules, no Wiles defect and no numerical criterion in any codimension. The atlas's other congruence modules are codimension-zero Hecke-module instances: AutomorphicCongruences L0, SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 and PadicFamilies L1. This Part II starts there. It ends at the numerical criterion of Iyengar–Khare–Manning, Invent. Math. 238 (2024) 769–864 (arXiv:2206.08212). It is the general owner of congruence modules, and those layers import its codimension-zero case (Proposition 2.10).

Setting. O is a DVR with uniformizer ϖ. The objects are pairs (A, λ_A): A is a complete noetherian local O-algebra and λ_A: A → O is a surjective O-algebra map whose kernel p_A is a prime at which A is regular, with c := height p_A. These form C_O and C_O(c). The O-algebra convention of the paper's Introduction and Glossary is required, because the p. 16 definition drops it.

Definitions:
- F^i_A(M) := Ext^i_A(O, M)^tf for M in D^b(mod A);
- Ψ_A(M) := Coker(F^c_A(M) → F^c_A(M/p_A M));
- Φ_A := tors(p_A/p_A²);
- δ_A(M) := rank_{A_p}(M_p) · length Φ_A − length Ψ_A(M).

Final theorems, as the paper states them (with the corrections recorded in sourceIssues):
- Theorem 2.5. A is regular at p_A iff Ψ_A is torsion; then F^c_A(A) and F^c_A(O) are free of rank one and Ψ_A is cyclic.
- Corollary 8.3. δ_A(M) ≥ 0 whenever grade(p_A, M) ≥ c.
- Theorem 9.6 (Theorem A). Let A be in C_O(c) and M finitely generated with depth M ≥ c + 1 and µ := rank M_{p_A} ≠ 0. Then δ_A(M) = 0 iff A is a complete intersection and M ≅ A^µ ⊕ W with W_{p_A} = 0. If moreover e_A(M) ≤ µ·e(A), then M is free.
- Theorem 9.2 (Theorem B). For A Gorenstein and M maximal Cohen–Macaulay with µ ≠ 0, δ_A(M) = µ·δ_A(A) iff M ≅ A^µ ⊕ W with W_{p_A} = 0.
- Theorem 9.5. If depth A ≥ c + 1, then A is a complete intersection iff δ_A(A) = 0.

routes.title: GL₂ Modularity Lifting, Part II: integral non-minimal R = T in positive defect and in weight one via congruence modules
routes.brief:
GL₂ Modularity Lifting (GL2ModularityLifting) proves modularity lifting for residually modular GL₂ representations over totally real fields. It follows KW II with defect ℓ₀ = 0, Betti or étale Hecke modules and component arguments, and its conclusions at non-minimal level are generic-fibre or reduced statements. It has no layer for positive defect (ℓ₀ > 0), where Hecke modules are torsion complexes. It also has none for weight-one coherent cohomology, or for integral R = T at non-minimal level proved through congruence modules. This Part II starts there. It follows Part 3 of Iyengar–Khare–Manning, Invent. Math. 238 (2024) 769–864 (arXiv:2206.08212), which runs the Wiles–Diamond induction on the level for the patched modules M_{Σ,∞} of Calegari–Geraghty's positive-defect patching.

Final theorems, as the paper states them:
- **Theorem 15.1.** Assume ρ̄_m|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} is absolutely irreducible, m is non-Eisenstein, and N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅. Then there is µ ≥ 1 such that for every Σ ⊆ T, H_d(C_Σ) ≅ R_Σ^µ ⊕ W_Σ, so R_Σ acts faithfully and R_Σ ↠ T_Σ is an isomorphism.
  - Case (PGL2): Hecke eigenclasses in the homology of the arithmetic manifolds Y_K of PGL₂ over an arbitrary number field F with ℓ unramified; d = r₁ + r₂, ℓ₀ = r₂. This case assumes Conjectures A (Galois representations for torsion classes), B (local–global compatibility, R_{Σ,Q} ↠ T_{Σ,Q}), C (concentration in degrees [r₁+r₂, r₁+2r₂]) and D (Ihara's lemma in the lowest degree), which the Part II states as explicit Prop-valued hypotheses and never as conclusions.
  - Case (Wt1): weight-one coherent cohomology of Shimura curves X^𝔇 over Q, unconditionally; d = 0, ℓ₀ = 1.
- **Theorem F.** The PGL₂ case for ℓ > 3.
- **Theorem G.** F imaginary quadratic, assuming Conjecture B. The recorded source issue on its Conjecture A input must be resolved or carried as a hypothesis.
- **Theorem 14.9 (Theorem H).** R^𝔇_Σ ≅ T^𝔇_Σ for weight-one forms on Shimura curves, ℓ > 3.
- **Theorem 14.10 (Theorem I).** The torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence T^∅_{Σ∪𝔇} ↠ T^𝔇_Σ, with kernel generated by q_vU_v² − ψ(Frob_v), v ∈ 𝔇. The additional hypotheses recorded in sourceIssues apply.

Layers:
1. **The PGL₂/F Hecke complexes.** Conjectures A–D as hypotheses; non-Eisenstein ideals; Lemmas 13.4 and 13.5; the Taylor–Wiles and level-raising Hecke algebras T_{Σ,Q} with their full Hecke algebras and maximal ideals m_{Σ,Q}; Lemma 13.8; Proposition 13.9 (perfectness over O[Δ_Q]); Proposition 13.10 (self-duality and π_v∘π_v^† = U_v² − 1); Lemma 13.11; Theorem 13.12 (Ihara's lemma for Bianchi manifolds via the congruence subgroup property of SL₂(O_F[1/v]), after Calegari–Venkatesh §4.1 and Klosin). The orientation twist at real places is to be kept (sourceIssues).
2. **Weight-one coherent cohomology of Shimura curves.** The sheaf ω = e·π_*Ω of the universal QM abelian surface; Kodaira–Spencer ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω; Pontryagin-dual coherent homology and the perfect complexes C_K^𝔇 (Proposition 14.1); Hecke operators on C_K^𝔇; Serre-duality self-duality (Proposition 14.3) and faithfulness on H_0 (Proposition 14.2, via Lemma 10.8); the Hasse invariant and its integral lifts (Lemma 14.4; Buzzard, Kassaei, Boxer); the doubling method without q-expansions (Theorem 14.5); Theorem 14.6; Proposition 14.7; Ihara's lemma in weight one (Proposition 14.8, Diamond–Taylor).
3. **Patching.** The patched rings R_{Σ,∞} = R_{loc,Σ}[[x]] with A_v, B_v, and the self-dual patching systems (Lemma 15.3). Patched level-lowering maps with π_v∘π_v^∨ = u_vB_v (Proposition 15.5, including the local–global computation of B_v against q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v)). The augmentation λ with λ(A_v) = 0 ≠ λ(B_v) (Lemma 15.6).
4. **The induction.** The growth of patched congruence modules, length Ψ(M_{Σ∪{v}}) = length Ψ(M_Σ) + µ·ν(λ(B_v)); δ = 0; free summands (Theorem 15.4); Theorem 15.1 and Theorems F, G, H.
5. **Torsion Jacquet–Langlands.** Theorem 14.10, from Calegari's modular-curve theorem (J. reine angew. Math. 740, 2018), classical Jacquet–Langlands, level and weight optimisation and companion forms. Remark 14.11 is recorded as a conditional statement. Remark 11.4, multiplicity 2^k over CM fields, is conditional.

Imports:
- DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra: P7 (perfect complexes), P8 (ultrapatching, Theorem 10.6, and the duality of patching of Theorem 11.3, which this paper supplies as a source), P9 (Lemma 10.7), R03.3.
- The proposed commutative-algebra Part II, CongruenceModulesHigherCodimension: Proposition 4.4, Theorem 7.4, Theorems 9.2, 9.5, and Φ of ⊗̂ O[[A_v,B_v]]/(A_vB_v).
- GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.6 (deformation functors, Taylor–Wiles and level-raising primes) and LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1–R08.2 (Proposition 12.1).
- ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.5 (Y_K, chain complexes, Hecke correspondences on complexes, level subgroups and level-lowering maps, Atkin–Lehner-twisted Verdier duality), IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1–IHG.4, and AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4.
- HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1–R18.2, PELModuli M2 and AutomorphicBundles B4–B5.
- tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge layer B and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction layer 2 (Serre duality), tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory.
- GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3 (Jacquet–Langlands), SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2–R20.3 (level and weight optimisation, companion forms), AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1–R15.3 (Katz forms), and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2 and R19.6.

The positive-defect Hecke side for PGL₂/F overlaps the queued extraction of Calegari–Geraghty (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18). The design job should import whatever that extraction routes and plan here only what remains.

Acceptance:
- The Bianchi case: F imaginary quadratic, where Conjectures C and D hold (Theorem 13.12).
- The modular-curve case 𝔇 = ∅ (Calegari's theorem as a consistency check).
- For Σ = {v}, the computation Φ_{R_{Σ,∞}} ≅ O/λ(B_v)O.
routes.reason: Part 3 of the paper is GL₂ modularity lifting, the direction of GL2ModularityLifting, but beyond it: that roadmap follows KW II (totally real fields, defect ℓ₀ = 0, Betti/étale Hecke modules, component arguments) and reaches only generic-fibre or reduced conclusions at non-minimal level. Nothing in the atlas plans R = T for torsion homology of PGL₂/F arithmetic manifolds (Calegari–Geraghty's Conjectures A–D, Bianchi manifolds), weight-one coherent cohomology of Shimura curves (doubling, Hasse invariants, Diamond–Taylor Ihara lemma), the patched level-raising maps with π_v∘π_v^∨ = u_vB_v, or the congruence-module induction on the level; nor the torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence. These form one development (Theorem 15.1 treats both cases uniformly), so they are one Part II. It imports the general patching (P7–P9), the congruence-module Part II above, the deformation rings (GlobalGaloisDeformations, LocalGaloisDeformationRings), arithmetic manifolds and Hecke operators (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) and the Shimura-curve geometry (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves, AutomorphicBundles) rather than re-planning them.

General local commutative algebra that the paper uses and cites from Bruns–Herzog, Kaplansky, Lescot and Stacks: symbolic powers and the regular-quotient criterion, coset prime avoidance, Lescot's criterion (next to Serre's criterion in the R03.3 decomposition), normalized dualizing complexes of complete local rings with local duality (the depth/dimension formulas (4.2) and 11.1), Cohen–Macaulay duals and their exactness, Gorenstein rings and maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules (9.1), Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity, trace ideals and Artinian Gorenstein socles. R03.3 plans 'depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings/modules, projective dimension, Auslander–Buchsbaum and the exact complete-intersection criteria', with 'depth and dimension formulas' and 'associated-prime and support lemmas'; the DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra README makes it, not the Gorenstein homological-algebra roadmap, the owner of this local ring theory, and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 and PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 route Matlis duality and local cohomology there. Dualizing complexes of local rings are placed with them (the scheme-level normalized dualizing complex routed by those extractions to AnalyticStacks:AS.1 should import this local version), with P7 for the perfect-complex statements of 11.1. Planned items the paper is a good source for are listed too.

§10 is the patching that P7–P9 plan (their reviewed decomposition already reads Calegari–Geraghty §6 and ACC+ §6.4). The paper adds, inside the same layers: the functor P on a category of patching systems with non-compatible surjections π_n (P8), the dual patching system and the theorem that patching commutes with duality, P(𝔆†) ≅ P(𝔆)^∨ (Theorem 11.3; P8, with the duals of P7), Lemma 10.8 on endomorphisms of two-term perfect complexes (P7), and Lemma 10.7 over a Cohen–Macaulay base with the Christensen–Iyengar dimension of finite free complexes (P9). The recorded gaps in the proofs of Theorems 10.6(1) and 11.3 are obligations for these layers.

R08.2 plans the unramified, Steinberg and minimally ramified conditions away from p with their dimensions and components. The paper's Proposition 12.1 (after Shotton) is the explicit GL₂ computation R^{uni(ε)} ≅ O[[A,B,X,Y]]/(AB) with its universal lift, R^St = R^uni/(B), R^min = R^uni/(A), which the level-raising argument needs verbatim; with CHT §2.4 and Shotton (Duke 2018, Thm 2.5) it is a source for R08.2 and L7.

R04.5 owns auxiliary primes chosen by Chebotarev and residual-image lemmas with prescribed Frobenius eigenvalues; the level-raising (Ribet) primes of Remark 12.2 — v ∤ ℓ, ρ̄ unramified, q_v ≢ 1, eigenvalue ratio q_v — are the sibling construction, with the corrected hypotheses recorded in sourceIssues (Frob_v ~ c in Gal(F(ρ̄, ζ_ℓ)/F); ℓ ≥ 7 or [k : F_ℓ] even). The global functors with Steinberg/unipotent conditions at Σ and 𝔇, the O[Δ_Q]-structure (Proposition 12.3) and the positive-defect presentation count of Proposition 15.2 are R04.1–R04.6 instances over an arbitrary number field, for which the paper is a source.

ALS.0–ALS.5 plan the arithmetic manifolds, their chain complexes, Hecke correspondences on complexes with change of level, and finite-level Verdier duality with Hecke adjoints ('including oriented and nonorientable cases by retaining the orientation local system'). The PGL₂/F level subgroups K_0(N), K_1(N), K_Δ(N) with the auxiliary t², the level-lowering maps π_{K,v} = π_1 ⊕ π_2 with their U_v-relation, the duality functor (−)^† and the Atkin–Lehner-twisted self-duality of Proposition 13.7 are instances inside those layers' scope; the paper (with Newton–Thorne Prop. 3.7, Thm 4.2, Lemma 2.19 and Khare–Thorne Lemma 6.1) is a source for them. The recorded mistakes (the U_v-matrix, the orientation twist at real places, the K_v-dichotomy at t) are obligations for these layers.

R20.3 owns weight optimisation at p, including Edixhoven's theorem, whose proof RS-06 assigns there; it gives weight one only in the non-exceptional case. The exceptional case (ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) scalar) used by Theorem 14.10(1) is Coleman–Voloch [21], with Gross [27]; they belong in R20.3 as sources (consistent with PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25).

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.6, p. 25 (arXiv v3; the same text in v1 and v2)
sourceIssues.printed: “Since the ideal generated by (f′_{j+1}) + (f′_{j+1}, …, f′_h)² in Ā agrees with IĀ up to radical, a prime avoidance argument yields an element f″ in (f′_{j+1}, …, f′_h)² such that f′_{j+1} + f″ is a not a zerodivisor in Ā”
sourceIssues.correction: Replace the upper index h (= height I) by m (the number of minimal generators): take f″ ∈ (f′_{j+2}, …, f′_m)² ⊆ I². By Nakayama IĀ = (f′_{j+1}, …, f′_m)Ā, so (f′_{j+1}) + (f′_{j+2}, …, f′_m)² has the radical of IĀ, which lies in no associated prime of Ā because IĀ contains a non-zero-divisor; Kaplansky's Theorem 124 then gives f″. Since f″ ∈ I² ⊆ (t)², the new generators keep the form (5.4) and minimality. Theorem 5.6 is true.
sourceIssues.reason: When h < m the first h minimal generators need not generate I up to radical. Example: P = O[[t1,t2]], I = (t1(ϖ+t2), ϖt2(ϖ+t2), t1t2), a minimal generating set of the form (5.4) with d = (1, 2, ∞). A = P/I is in C_O(0) (I·P_{(t)} = (t1,t2)), the minimal primes of I are (t1,ϖ), (t1,t2), (t1,ϖ+t2), (ϖ,t2), so h = 2 = n − c and dim A = 1 = c + 1, while m = 3. For j = 1, f1 = t1(ϖ+t2) and Ā = P/(f1) has associated primes (t1) and (ϖ+t2). The printed ideal is (f′_2) and every element of f′_2 + (f′_2)² lies in (ϖ+t2), so it is a zero-divisor: the step fails. With the correction, f2 = f′_2 + (t1t2)² is a non-zero-divisor on Ā.

sourceIssues.printed: “Thus δ_A(M) ≥ δ_B(M) with equality if and only if length_O Φ_A = length_O Φ_B.”
sourceIssues.correction: With r := rank_{B_{p_B}}(M_{p_B}) (= rank_{A_{p_A}}(M_{p_A}), since A_{p_A} ≅ B_{p_B}), δ_A(M) − δ_B(M) = r·(length_O Φ_A − length_O Φ_B) ≥ 0. So δ_A(M) ≥ δ_B(M), and when r ≠ 0 equality holds if and only if length_O Φ_A = length_O Φ_B; when r = 0 equality always holds. (r ≠ 0 holds, for example, when M is supported at p_B with grade(p_B, M) ≥ c, since M is then free at p_B.)
sourceIssues.reason: The first sentence of the theorem gives length Ψ_A(M) = length Ψ_B(M), and Φ_A ↠ Φ_B (5.9), so the difference of defects is r·(length Φ_A − length Φ_B). When r = 0 the 'only if' fails. Example (c = 0): A = O[[t]]/(t², ϖ²t) → B = O[[t]]/(t², ϖt), both in C_O(0) (t = 0 after localizing at (t)), with Φ_A ≅ O/ϖ² and Φ_B ≅ O/ϖ; M = k has depth 0 ≥ c and Ψ_A(k) = Ψ_B(k) = 0, so δ_A(k) = δ_B(k) = 0. For c ≥ 1, M_{p_B} ≠ 0 is not enough: A = O[[x,t]]/(t², ϖ²t) → B = O[[x,t]]/(t², ϖt), M = O = B/(x,t) gives M_{p_B} ≠ 0 of rank 0 and δ_A(M) = δ_B(M) = 0 with lengths 2 ≠ 1. sourceIssues.correction: Require A to be an O-algebra, λ_A a map of O-algebras and morphisms O-algebra maps, as the Introduction (p. 4, 'A a complete local noetherian O-algebra') and the Glossary (p. 80, 'a surjective map in CNL_O') say. Then every A in C_O is O[[t]]/I with I ⊆ (ϖ)(t) + (t)², and §§5–9 apply as written. (Existence of a dualizing complex holds in general by Cohen's structure theorem.)
sourceIssues.reason: Under the p. 16 definition the p. 21 and p. 40 claims fail: O = Z_p[√p], A = Z_p[[x]], λ(x) = √p is surjective with kernel (x² − p), A is regular, so A ∈ C_O(1); but A contains no square root of p (reduce mod x), so it is no O-algebra and no quotient of O[[t]]. The proofs of Theorem 5.6, Lemma 5.10, 6.3, Lemma 6.5, Theorem 6.8(2) and Propositions 6.10–6.11 start from A = P/I and so do not cover such A.

Then modify the lifts of y, w by elements of K = Ker(R∞ → Q̄) one at a time so that, with ϖ, they cut out a finite-length quotient of R∞ (prime avoidance on R∞/(ϖ, earlier lifts), using dim R∞/ϖ = dim S∞/ϖ − ℓ_0 and dim Q̄ = dim R∞). sourceIssues.reason: [8, Lemma 3.6] (arXiv:2108.09729v2, p. 11) assumes (P): S ↪ R making R finite free, and (CI): R̃ a complete intersection, O-flat and equidimensional; neither holds for S∞ → R∞ here (dim R∞ = dim S∞ − ℓ_0 < dim S∞ when ℓ_0 > 0, and R∞ need not be Cohen–Macaulay), so the lemma does not apply as stated. The proof also takes R′ from an unspecified 𝔆, although ϕ∞ must serve the whole functor P, and dim R′ = dim R∞ needs P(𝔆) ≠ 0. sourceIssues.locator: Remark 12.2, second paragraph, second sentence, p. 55
sourceIssues.printed: “If the projective image of ρ̄ is PSL_2(k) (for |k| ≥ 5) and [F(ζ_ℓ) : F] > 2 then there are places v such that ρ̄(Frob_v) has eigenvalues with ratio q_v and q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ); these are again level raising primes in our sense.”
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that some a ∈ F_ℓ^× ∖ {±1} is a square in k (e.g. ℓ ≥ 7, or [k : F_ℓ] even). Then choose λ ∈ k with λ² = a and use Chebotarev in the compositum of F(proj ρ̄) and F(ζ_ℓ), which are linearly disjoint because PSL_2(k) is simple.
sourceIssues.reason: An element of GL_2 with class in PSL_2(k) is z·h with h ∈ SL_2(k), so its eigenvalue ratio is μ² for an eigenvalue μ of h; if μ ∉ k then μ^{|k|} = μ^{−1} and a ratio in F_ℓ is ±1. So a ratio in F_ℓ ∖ {±1} must be a square in k. For ℓ = 5 and [k : F_5] odd, 2 and 3 are non-squares; e.g. F = Q with projective image PSL_2(F_5) ≅ A_5: q_v ≢ ±1 (mod 5) forces a ratio of order 4, but A_5 has no element of order 4. The hypothesis [F(ζ_5):F] = 4 > 2 holds. The remark is used in no proof.

At Taylor–Wiles level K^𝔇_{Σ,Q} (Q ≠ ∅) this is not ψ: the scalars Z_v^× (v ∈ Q) lie in K_0^𝔇(Q) and map onto Δ_v, so Δ_Q acts through the central character. Either define the Taylor–Wiles levels through ad^{−1} as in §13.4 (keeping d ≡ 1 mod t²), which makes ⟨d⟩_v the diamond operators of the O[Δ_Q]-structure and the determinant ψ; or keep the d-type level, state Theorem 14.5(ii) with x² − T_v x + ⟨v⟩, and in Theorem 14.6 twist ρ_{Σ,Q} by the square root of the ℓ-power-order character ψ·det(ρ_{Σ,Q})^{−1} (ℓ odd), as in Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11], before mapping from R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} (whose lifts have determinant ψ).
sourceIssues.reason: Forms with a nontrivial Δ_v-character have central character ramified at v ∈ Q, and in weight one det ρ_π is the central character. Patching needs H_0(C^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) to be free over O[Δ_Q] (Proposition 14.1(2)), so such forms occur after localizing at m; but ψ is unramified outside S and ℓ, so the printed characteristic polynomial, and the existence of R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} with determinant ψ, fail as printed. At level Q = ∅ with prime-to-ℓ nebentypus the two agree, so the minimal-level statements are unaffected once the Taylor–Wiles levels are corrected.

sourceIssues.printed: p. 7: “When F is a CM field and ℓ is sufficiently large, Conjecture A is known by [45, Theorem 1.3]. … Theorem G. … For ℓ > 20, there exists an integer µ ≥ 1 …” Footnote 1: “The precise bound is given in [45, (1.2)], in our situation, ℓ > 20 is sufficient if [F : Q] = 2.” p. 60: “part (ii) is known for sufficiently large ℓ; see [45, Theorem 1.1, Theorem 1.3].”
sourceIssues.correction: [45, Theorem 1.3] gives ρ_m only modulo an ideal I with I^4 = 0, so it does not give Conjecture A(ii). The nilpotent-free result, whose bound is (1.2), is [45, Theorem 1.4 = Theorem 5.13]; it assumes ℓ unramified in F and a strictly regular weight (λ_{τ,1} > λ_{τ,2} for every τ), whereas the complexes C_K of §13 have trivial coefficients (λ = 0). So the cited results do not supply Conjecture A(ii) for C_K; Theorem G should also assume Conjecture A(ii) (and ℓ unramified in F), or cite a result covering trivial weight.
sourceIssues.reason: For n = 2 and F imaginary quadratic, the left side of [45, (1.2)] is 16 + 3(a_1 − a_2) + (b_1 − b_2) for λ_τ̃ = (a_1, a_2), λ_τ̃c = (b_1, b_2); its minimum over regular weights is 20, at λ = ((1,0),(1,0)), which is the footnote's ℓ > 20. At λ = 0 the Lan–Suh vanishing behind [45, Thm 5.10] fails already in degree 0. Also ℓ = 23 with F = Q(√−23) meets ℓ > 20 but is ramified in F. Theorem G as stated therefore rests on an input the citation does not provide; its other inputs (Conjectures C, D via Theorem 13.12) need only ℓ > 3.
